### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the example project attached
2. Tap some of the red markers
3. Notice that the Map zooms to the location after a significant delay

### Expected results

Zooming after tapping happens (almost) instantly.

### Actual results

Zooming after tapping happens with over a 350ms delay.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:google_maps_flutter/google_maps_flutter.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const MainApp());
}

class MainApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MainApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(body: Center(child: MapSample())),
    );
  }
}

class MapSample extends StatefulWidget {
  const MapSample({super.key});

  @override
  State<MapSample> createState() => MapSampleState();
}

class MapSampleState extends State<MapSample> {
  final Completer<GoogleMapController> _controller =
      Completer<GoogleMapController>();

  static const CameraPosition _nl = CameraPosition(
    target: LatLng(52.221, 5.281),
    zoom: 8.0,
  );

  static const List<LatLng> _markerPositions = <LatLng>[
    LatLng(52.3676, 4.9041), // Amsterdam
    LatLng(51.9244, 4.4777), // Rotterdam
    LatLng(52.0907, 5.1214), // Utrecht
    LatLng(51.4416, 5.4697), // Eindhoven
    LatLng(53.2194, 6.5665), // Groningen
  ];

  bool _zoomGesturesEnabled = true;

  // Raw pointer timestamps captured above the platform view, before any gesture recognition.
  DateTime? _pointerDownAt;
  DateTime? _pointerUpAt;

  final List<int> _sinceUpSamplesMs = <int>[];
  String _lastResult = 'Tap the map or a marker';

  void _onPointerDown(PointerDownEvent event) {
    _pointerDownAt = DateTime.now();
    _pointerUpAt = null;
  }

  void _onPointerUp(PointerUpEvent event) {
    _pointerUpAt = DateTime.now();
  }

  void _recordTap(String source) {
    final DateTime now = DateTime.now();
    final DateTime? down = _pointerDownAt;
    final DateTime? up = _pointerUpAt;
    if (down == null || up == null) {
      setState(() => _lastResult = '$source: no pointer timestamps captured');
      return;
    }
    final int sinceDown = now.difference(down).inMilliseconds;
    final int sinceUp = now.difference(up).inMilliseconds;
    _sinceUpSamplesMs.add(sinceUp);
    final String line =
        '[zoom=${_zoomGesturesEnabled ? 'on' : 'off'}] $source: '
        '${sinceUp}ms after finger up (${sinceDown}ms after finger down)';
    debugPrint('TAP_LATENCY $line');
    setState(() => _lastResult = line);
  }

  String get _stats {
    if (_sinceUpSamplesMs.isEmpty) return 'n=0';
    final List<int> s = List<int>.of(_sinceUpSamplesMs)..sort();
    final double avg = s.reduce((int a, int b) => a + b) / s.length;
    final int median = s[s.length ~/ 2];
    return 'n=${s.length}  avg=${avg.toStringAsFixed(0)}ms  '
        'median=${median}ms  min=${s.first}ms  max=${s.last}ms';
  }

  Set<Marker> get _markers => <Marker>{
    for (int i = 0; i < _markerPositions.length; i++)
      Marker(
        markerId: MarkerId('m$i'),
        position: _markerPositions[i],
        onTap: () => _recordTap('marker m$i'),
      ),
  };

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      body: Stack(
        children: <Widget>[
          Listener(
            behavior: HitTestBehavior.translucent,
            onPointerDown: _onPointerDown,
            onPointerUp: _onPointerUp,
            child: GoogleMap(
              zoomGesturesEnabled: _zoomGesturesEnabled,
              initialCameraPosition: _nl,
              markers: _markers,
              onTap: (LatLng _) => _recordTap('map'),
              onMapCreated: (GoogleMapController controller) {
                _controller.complete(controller);
              },
            ),
          ),
          Positioned(
            left: 8,
            right: 8,
            top: MediaQuery.paddingOf(context).top + 8,
            child: Card(
              child: Padding(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
                child: Column(
                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                  mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
                  children: <Widget>[
                    SwitchListTile(
                      dense: true,
                      contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
                      title: const Text('zoomGesturesEnabled'),
                      value: _zoomGesturesEnabled,
                      onChanged: (bool v) => setState(() {
                        _zoomGesturesEnabled = v;
                        _sinceUpSamplesMs.clear();
                        _lastResult = 'Samples reset';
                      }),
                    ),
                    Text(_lastResult),
                    const SizedBox(height: 4),
                    Text(
                      _stats,
                      style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodySmall,
                    ),
                  ],
                ),
              ),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

title: unsigned executable
body:
Building a Flutter web release fails because Windows application control blocks Flutter’s font-subset.exe.

Environment

Flutter 3.47.7 stable, Windows x64
Windows 11 Home
Smart App Control enabled
Steps to reproduce

Run flutter build web --release.
The build fails when Flutter tries to run font-subset.exe.
Error

An Application Control policy or security policy has blocked execution.

Windows CodeIntegrity Event ID 3033 says that font-subset.exe did not meet the Enterprise signing level requirements.

Checks performed

Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports NotSigned.
I downloaded Flutter 3.47.7 from the official SDK archive and verified the ZIP against Flutter’s published SHA-256 checksum.
The installed font-subset.exe has the same SHA-256 hash as the copy inside the verified ZIP.
Microsoft support suggested the unsigned executable is the issue.
Is a signed version of this tool available, or is there a supported way to build Flutter web releases with Smart App Control enabled?

title: [camera_avfoundation] Front camera preview rotated 90° and stretched on iPhone 17 Pro Max since 0.11.0+2
[webview_flutter][Android] JavaScript execution Futures never complete when executed during navigation with Android System WebView 157
[Impeller] framebuffer_blend.frag checks `supports_decal > 1` instead of `> 0.0`, always taking the software decal fallback
[Impeller][macOS] `Image.toByteData` returns all zeros when Impeller renders on a discrete AMD GPU (Radeon Pro 560X); draws are correct, Skia reads back correctly
[Android] Semantics are compiled every frame whenever any accessibility service is enabled, not only when a screen reader is active
body:
### Use case

On Android, `AccessibilityManager.isEnabled()` returns true as soon as *any* accessibility service is enabled. The embedding treats that as a request for the full semantics tree, and from then on the framework compiles semantics and sends a `SemanticsUpdate` to the embedding on every frame.

Many users keep services enabled permanently that do not need a per-frame semantics tree:

- ad / splash-screen skippers and auto-clickers, which are very common in China (李跳跳 / Li Tiaotiao, GKD, 轻启动, various auto-clickers). They query the node tree occasionally, typically after a window change, or only inject gestures;
- password managers that use an accessibility service to find login fields.

For these users every Flutter app pays the semantics cost on every frame, which shows up as jank on 120 Hz devices (8.3 ms frame budget).

#### How semantics get enabled today (main @ [`f0add0e`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a))

1. `AccessibilityBridge` reports `accessibilityManager.isEnabled()` at construction and on every change ([AccessibilityBridge.java#L543-L544](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/view/AccessibilityBridge.java#L543-L544)). The `accessibilityStateChangeListener` calls `accessibilityChannel.onAndroidAccessibilityEnabled()` when it is true ([#L394-L414](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/view/AccessibilityBridge.java#L394-L414)).
2. `AccessibilityChannel.onAndroidAccessibilityEnabled()` calls `flutterJNI.setSemanticsEnabled(true)` ([AccessibilityChannel.java#L124-L126](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/systemchannels/AccessibilityChannel.java#L124-L126)) → `nativeSetSemanticsEnabled` ([FlutterJNI.java#L951-L963](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/FlutterJNI.java#L951-L963)) → `Shell::OnPlatformViewSetSemanticsEnabled` ([shell.cc#L1286](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/common/shell.cc#L1286)) → `PlatformDispatcher.semanticsEnabled`.
3. The `touchExplorationStateChangeListener` ([AccessibilityBridge.java#L548-L569](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/view/AccessibilityBridge.java#L548-L569)) does not affect whether semantics are enabled. It only resets `accessibleNavigation` and is forwarded to `FlutterView.resetWillNotDraw`.
4. In the framework, `SemanticsBinding._handleSemanticsEnabledChanged` takes a `SemanticsHandle` whenever `platformDispatcher.semanticsEnabled` is true ([semantics/binding.dart#L162-L169](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/packages/flutter/lib/src/semantics/binding.dart#L162-L169)), which creates a `SemanticsOwner` on each `PipelineOwner` ([rendering/object.dart#L1398-L1413](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/object.dart#L1398-L1413)).
5. `RendererBinding.drawFrame` calls `rootPipelineOwner.flushSemantics()` after compositing on every frame ([rendering/binding.dart#L691-L699](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/binding.dart#L691-L699)). `PipelineOwner.flushSemantics` ([object.dart#L1465](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/object.dart#L1465)) updates dirty nodes and geometry and calls `SemanticsOwner.sendSemanticsUpdate()` ([semantics.dart#L5104](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/packages/flutter/lib/src/semantics/semantics.dart#L5104)), which serializes the dirty nodes and calls `onSemanticsUpdate(builder.build())` ([semantics.dart#L5331](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/packages/flutter/lib/src/semantics/semantics.dart#L5331)). The Java `AccessibilityBridge.updateSemantics` then rebuilds its node map and emits accessibility events ([AccessibilityBridge.java#L1533](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/view/AccessibilityBridge.java#L1533)).

#### Native Android and Chromium build accessibility data on demand

- Android `View`s create `AccessibilityNodeInfo` only when a service asks for it. While a service is enabled they send throttled `TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED` events, but they do not build node info per frame.
- Chromium's Android accessibility is "lazy" and "on demand" and can pick a reduced mode based on which services are running ([docs/accessibility/browser/android.md](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/docs/accessibility/browser/android.md)).
- Jetpack Compose, which like Flutter draws its own UI and keeps its own semantics tree, materializes the flattened node map only when it is requested and invalidated (`currentSemanticsNodes` getter), and batches semantics-change and bounds events with a 100 ms delay instead of per frame. It also distinguishes `isEnabled` (any service) from `isTouchExplorationEnabled` for screen-reader-only behavior ([AndroidComposeViewAccessibilityDelegateCompat.android.kt](https://github.com/androidx/androidx/blob/androidx-main/compose/ui/ui/src/androidMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/platform/AndroidComposeViewAccessibilityDelegateCompat.android.kt): `isEnabled`, `isTouchExplorationEnabled`, `onSemanticsChange`, `boundsUpdatesEventLoop`).

#### This hits apps in practice

Alibaba's Taote team wrote in 2021 that Flutter has a performance problem during fast scrolling when accessibility is on, and that they wrapped content in `ExcludeSemantics` when "the business doesn't need accessibility or the user turned it on by mistake"; they also had to measure by hand because uiautomator triggered the same accessibility slowdown ([淘特 Flutter 流畅度优化实践](https://segmentfault.com/a/1190000041187106)). That workaround removes the content for screen-reader users too, which is exactly what an engine-side fix would avoid.

#### Measurements

Xiaomi Pad 7 (Snapdragon 7+ Gen 3, 3200×2136, 120 Hz), Impeller/Vulkan, Flutter 3.47.7 stable, profile build. App: a diary with 4000 entries and 400 photos. Two non-screen-reader services enabled: 轻启动 (`com.wpengapp.lightstart`) and an auto-clicker (`com.clicker.automatic`). One run per configuration; skipped refreshes on screen, with build-phase p99 in parentheses.

| Scenario | Services on | Services off | Services on, semantics kept off by the app |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open an entry | 7.17 % (13.8 ms) | 6.09 % (9.1 ms) | 4.89 % (8.6 ms) |
| Switch tabs | 15.25 % (77 ms) | 10.71 % (50 ms) | 11.19 % (51 ms) |
| Scroll the journal list | 0.07 % | 1.03 % | 0.86 % |
| Scroll a media grid | 0.90 % | 1.05 % | 0.73 % |

Scrolling differences are within run-to-run noise here. On build-heavy frames (opening a page, switching tabs) semantics add roughly 5 ms (p99 build 13.8 → 9.1 ms) and 27 ms (77 → 50 ms). The third column uses an app-side workaround: a `FlutterJNI` subclass, installed through `FlutterInjector`, that withholds `setSemanticsEnabled(true)` while the only enabled services are known non-reading tools. It shows the cost disappears when semantics stay off, and it is the kind of decision we believe belongs in the engine instead.

For reference, #150234 recorded semantics at about 2.6 ms of a 6 ms frame when scrolling static content, and about 1.6 ms → 0.3 ms per 4 ms frame after the caching in #161195.

#### Related issues

- #61193 Scrolling jank in ListView when semantics are enabled. Closed 2025-05-19 as fixed by #161195.
- #150234 [A11y] Identify Flutter semantics performance issues. Closed 2025-02-06.
- #161195 Introduce caching mechanism during compile semantics tree. Merged 2025-02-06.
- #28204 `_getSemanticsForParent` should cache result for smoother scrolling. Opened 2019, closed 2024.
- #195577 Excluded subtrees still add semantics work on every frame. Open.
- #166173 Further optimize geometry calculation in semantics. Closed 2026-03-09.

#161195 made the per-frame compile cheaper; this issue is about not compiling every frame when no service consumes per-frame updates. The [2026 roadmap](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/roadmap/Roadmap.md) mentions accessibility work only for web and multi-window desktop.

### Proposal

#### Main proposal: compile semantics on demand on Android unless a screen reader is active

**Eager mode.** When `AccessibilityManager.isTouchExplorationEnabled()` is true, keep today's behavior. TalkBack and other screen readers request touch exploration.

**On-demand mode** (`isEnabled()` true, touch exploration off):

1. The framework keeps its `SemanticsOwner` and keeps marking render objects dirty, but `drawFrame` skips `flushSemantics()`. This needs a third engine → framework state between "off" and "on".
2. After a frame leaves semantics dirty, the bridge sends one throttled `TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED` for the root, as native views do, without compiling anything.
3. When a service calls `createAccessibilityNodeInfo`, `findFocus` or `performAction` and semantics are dirty, the bridge synchronously asks the framework to flush, applies the update, then answers. Since 3.29 Android runs Dart on the platform thread ([What's new in Flutter 3.29](https://flutter.dev/blog/whats-new-in-flutter-3-29), #150525), where Android calls the `AccessibilityNodeProvider` methods; `Shell::OnEngineUpdateSemantics` then runs immediately via `RunNowOrPostTask` ([shell.cc#L1498-L1512](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/common/shell.cc#L1498-L1512)), and `OnPlatformViewSetSemanticsEnabled` already makes a synchronous platform → UI call ([shell.cc#L1286-L1296](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/common/shell.cc#L1286-L1296)).
4. Between frames layout is clean, so the flush yields the tree of the last rendered frame.
5. Diff-derived events (scrolled, focus changes, live regions) stay eager-only; their consumers are screen readers.
6. With merged threads disabled (`DisableMergedPlatformUIThread`), stay eager.

**Screen-reader users** see no change. **Switch Access, Voice Access, Select to Speak** do not request touch exploration, so they would be on-demand: they still get a complete, current tree on query, at the cost of one flush after a change. If maintainers prefer them eager, the embedding can inspect `getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList()`; feedback types alone do not separate them from skippers (both commonly `FEEDBACK_GENERIC`).

#### Smaller alternatives

- **(c, framework only)** When touch exploration is off, coalesce semantics updates instead of sending one per frame, e.g. at most every 100 ms like Compose. Smaller gain, smallest change, no embedding work.
- **(a)** Expose the enabled services (`AccessibilityServiceInfo`, touch exploration) to the app. Not enough alone: the app cannot release the handle `SemanticsBinding` holds.
- **(b)** A documented embedding hook to keep semantics off for chosen services. Small, but every app then makes an accessibility decision that can break real users; the main proposal keeps it in the engine.

#### Related side effect

`createAccessibilityNodeInfo` calls `setAccessibleNavigation(true)` on every query ([AccessibilityBridge.java#L781-L782](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/view/AccessibilityBridge.java#L781-L782)), reset only when accessibility or touch exploration turns off. One query by a skipper sets `MediaQuery.accessibleNavigation` for the rest of the session (SnackBar/MaterialBanner skip animations, AppBar stays opaque). On-demand mode would make it natural to derive `accessibleNavigation` from touch exploration only.

---

Checked against Flutter 3.47.7 stable and `main` at f0add0e1fe9d8229638cbbc92d005c2959d6f19a (2026-11-09).

title: [google_sign_in] Support App Check for Google Sign-In on iOS
body:
### Use case

GoogleSignIn-iOS has supported Firebase App Check since 8.0.0. When it is
configured, GIDSignIn attaches an App Check (App Attest) token to the
authorization requests, so the iOS OAuth client can verify that sign-in
requests come from the genuine app. Google Cloud lets you enforce this for
the OAuth client.

To enable it, the app has to call one of these on GIDSignIn.sharedInstance
"as early as possible" (they pre-generate the App Attest key and attestation):

- configure(completion:)                            // App Attest
- configureDebugProvider(withAPIKey:completion:)    // simulator / debug builds

google_sign_in_ios never calls either, and the plugin owns GIDSignIn, so a
Flutter app currently has no way to turn this on. Without App Check, an
OAuth client that enforces it rejects every sign-in from a Flutter app.

We are currently running a local fork of google_sign_in_ios 6.4.0 that calls
these in register(with:), and it works in production with GoogleSignIn-iOS
10.1.0.


### Proposal

Add an opt-in way to configure App Check from the plugin, for example:

1. An Info.plist key (e.g. `GIDEnableAppCheck` = YES). When it is set, the
   plugin calls configure(completion:) during registration, or
   configureDebugProvider(withAPIKey:) in debug builds, using API_KEY from
   GoogleService-Info.plist. This needs no Dart API change and runs early
   enough, because registration happens at app launch.

2. Alternatively, an option on GoogleSignIn.initialize() (passed through the
   platform interface). This is more discoverable, but it runs later than
   registration, and on its own it covers fewer of the cases the SDK
   recommends.

Notes:
- It should stay opt-in, so apps that don't use App Check don't pay for an
  App Attest round trip at launch.
- GIDSignIn reads the client ID for App Check from `GIDClientID` in
  Info.plist (not from the `configuration` passed to the sign-in call), so
  the docs should mention that this key is required.
- Configuration failures should not be fatal: GIDSignIn then sends the
  request without a token, which still succeeds unless enforcement is on.

I'm happy to send a PR for option 1 if this direction sounds good.

title: [multicast_dns] IPv4 queries ignore the Wi-Fi interface and leave over cellular when mobile data is up
body:
### Package

multicast_dns 0.3.3+1

### Platform seen on

Android (the root cause is platform-independent)

### Summary

On IPv4, `MDnsClient.start()` never sets `IP_MULTICAST_IF` on its sending socket. For IPv6 it does — the per-interface loop sets `RawSocketOption.IPv6MulticastInterface`. The IPv4 path calls `joinMulticast` but sets no `IPv4MulticastInterface`, so IPv4 multicast egress follows the OS routing table.

On a phone with both Wi-Fi and mobile data up, the default route is cellular, so mDNS queries leave over the cellular interface and never reach the LAN. Discovery silently finds nothing and reports no error.

### Evidence

In `lib/multicast_dns.dart`, the interface loop sets the multicast interface only inside the `if (targetAddress.type == InternetAddressType.IPv6)` branch. The IPv4 send socket (`_incomingIPv4`, bound to `anyIPv4`) joins multicast but is never given an `IPv4MulticastInterface` option.

Confirmed on desktop that `joinMulticast` does not set `IP_MULTICAST_IF`: reading the socket's `IPv4MulticastInterface` option stays `0.0.0.0` after joining on every interface, so the socket relies on routing for IPv4 egress.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On an Android device, turn on **both** Wi-Fi and mobile data.
2. Announce an mDNS service on the LAN from another machine (e.g. `dns-sd -R sample _http._tcp . 8000`).
3. Run a lookup from the device. It returns nothing.
4. Force the socket's IPv4 multicast interface to the Wi-Fi address and repeat — the same lookup resolves.

### Suggested fix

In the IPv4 path, set the multicast interface, mirroring the IPv6 branch:

```dart
socket.setRawOption(RawSocketOption(
  RawSocketOption.levelIPv4,
  RawSocketOption.IPv4MulticastInterface,
  interfaceAddress.rawAddress,
));
```

### Workaround

Callers can override `rawDatagramSocketFactory` and set the option on the returned socket themselves.

### Versions

Flutter 3.47.5 · Dart 3.13.4 · multicast_dns 0.3.3+1

[flutter_svg] Failed pending cache loads escape as unhandled errors and prevent retries
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. In the flutter_svg package on main, add and run the test below.
2. Complete the first load with an error.
3. Observe the unhandled asynchronous error. Then request the same key again with a successful loader; the failed pending future is reused and the loader is not called.
4. To see the user-facing impact, load an SVG with SvgPicture.network while the connection drops. The errorBuilder runs, but the escaped error reaches PlatformDispatcher.onError.

### Expected results

The future returned by putIfAbsent completes with the original error so callers can handle it. No separate unhandled asynchronous error reaches the zone or PlatformDispatcher.onError. The failed pending entry is removed, allowing a later request for the same key to retry.

### Actual results

The success-only pendingResult.then callback creates a derived future with no error handler. When loading fails, that derived future surfaces an unhandled asynchronous error. The failed future also remains in _pending, so subsequent requests for the same key replay the failure instead of retrying.

With SvgPicture.network, errorBuilder runs, but the widget does not expose the escaped future for the application to catch. This can reach PlatformDispatcher.onError and be recorded by Crashlytics as a fatal error.

Related: https://github.com/dnfield/flutter_svg/issues/881
Related PR: https://github.com/dnfield/flutter_svg/pull/1104

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter_svg/src/cache.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

void main() {
  test('Failed load is evicted from pending and retried', () async {
    final cache = Cache();
    final error = StateError('boom');
    final completer = Completer<ByteData>();
    final Future<ByteData> future = cache.putIfAbsent(
      'key',
      () => completer.future,
    );

    completer.completeError(error);
    await expectLater(future, throwsA(same(error)));
    await null;

    var calls = 0;
    await cache.putIfAbsent('key', () async {
      calls++;
      return ByteData(1);
    });
    expect(calls, 1);
  });
}
```

title: [Linux] Semantics are built on every frame even when no assistive technology is running
Nested SafeArea applies bottom view padding twice when the keyboard opens
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Put a text field and a bottom-anchored bar in a Scaffold.

2. Wrap the Scaffold in two nested SafeAreas. Set maintainBottomViewPadding: true on both, and disable their top, left, and right padding so only the bottom inset is involved. Keep the wrappers outside the Scaffold.

3. Run the app on an Android device or emulator with a nonzero bottom safe inset and a docked on-screen keyboard.

4. Note the gap below the bar with the keyboard closed. Tap the text field to open the keyboard and compare the gap. Close the keyboard to see it return to its original size.

On a Pixel 10 Pro emulator running Android 17, viewPadding.bottom remained 24.0 when the keyboard opened and viewInsets.bottom became 336.0.



#### Likely cause

With the keyboard open, SafeArea uses viewPadding.bottom because maintainBottomViewPadding is true, but its child [MediaQuery.removePadding](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c197ca5199e9ee5661e865596c9c07294dfab51c/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/safe_area.dart#L112-L136) consumes padding.bottom, which is then zero. The inner SafeArea still sees the bottom viewPadding and applies it again. A local patch that consumes that bottom view padding for descendants keeps the bars aligned in this demo.

### Expected results

The bottom bar stays one bottom safe inset above the keyboard: 24 logical pixels in this example. The inner SafeArea should not apply an inset already consumed by the outer one.

### Actual results

The bar sits two bottom safe insets above the keyboard: 48 logical pixels in this example. The extra gap disappears when the keyboard closes.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

One nested pair is sufficient to trigger the bug. This sample adds a panel with just one SafeArea as a visual baseline. Its two bars align with the keyboard closed; when the keyboard opens, the bar in the nested panel rises by one extra bottom inset. The text above the panels displays the root MediaQuery insets.

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Repro()));

class Repro extends StatelessWidget {
  const Repro({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final media = MediaQuery.of(context);

    Widget panel(bool nested) {
      Widget safe(Widget child) => SafeArea(
            top: false,
            left: false,
            right: false,
            maintainBottomViewPadding: true,
            child: child,
          );

      final scaffold = Scaffold(
        backgroundColor: nested ? Colors.green.shade50 : Colors.blue.shade50,
        body: Column(
          children: [
            Text(nested ? 'Two SafeAreas' : 'One SafeArea'),
            const TextField(
              decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Open keyboard'),
            ),
            const Spacer(),
            SizedBox(
              height: 48,
              child: ColoredBox(
                color: nested ? Colors.green : Colors.blue,
                child: Center(child: Text(nested ? 'Nested' : 'Single')),
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      );
      return safe(nested ? safe(scaffold) : scaffold);
    }

    return Material(
      child: SafeArea(
        bottom: false,
        child: Column(
          children: [
            Text('viewPadding.bottom=${media.viewPadding.bottom}; '
                'viewInsets.bottom=${media.viewInsets.bottom}'),
            Expanded(
              child: Row(
                children: [
                  Expanded(child: panel(false)),
                  Expanded(child: panel(true)),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

title: SnackBars on iOS show unusable and unnecessary Voice Control tag (reopening #193966)
body:
### Steps to reproduce 1. Create an app with a SnackBar and open it on an iOS device. 2. Enable Voice Control (https://support.apple.com/en-us/111778) 3. View the SnackBar This was tested on the latest stable flutter version (3.47.9), on an iPhone 17 running iOS 26.6.2. ### Expected results The SnackBar should have just one Voice Control tag, which can be used to close the snackbar. ### Actual results As seen in the image above, the SnackBar actually has two voice control tags. Tag '1' triggers no action, and it also should not be on the SnackBar. Tag '2' on the 'X' button is expected. I suspect this is because in packages/flutter/lib/src/material/snack_bar.dart inside _SnackBarState.build, the Semantics node unconditionally assigns an onDismiss action for swipe-to-dismiss behavior on SnackBars, and Voice Control is adding a tag for this. However, this doesn't actually do anything since Voice Control performs a tap, not a swipe. ``` snackBar = Semantics( container: true, liveRegion: true, onDismiss: () { ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).removeCurrentSnackBar(reason: SnackBarClosedReason.dismiss); }, child: Dismissible( // ... direction: dismissDirection, child: snackBar, ), ); ``` One potential fix would be omitting the onDismiss semantic action if dismissDirection is DismissDirection.none (I tried this locally and this seemed to fix the issue) ``` snackBar = Semantics( container: true, liveRegion: true, onDismiss: dismissDirection == DismissDirection.none ? null : () { ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).removeCurrentSnackBar(reason: SnackBarClosedReason.dismiss); }, // ... ``` ### Code sample
Code sample ```dart import 'package:flutter/material.dart'; final messengerKey = GlobalKey(); void main() { runApp(MaterialApp( scaffoldMessengerKey: messengerKey, home: const Scaffold(), )); WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) { messengerKey.currentState?.showSnackBar( SnackBar( behavior: SnackBarBehavior.fixed, dismissDirection: DismissDirection.down, content: const Text('Text'), action: SnackBarAction(label: 'X', onPressed: () {}), duration: const Duration(days: 365), ), ); }); } ```

[RFC] Size-aware design systems and tree-shakable theme defaults
body:
Every `MaterialApp` using `package:material_ui` retains `package:material_color_utilities` (`146` functions) and all 47 component `*ThemeData` classes in release builds—even when unused—because [`Theme.of`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/63881f9b118bc33792b338e7908f263ab936a6c4/packages/material_ui/lib/src/theme.dart#L136) and [`factory ThemeData`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/63881f9b118bc33792b338e7908f263ab936a6c4/packages/material_ui/lib/src/theme_data.dart#L343) unconditionally root them against Dart whole-program tree-shaking (`gen_snapshot`, `dart2wasm`, and `dart2js`), adding `180 KB` (`5.79%`) on Linux x64 AOT and `81 KB` (`3.25%`) on WebAssembly in [`kevmoo/slide_puzzle`](https://github.com/kevmoo/slide_puzzle).

### RFC Pull Request Link

https://github.com/flutter/rfc/pull/43

### Possible directions

- Break the `Theme.build` -> `InheritedCupertinoTheme` -> `Theme.of` -> `CupertinoBasedMaterialThemeData` -> `ColorScheme.fromSeed` retention cycle ([flutter/packages#13515](https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13515)).
- Store `ThemeData`'s 47 component themes in private nullable backing fields (`_fooTheme`) so Dart Type Flow Analysis constant-folds unused `.lerp()`, `==`, and `hashCode` paths without changing public getter types ([flutter/packages#13516](https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13516)).
- Add deterministic symbol-retention presubmit tests in `packages/material_ui` so unreferenced subsystems cannot silently re-enter release binaries.

Related: #91772, #101479

title: Lost-wakeup race in flutter::Pipeline between ProducerCommit and Consume permanently freezes UI rendering (PipelineFull)
[go_router] push into a StatefulShellRoute while a root-navigator route sits above the shell duplicates the shell's page/navigator key
body:
### Steps to reproduce

go_router 18.1.3 (also 18.1.4's `match.dart` is unchanged here).

1. `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack` with two or more branches (e.g. `/a`, `/b`).
2. Under branch `/a`, declare a child `GoRoute(path: ':id', parentNavigatorKey: rootNavigatorKey, ...)` so it is built on the root navigator, over the shell.
3. Open `/a/1` (cold link or `context.go('/a/1')`). The match list is `[ShellRouteMatch(branch a), GoRouteMatch(/a/1)]`.
4. `context.push('/b')` (any location whose last top-level match is the shell).

### Expected

`/b` is shown on top; later navigation keeps working.

### Actual

`RouteMatchList.push` -> `_createNewMatchUntilIncompatible` appends a clone of the shell match after the leaf. `_cloneBranchAndInsertImperativeMatch` only re-scopes the clone's page and navigator keys when `branch.route is ShellRoute`; a `StatefulShellRoute` clone keeps the original's keys. The root `Navigator` then holds two pages with one key:

```
Failed assertion: '!keyReservation.contains(key)': is not true.
... NavigatorState._debugCheckDuplicatedPageKeys
```

followed by `A GlobalKey was used multiple times inside one widget's child list` on every later navigation (the navigator is corrupted).

Observed in an app on go_router 18.1.3; the root cause was traced to the `branch.route is ShellRoute` condition in `_cloneBranchAndInsertImperativeMatch` (lib/src/match.dart). I have not yet reduced it to a standalone sample.

Workaround: open shell destinations with `go` while a route sits above the shell.

title: [Linux] libflutter_linux_gtk.so exports _Unwind_* since 3.50.0, C++ exceptions caught inside plugins abort the app
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --template=plugin --platforms=linux unwind_probe`
2. in `linux/unwind_probe_plugin.cc` add `#include <stdexcept>` and put this at the top of `unwind_probe_plugin_register_with_registrar`:

```cpp
  try {
    throw std::runtime_error("thrown inside the plugin");
  } catch (const std::exception& e) {
    g_print("unwind_probe: caught: %s\n", e.what());
  }
```

3. `cd example && flutter build linux --release` (same with `--debug`)
4. run `build/linux/x64/release/bundle/unwind_probe_example`

done with the official tarballs `flutter_linux_3.47.9-stable.tar.xz` and `flutter_linux_3.50.0-stable.tar.xz` on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 x64, each project created by its own sdk, two runs each

### Expected results

the exception is caught inside the plugin, like on 3.47.9:

```
unwind_probe: caught: thrown inside the plugin
```

### Actual results

on 3.50.0 the app aborts (SIGABRT, debug and release):

```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
terminate called recursively
```

real world case: `flutter_secure_storage_linux` throws `LibsecretError` when there is no unlocked keyring and catches it in its method call handler, so on 3.50.0 the app dies at start on any machine without one instead of getting a `PlatformException`

`libflutter_linux_gtk.so` exports an unwinder since 3.50.0:

```
$ nm -D --defined-only 3.47.9/flutter/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/linux-x64-release/libflutter_linux_gtk.so | grep -c _Unwind_
0
$ nm -D --defined-only 3.50.0/flutter/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/linux-x64-release/libflutter_linux_gtk.so | grep _Unwind_
0000000001037250 T _Unwind_DeleteException
00000000010370b0 T _Unwind_ForcedUnwind
00000000010372b0 T _Unwind_GetGR
0000000001037370 T _Unwind_GetIP
0000000001037140 T _Unwind_GetLanguageSpecificData
00000000010371e0 T _Unwind_GetRegionStart
0000000001036610 T _Unwind_RaiseException
0000000001036cd0 T _Unwind_Resume
0000000001037310 T _Unwind_SetGR
00000000010373d0 T _Unwind_SetIP
```

same 10 symbols in `linux-x64` and `linux-x64-profile`, 0 in all three on 3.47.9

`LD_DEBUG=bindings` on the 3.50.0 release build shows libstdc++ and even libgcc_s throwing through the engines copy:

```
binding file /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 [0] to .../bundle/lib/libflutter_linux_gtk.so [0]: normal symbol `_Unwind_RaiseException' [GCC_3.0]
binding file /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgcc_s.so.1 [0] to .../bundle/lib/libflutter_linux_gtk.so [0]: normal symbol `_Unwind_RaiseException' [GCC_3.0]
```

so the plugin is compiled against libstdc++/libgcc but unwinds with the llvm libunwind inside the engine, and the handler is never found

looks like it comes from #192607 (2553f89be1ef), `engine/src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn` at 3.50.0, lines 640 to 646:

```gn
    ldflags += [ "-nostdlib++" ]

    if (is_linux) {
      # Our custom libcxx doesn't include the unwinder, which is included in
      # libc++.a. Link the libunwind directly.
      ldflags += [ "--unwindlib=libunwind" ]
    }
```

on 3.47.9 linux was excluded there (`if (!is_linux) { ldflags += [ "-nostdlib++" ] }`). nothing hides the static libunwind, so its symbols end up in the dynamic symbol table. i guess `-Wl,--exclude-libs,libunwind.a` (or a version script) for the linux shared library would fix it, didnt build the engine to verify that. `testing/symbols/verify_exported.dart` only checks `libflutter_engine.so` on linux, not `libflutter_linux_gtk.so`, probably why it wasnt caught

workaround for apps: link libgcc_s first in `linux/runner/CMakeLists.txt`, then its unwinder wins the lookup again and the probe catches on 3.50.0 (debug and release, two runs each):

```cmake
target_link_options(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE
  "LINKER:--push-state,--no-as-needed,-lgcc_s,--pop-state")
```

maybe related to #188877, same area (static runtime of the engine colliding with the host process) but a different symptom

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

`linux/unwind_probe_plugin.cc` of a fresh `flutter create --template=plugin --platforms=linux unwind_probe`, only change:

```cpp
#include <stdexcept>

void unwind_probe_plugin_register_with_registrar(FlPluginRegistrar* registrar) {
  try {
    throw std::runtime_error("thrown inside the plugin");
  } catch (const std::exception& e) {
    g_print("unwind_probe: caught: %s\n", e.what());
  }
  // ... generated code unchanged
}
```

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

<details open><summary>Doctor output</summary>

```console
[!] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.50.0, on Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS 7.2.12-orbstack-00394-gbecdd6130068, locale en_US.UTF-8)
```

body:
### Steps to reproduce

We reproduced this with Flutter 3.47.7 / Dart 3.13.5 and the SDK `integration_test` package, using plain `FlutterTestRunner` (not Patrol).

1. Bundle a passing Dart integration-test suite into the application APK. Our reproducing Shop demo has ten `testWidgets` tests in its starter suite (catalog, product details, and cart).
2. Use `androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner` as the instrumentation runner and the `FlutterTestRunner` host below.
3. Build the app using the test entry point, and build the instrumentation APK:

```sh
flutter build apk --debug -t integration_test/starter_test.dart
(cd android && ./gradlew app:assembleDebugAndroidTest)
```

4. Run those APKs with Android Test Orchestrator. We reproduced the test-count mismatch locally on an arm64 Android API 36 emulator with Orchestrator **1.4.1 and 1.6.1**, and on a physical Galaxy S24 (API 34) through **Google Cloud Developer Device Platform (DDP), Device Run**:

```sh
gcloud beta device-run sessions submit instrumentation \
  --project=my-project \
  --device=e1q-34 \
  --apps=app.apk --test=test.apk \
  --orchestrator-version=auto
```

`app.apk` and `test.apk` above are the application APK built from the test entry point and its instrumentation APK, respectively. The DDP run used `auto`; the explicit 1.4.1/1.6.1 checks were local.

### Expected results

When all ten Dart test cases pass, instrumentation and the overall run should report success, with a consistent discovered/executed test count.

### Actual results

All ten test cases pass, but the instrumentation/orchestrator summary reports:

```text
FAILURES!!!
Tests found: 1, Tests run: 10,  Failures: 0
```

The DDP execution is consequently reported as:

```text
FAILED: 10 test cases passed
```

Its JUnit report contains `tests='10' failures='0' errors='0'` and no failing test cases.

This is not inferred solely from the DDP status: the same contradictory summary was recorded locally with Android Test Orchestrator. As a control, a separate native Kotlin/Compose ten-test suite on the same DDP Galaxy S24 configuration, also using `--orchestrator-version=auto`, completed with all ten tests passing and overall **PASSED**.

### Code sample

Runner setup from the reproducing application:

```java
package com.example.shopflutter;

import androidx.test.rule.ActivityTestRule;

 */
@RunWith(FlutterTestRunner.class)
public class MainActivityTest {
  @Rule
  public ActivityTestRule<MainActivity> rule =
      new ActivityTestRule<>(MainActivity.class, true, false);
}

```

The Dart suite registers ten normal `testWidgets` cases after:

```dart
IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized().framePolicy =
    LiveTestWidgetsFlutterBindingFramePolicy.fullyLive;
```

There are no parameterized JUnit host methods or custom result-reporting code. This excerpt shows the runner configuration; the recorded reproduction used the Shop suite described above, rather than a separately validated minimal project.

title: [web][tool] `flutter build web` after a `--web-content-hash` build leaves `build/web` without `index.html`
body:
### Steps to reproduce

```
flutter create --platforms=web hash_demo && cd hash_demo
flutter build web --web-content-hash
flutter build web
ls build/web/index.html
```

### Expected results

`build/web/index.html` exists after every successful `flutter build web`.

### Actual results

`ls: build/web/index.html: No such file or directory`. The build reports success (`✓ Built build/web`). Running `flutter build web` a second time restores `index.html`. Building with `--web-content-hash` after a plain build is fine.

`flutter build web -v` on the second build shows:

```
web_templated_files: Starting due to {InvalidatedReasonKind.buildKeyChanged ...}
web_templated_files: Complete
web_release_bundle: Starting due to {InvalidatedReasonKind.outputSetRemoval: The following outputs were removed from the output set: .../build/web/main.dart.276ca6e0.js, .../build/web/index.html, .../build/web/flutter_bootstrap.js, ...}
```

### Likely cause

In `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/targets/web.dart`, `WebReleaseBundle.outputs` includes `{OUTPUT_DIR}/index.html` and `{OUTPUT_DIR}/flutter_bootstrap.js` only when `_hasWebContentHash`. On the next plain build those paths leave the target's output set, so the build system deletes them as stale outputs, after `WebTemplatedFiles` (a dependency of `WebReleaseBundle`) has already written the new `index.html`. The same structure is on master today.

### Why it matters

Someone trying the new flag locally and then deploying a plain build from their machine ships a site without `index.html`.

body:
### Steps to reproduce

After upgrading from Flutter 3.47.8 to Flutter 3.50, my web app crashes when compiled to WebAssembly. The failure occurs in both debug and release modes, before the first Flutter frame is displayed.

I initially encountered the crash at:

`await PackageInfo.fromPlatform();`

After removing that call, an ordinary `http.get()` failed with the same stack trace.

I then reproduced the failure using only Dart SDK APIs, without HTTP requests or third-party package calls. Passing sink.close directly as a stream’s onDone callback causes a WebAssembly runtime trap. Wrapping the same call in a closure avoids the failure.

### Expected results

the wasm build should not crash

### Actual results

the wasm build crashes

title: [widget_preview] 5s timeout on `getFlutterWidgetPreviews` drops live updates in larger projects ("Lost connection to the Dart Tooling Daemon")
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Flutter app with roughly 1,000+ Dart files (app + local path packages) where previews transitively import a large part of the app.
2. Run `flutter widget-preview start` (also reproducible with `--web-server -v`).
3. Wait until the previewer has started and the previews are shown.
4. Edit and save a file that many libraries depend on (e.g. the file that builds the app's `ThemeData`).

## Expected results

The previewer waits until the analysis server is done and then updates the previews, as it did in Flutter 3.47.

## Actual results

The change is not applied. After about 25 seconds the tool prints:

```
Lost connection to the Dart Tooling Daemon (DTD). Live preview updates are paused. Details: TimeoutException after 0:00:05.000000: Future not completed
```

The connection to DTD is not actually lost. The message comes from the retry loop in
`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/widget_preview/lsp_preview_detector.dart`, which was added in #190929 to deal with flaky
integration tests:

```dart
result = await dtd.getFlutterWidgetPreviews().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5));
```

In a project of this size a full re-analysis takes longer than 5 seconds, so all 5 attempts time out and the update is dropped.
The only workarounds are saving the file again once analysis has finished or restarting the previewer.

### Measurements (`-v` log, timestamps summed from the log deltas)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 9–20 s | Initial analysis, ~1,000 files reported (~11 s) |
| 40 s | Re-analysis starts after a file change |
| 45 / 50 / 55 / 60 s | `Failed to get widget previews, retrying in 200ms... (4..1 retries left)` |
| 65 s | `Lost connection to the Dart Tooling Daemon (DTD). Live preview updates are paused.` |
| 40–70 s | Analysis server is busy the whole time: ~3,200 `publishDiagnostics` notifications, i.e. about 3 full passes of 7–10 s each |

The analysis server stops working shortly after the last retry. That suggests that every new `getFlutterWidgetPreviews`
request starts another analysis pass, so the server can never answer within the timeout. I have not verified this beyond the
log.

Other Dart analysis servers were running at the same time (IDE), which slows analysis down further. That is a normal
development setup, though.

### Suggestions

* Don't count time spent waiting for analysis against the timeout. For example, only start the timeout once `waitForAnalysis()`
  has completed, or wait for analysis again before each retry.
* Make the timeout configurable (flag or environment variable), or scale it with the project size.
* Reword the warning. "Lost connection" sends users looking for a DTD/network problem, although it is only a timeout.
* Apply the next file change normally. Users currently read "paused" as "restart required".

## Code sample

Not specific to the code. Any project where a full analysis pass takes more than 5 seconds should reproduce it.

## Flutter Doctor output


title: [gen-l10n] Generated localizationsDelegates uses deprecated GlobalMaterialLocalizations and GlobalCupertinoLocalizations from flutter_localizations
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Flutter 3.50.0 (stable), any app with `flutter: generate: true` and an ARB file.
2. Migrate the app to `material_ui` / `cupertino_ui` as described in https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/material-ui-and-cupertino-ui
3. Run `flutter gen-l10n` (or `flutter pub get`) and then `flutter analyze`.

### Expected results

The generated `app_localizations.dart` uses the non-deprecated delegates (`GlobalMaterialLocalizations` from `package:material_ui`, `GlobalCupertinoLocalizations` from `package:cupertino_ui`), or offers an option to do so, so a fully migrated app analyzes clean.

### Actual results

The template in `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/localizations/gen_l10n_templates.dart` always imports `package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart` and emits:

```dart
static const List<LocalizationsDelegate<dynamic>> localizationsDelegates = <LocalizationsDelegate<dynamic>>[
  delegate,
  GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegate,
  GlobalCupertinoLocalizations.delegate,
  GlobalWidgetsLocalizations.delegate,
];
```

which produces:

```
info • 'GlobalMaterialLocalizations' is deprecated and shouldn't be used. Use GlobalMaterialLocalizations from package:material_ui/material_ui.dart instead. This feature was deprecated after v3.47.0-0.0.pre • lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart • deprecated_member_use
info • 'GlobalCupertinoLocalizations' is deprecated and shouldn't be used. Use GlobalCupertinoLocalizations from package:cupertino_ui/cupertino_ui.dart instead. This feature was deprecated after v3.47.0-0.0.pre • lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart • deprecated_member_use
```

Editing the generated file does not help because `flutter pub get` regenerates it, and `flutter gen-l10n` refuses to run without `generate: true`. The only workaround is excluding the generated file from analysis.

### Flutter version

Flutter 3.50.0 • channel stable • framework revision ab2912035e • engine revision 371f77202a • macOS

title: [web] Tooltip text is read twice: while a tooltip shows, its target button's accessible name is doubled via aria-owns
body:
### Steps to reproduce 1. `flutter create bug`, replace `lib/main.dart` with the sample below (it calls `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()` so no screen reader is needed to build the DOM). 2. `flutter run -d chrome` (or `flutter build web` and serve it). 3. Open Chrome DevTools → Accessibility pane (or use a screen reader such as NVDA/VoiceOver). 4. Note the computed name of the `IconButton`: `New group`. 5. Hover the `IconButton` with the mouse until the tooltip appears (a long press with touch emulation gives the same result). 6. Check the computed name of the same button again. ### Expected results The button's accessible name stays `New group` while the tooltip is visible. The tooltip text is already exposed on the button through `Semantics(tooltip:)`, so showing the tooltip box should not change what the button is called. ### Actual results While the tooltip is visible, the button's accessible name is `New group New group`. Screen readers announce this computed name, so the label is read twice. The name goes back to `New group` when the tooltip hides (the overlay node is removed; the button keeps a stale `aria-owns` pointing at the removed id, which looks related to #195016). Chrome's accessibility tree (`Accessibility.getFullAXTree` over CDP), the `IconButton` node: | State | role | computed name | name source | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before hover | button | `New group` | contents | | tooltip visible | button | `New group New group` | contents | The DOM shows why: while the tooltip is visible, the button's semantics element gets `aria-owns` pointing at the tooltip overlay's semantics node, whose child holds the tooltip text. Because a button's name is computed from its contents, and aria-owned elements count as contents, the text is added a second time. ```text New group New group ... New group ``` The second widget in the sample (`Tooltip` around a `FilledButton` that has its own label) shows a milder form: the button's name stays `Delete`, but the wrapper node that carries the tooltip gets `aria-owns` to the overlay too, so the tooltip text `Delete the item` appears as an extra static text in the reading order while the tooltip is visible. Showing the tooltip through keyboard focus does not apply here: in this version a focused button does not show its tooltip. **Cause.** `RawTooltip` (which Material's `Tooltip` in both `package:flutter/material.dart` and `package:material_ui` builds on) exposes the message twice: - on the child, as `Semantics(tooltip: semanticsTooltip)`: [raw_tooltip.dart#L949-L952](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/raw_tooltip.dart#L949-L952) - in the overlay, where the `tooltipBuilder` output (a `Text` with the same message) is placed without excluding semantics: [raw_tooltip.dart#L886-L894](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/raw_tooltip.dart#L886-L894), shown through `OverlayPortal.overlayChildLayoutBuilder` at [#L965-L969](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/raw_tooltip.dart#L965-L969) Since the `OverlayPortal` semantics refactor (#173005, relanded in #178095, first in 3.41.0), `OverlayPortal` marks its child as the traversal parent of the overlay child ([overlay.dart#L2146](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/overlay.dart#L2146), [overlay.dart#L2724-L2730](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/overlay.dart#L2724-L2730)), and the web engine turns that into `aria-owns` ([semantics.dart#L977-L987](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/semantics.dart#L977-L987)). The tooltip's overlay text therefore ends up inside the button it describes. The framework's semantics tree (from `debugDumpSemanticsTree` in a widget test, same for `TargetPlatform.android` and `TargetPlatform.linux`) has the same shape while the tooltip shows, so this is not web-only in the framework; I have only confirmed the user-facing effect on the web and have not checked what TalkBack or Orca read. ``` ├─SemanticsNode#4 │ │ actions: focus, tap │ │ flags: isButton, hasEnabledState, isEnabled, isFocusable │ │ traversalParentIdentifier: _OverlayPortalState#f10eb │ │ tooltip: "New group" │ │ │ └─SemanticsNode#7 │ │ traversalChildIdentifier: _OverlayPortalState#f10eb │ │ │ └─SemanticsNode#8 │ label: "New group" ``` **Suggested fix.** When `semanticsTooltip` is non-empty, the message is already on the child, so `RawTooltip` could keep the overlay content out of the semantics tree, e.g. wrap `widget.tooltipBuilder(context, _overlayAnimation)` in `ExcludeSemantics`. I checked this on the web with two buttons built from the public `RawTooltip` in the shape `ButtonStyleButton` uses (`Semantics(container: true, button: true)` around a `RawTooltip` around an `InkWell`): `Control` with the overlay unchanged, and `Fixed` with the overlay wrapped in `ExcludeSemantics`. On hover the first is named `Control Control`, the second stays `Fixed`. (The empty overlay node is still aria-owned, which does not affect the name.) If the overlay should instead carry `SemanticsRole.tooltip` (#161630), it would need to describe the button (for example `aria-describedby`) rather than be owned by it, or the name doubles again. The relevant code is unchanged on `master` (22b8692dea61d1a2d467d22b4627d90e435206b0); I reproduced on 3.50.0 stable. ### Code sample
Code sample ```dart import 'package:flutter/material.dart'; import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart'; void main() { runApp(const MyApp()); // Turn semantics on without waiting for an assistive technology. SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics(); } class MyApp extends StatelessWidget { const MyApp({super.key}); @override Widget build(BuildContext context) { return MaterialApp( home: Scaffold( body: Center( child: Column( mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, spacing: 40, children: [ IconButton( icon: const Icon(Icons.add), tooltip: 'New group', onPressed: () {}, ), Tooltip( message: 'Delete the item', child: FilledButton( onPressed: () {}, child: const Text('Delete'), ), ), ], ), ), ), ); } } ```
### Screenshots or Video
Screenshots / Video demonstration No visual difference; the evidence is the accessibility tree and DOM excerpts above.
### Logs
Logs ```console Chrome 157.0.8103.50, headless, Accessibility.getFullAXTree, IconButton node: before hover: role=button name="New group" (source: contents) tooltip visible: role=button name="New group New group" (source: contents) after pointer left: role=button name="New group" (source: contents) ```
### Flutter Doctor output
Doctor output ```console [✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.50.0, on Manjaro Linux 7.2.9-1-MANJARO, locale en_US.UTF-8) • Flutter version 3.50.0 on channel stable • Upstream repository https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git • Framework revision ab2912035e (3 days ago), 2026-11-09 08:50:21 -0800 • Engine revision 371f77202a • Dart version 3.14.0 • DevTools version 2.61.0 [✓] Chrome - develop for the web • CHROME_EXECUTABLE = /usr/bin/google-chrome-stable [✓] Linux toolchain - develop for Linux desktop • clang version 23.1.1 • cmake version 4.4.4 • ninja version 1.13.2 • pkg-config version 3.0.7 [✓] Connected device • Linux (desktop) • linux • linux-x64 • Manjaro Linux 7.2.9-1-MANJARO • Chrome (web) • chrome • web-javascript • Google Chrome 157.0.8103.50 [✓] Network resources • All expected network resources are available. • No issues found! ```

title: [web][skwasm] Multi-threaded skwasm triggers a major V8 GC on the raster worker in every frame (seen in Chrome 157; the V8 rule dates from V8 14.8 / Chrome 148)
body:
## Summary

With the multi-threaded skwasm renderer, V8 starts one incremental marking and one major GC on the raster worker in
every frame. The cause is the `ImageBitmap` that skwasm creates in each frame with `transferToImageBitmap()`. Blink
reports each bitmap to V8 as external memory. Since V8 14.8 (Chrome 148), external memory counts against the global
allocation limit, with a growing factor of at most 1.1. On a large canvas, one bitmap is larger than the room that
this limit leaves, so each frame crosses the limit.

The GC frees nothing: the transfer to the main thread gives the external memory back before the GC finishes. On an
Apple M3 Max, the GC adds about 0.26 ms to the raster interval of each frame. Computed from the trace, it costs about
2 to 2.4 ms of CPU time for each frame in total. The behavior is the same in release and profile builds.

I found no existing issue in flutter/flutter, dart-lang/sdk or emscripten. The Chromium and V8 trackers were searched
only through a web search.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.50.0-0.4.pre (beta), engine 1b9ee1a5. The source of Flutter master at b98afb52407 (read, not run) has
  the same frame path for skwasm with threads: the same `transferToImageBitmap()` in each frame.
- Chrome 157.0.8103.39 (V8 15.7.112.23), macOS, Apple M3 Max, 120 Hz display. No other Chrome version was tested.
- `flutter build web --wasm`, served with `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and
  `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`, so that skwasm runs with threads.
- A viewport (`innerWidth` x `innerHeight`) of 1400 x 913 CSS pixels at device pixel ratio 2, that is, a canvas of
  2800 x 1826 physical pixels (5.1 megapixels). One bitmap is 4 x 2800 x 1826 = 20,451,200 bytes.

`flutter doctor -v`:

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `flutter create --platforms=web --empty gc_repro` and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code below.
2. Run `flutter build web --wasm`.
3. Put `serve.py` (below) in the project folder and run `python3 serve.py`. It serves `build/web` on
   http://127.0.0.1:8080 with the two headers above.
4. Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 in Chrome with a viewport of about 1400 x 913 CSS pixels at device pixel ratio 2. In the
   DevTools console, `crossOriginIsolated` must be `true`; otherwise skwasm runs single-threaded and there is no
   raster worker.
5. Record a trace of a few seconds with the categories `devtools.timeline`, `v8` and `disabled-by-default-v8.gc` (for
   example in `chrome://tracing` or the Perfetto UI).
6. On the `DedicatedWorker thread` of the raster worker, look at the events inside and after each
   `HandlePostMessage` of a frame.

`lib/main.dart`:

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

void main() => runApp(const GcRepro());

/// Repaints a full-window canvas in every frame.
class GcRepro extends StatefulWidget {
  const GcRepro({super.key});

  @override
  State<GcRepro> createState() => _GcReproState();
}

class _GcReproState extends State<GcRepro> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _controller = AnimationController(
    vsync: this,
    duration: const Duration(seconds: 2),
  )..repeat();

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _controller.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return CustomPaint(
      painter: _MovingBox(_controller),
      child: const SizedBox.expand(),
    );
  }
}

class _MovingBox extends CustomPainter {
  _MovingBox(this.progress) : super(repaint: progress);

  final Animation<double> progress;

  @override
  void paint(Canvas canvas, Size size) {
    canvas.drawRect(Offset.zero & size, Paint()..color = const Color(0xFFFFFFFF));
    final double x = (size.width - 100) * progress.value;
    canvas.drawRect(
      Rect.fromLTWH(x, size.height / 2 - 50, 100, 100),
      Paint()..color = const Color(0xFF2196F3),
    );
  }

  @override
  bool shouldRepaint(_MovingBox oldDelegate) => false;
}
```

`serve.py`:

```python
import functools
import http.server


class Handler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def end_headers(self):
        self.send_header('Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy', 'same-origin')
        self.send_header('Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy', 'require-corp')
        super().end_headers()


http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(
    ('127.0.0.1', 8080), functools.partial(Handler, directory='build/web')
).serve_forever()
```

The traces below come from a larger app with a continuous animation, not from this sample.

## What happens

In 4 traces (2 release and 2 profile builds, about 12 s of continuous animation each, 1400 to 1452 worker frame
handlers in each trace), each frame handler holds one `V8.GCIncrementalMarkingStart`, and a `MajorGC` follows each
handler: 1400 of 1400, 1434 of 1435, 1449 of 1449 and 1452 of 1452 handlers.

A typical cycle:

```
V8.GCIncrementalMarkingStart  gc_reason "global allocation limit", reason "global allocation limit reached",
    global_allocation_limit 82224788, global_consumed_bytes 90340729, global_space_available 0,
    old_gen_consumed_bytes 1610416, old_gen_space_available 9436940
V8.GCEnsureMinimumRemainingAllocationLimit  external_memory_since_mark_compact 20451287
MajorGC  type "finalize incremental marking via task"
V8.GCUpdateAllocationLimits  external_memory_low_since_last_gc 67779233, global_consumed_bytes 69433997,
    external_growing_factor 1.1, global_growing_factor 4, v8_growing_factor 1.1,
    computed_global_allocation_limit 81176212, next_global_allocation_limit 82224788
```

The old generation has room (9.4 MB available). Only the external memory crosses the limit. The heap size does not
change (1,611,964 bytes before, 1,610,156 bytes after).

## Why

1. `transferToImageBitmap()` creates an `ImageBitmap`. Its constructor calls `UpdateImageBitmapMemoryUsage()`, which
   reports `4 * width * height` bytes as external memory
   (`third_party/blink/renderer/core/imagebitmap/image_bitmap.cc`).
2. `Heap::UpdateExternalMemory()` calls `StartIncrementalMarkingIfAllocationLimitIsReached()` for a positive delta.
   `Heap::GlobalSizeOfObjects()` includes `external_memory()`, so the bitmap counts against the global limit
   (`v8/src/heap/heap.cc`).
3. After each GC, the global limit is about `(old generation + embedder) * global_growing_factor +
   external_memory_low_since_last_gc * external_growing_factor`. The external factor is the smaller of the global
   growing factor and the flag `--external-memory-max-growing-factor`, default 1.1 (`v8/src/heap/heap-controller.cc`,
   `v8/src/flags/flag-definitions.h`). The values of the cycle above reproduce this formula.
4. The worker isolate holds 67.8 to 73.5 MB of permanent external memory. I did not split it. One known part:
   `CanvasRenderingContextHost::UpdateMemoryUsage()` reports `WebGLRenderingContextBase::AllocatedBufferSize()` (the
   drawing buffer estimate, the resource provider and the cached snapshot) to V8 as external memory, so it probably
   grows with the canvas. With the factor 1.1, the room above the permanent part is 12.8 to 13.3 MB, which is less
   than one bitmap of 20.45 MB. So each frame crosses the limit.
5. The transfer of the bitmap to the main thread reports the decrease. So the GC finds nothing to free, and the next
   frame crosses the limit again.

V8 commit 6a5039d9db92 (2026-03-19, V8 14.8) turned on `external_memory_accounted_in_global_limit` by default and
lowered the external growing factor from 1.3 to 1.1 (Bug 361124432). Up to V8 14.7 the accounting was off by default,
and external memory had its own soft limit. With the accounting on and the old factor 1.3, the formula gives a limit
of about 95.8 MB against a peak of 90.3 MB, so no GC in each frame. These two figures are computed, not measured.

From the formula, and if the permanent external memory scales with the canvas area (about 3.3 bitmaps here), a GC
in each frame needs a bitmap above about 9 to 10 MB, that is, a canvas above about 2.2 to 2.5 megapixels. This is an
estimate.

## Cost

From the traces of the worker:

- Inside the raster interval: the marking start, 0.15 to 0.16 ms, and one marking step, 0.10 ms, in each frame.
- After the handler: about 0.46 ms of finalization on the worker, plus background jobs on 9 helper threads.
- In total, about 2 to 2.4 ms of CPU time for each frame. This is computed: the sum of the medians of the GC time of
  the worker inside and after the handler and of the thread-pool tasks. The pool part can include up to about 0.3 ms
  of WebAssembly tier-up compilation for each frame.
- The two longest worker stalls are inside GC events, off the CPU: 6.5 ms and 3.7 ms in
  `V8.GC_HEAP_ENSURE_SWEEPING_COMPLETED` (the wait for the end of background sweeping), in two consecutive frames of
  one of the 4 traces.

## Check with a flag

With `--js-flags=--external-memory-max-growing-factor=1.5`, the trace of one visit shows 2 marking starts in the 1140
frames of its 10 s capture window, against one in each frame without the flag. In 3 visits with the flag:

- The time from the `rasterEnd` stamp of the worker to the arrival of the `onRenderComplete` reply on the main thread
  is 0.045 to 0.070 ms at the median, against 0.140 to 0.175 ms in 7 default visits. The marking step of about
  0.10 ms is gone from that interval.
- The raster time of the worker (its `rasterStart` to `rasterEnd` stamps) is 0.08 to 0.19 ms shorter at the median of
  the 300 frames with the shortest engine callback of each visit.
- The mean `FrameTiming` raster time fell by only 0.02 to 0.15 ms, because the flag visits had longer engine
  callbacks. Their share of slow frames was not lower.

These are 3 visits on one machine, in different Chrome launches. They confirm the cause, not the full size of the
gain.

## Related

- denoland/deno#35808: the same V8 mechanism (the growing factor 1.1 under churn of external memory) in another
  runtime.
- nodejs/node#61967: names the V8 change (commit 6a5039d9db92) as the cause of another slowdown.

title: [widget_preview] Previewer restarts on pubspec.yaml changes in nested directories that are not part of the project or workspace
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `flutter widget-preview start` in a Flutter project.
2. Create a git worktree inside the project directory. Tools such as AI coding agents do this by default, e.g. under
   `.claude/worktrees/<name>`:
   ```bash
   git worktree add .claude/worktrees/some-branch -b some-branch
   ```
3. Edit `.claude/worktrees/some-branch/pubspec.yaml` or run `flutter pub get` there, or switch branches inside the
   worktree.

## Expected results

The previewer ignores the change: the nested `pubspec.yaml` belongs neither to the root project nor to one of its workspace projects.

## Actual results

The previewer runs a hot restart for every change:

```
Triggering restart based on update to pubspec.yaml: /path/to/project/.claude/worktrees/some-branch/pubspec.yaml
```

Edits to Dart files inside the worktree also trigger a preview lookup over DTD (`getFlutterWidgetPreviews`). This keeps the analysis busy and makes the DTD timeouts in `LspPreviewDetector` more likely.

## Cause

The file watcher watches the whole project directory recursively. `LspPreviewDetector._onFileSystemEvent` and `PreviewDetector` skip only `.dart_tool`, `.widget_preview` and the ephemeral directories of the project. `_fileAddedOrUpdated` then calls `onPubspecChangeDetected` for every path that ends with `pubspec.yaml`:

```dart
if (filePath.isPubspec) {
  onPubspecChangeDetected(filePath);
  return;
}
```

`PreviewManifest` already checks whether a pubspec belongs to the root project or to a workspace project
(`_isPubspecPathForProject`), but this check runs only after the restart has been triggered.

## Proposal

- Trigger the restart only for the pubspec of the root project or of a workspace project. Check against
  `rootProject.workspaceProjects` before calling `onPubspecChangeDetected`.
- Optionally, ignore Dart file changes in directories that do not belong to an analysis context of the project, or
  make the excluded directories configurable, e.g. through `analyzer: exclude:` in `analysis_options.yaml`.

As a local workaround, I added a check for a `.claude` path segment next to `doesContainDartTool` in both detectors.

## Environment

- Flutter (main channel) revision ab2912035e (2026-11-09), Dart 3.14.0
- macOS, `flutter widget-preview start` (web)

title: [Android] Phantom IME inset remains after returning through Recent apps and survives route pop
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the minimal reproduction:

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/liushuai42/flutter_keyboard_insets_repro.git
   cd flutter_keyboard_insets_repro
   flutter run --print-dtd
   ```

2. Open **2. Trigger page**.
3. Tap the text field and leave the keyboard visible.
4. Open Recent apps and switch to another app.
5. Return to the reproduction app through Recent apps.
6. Observe that the keyboard is not visible, but a keyboard-sized blank area can remain at the bottom.
7. Press Back and observe that the blank area can survive on **1. Observer page**, after the route containing the TextField has been disposed.

Step 4 & 5 can be replaced with just swipe up to Go Home and Click the app icon to Go Back.

The problem is intermittent and timing-sensitive. It reproduces on the affected Pixel 8 Pro in both debug and profile modes.

### Expected results

When the IME is no longer visible, Android and Flutter should both report a zero IME inset. The current route should use the full available height, and no keyboard-sized blank area should survive after popping the route containing the TextField.

### Actual results

After returning through Recent apps, the keyboard is no longer drawn, but the Flutter layout can remain resized by approximately the keyboard height. The stale blank area can survive popping the editable route and affect the previous route.

This appears related to, but observably different from #21193: the symptom is not only retained input focus. An invisible IME inset changes the layout globally and can remain after the editable route is disposed.

[Impeller][iOS Simulator] A stroked rect with a horizontal/vertical linear gradient ending on its bounds draws only the inner half of its stroke
body:
### Steps to reproduce 1. `flutter create --platforms ios,macos --empty stroke_repro`, and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below. 2. `flutter run` on an iOS Simulator, then on macOS, and read the console. The sample strokes a 100x100 square with `drawRect`, `PaintingStyle.stroke`, and a two-color linear gradient, renders it with `Picture.toImage`, and counts the pixels drawn. The stroke covers (100 + w)² − (100 − w)² = 400·w pixels for a width w. The gradient runs: - horizontally, from the square's left edge to its right edge; - vertically, from its top edge to its bottom edge; - diagonally, from its top-left corner to its bottom-right corner; - horizontally, from the stroke's outer left edge to its outer right edge. Gradients whose ends lie on the shape's bounds are what SVG's default gradient units (`objectBoundingBox`) give, so an SVG renderer such as vector_graphics makes these calls for any stroked `` with such a gradient. ### Expected results The whole stroke is drawn in every case, as on macOS: ``` stroke width 6.0, expected 2400: horizontal, ends on the square: 2400 vertical, ends on the square: 2400 diagonal, ends on the square: 2400 horizontal, ends on the stroke: 2400 stroke width 24.0, expected 9600: horizontal, ends on the square: 9600 vertical, ends on the square: 9600 diagonal, ends on the square: 9600 horizontal, ends on the stroke: 9600 ``` ### Actual results On the iOS Simulator, with a horizontal or vertical gradient whose ends lie on the square's bounds, only the inner half of the stroke is drawn, inside the square: 100² − 94² = 1164 pixels for a width of 6, and 100² − 76² = 4224 for 24. ``` stroke width 6.0, expected 2400: horizontal, ends on the square: 1164 vertical, ends on the square: 1164 diagonal, ends on the square: 2400 horizontal, ends on the stroke: 2400 stroke width 24.0, expected 9600: horizontal, ends on the square: 4224 vertical, ends on the square: 4224 diagonal, ends on the square: 9600 horizontal, ends on the stroke: 9600 ``` Other findings, from variants of the sample: - Diagonal gradients, and gradients whose ends lie on the stroke's outer bounds, draw the whole stroke. - Stroked lines and curves (`moveTo`/`lineTo`, `quadraticBezierTo`) with the same gradients draw the whole stroke. - Filled rects with the same gradients are drawn whole. - The same calls recorded into a picture that's drawn with `drawPicture` miss the same pixels. - With Flutter 3.47.x, these strokes weren't drawn at all on the Simulator. macOS drew them whole then too. One possible lead, not verified: `LinearGradientContents::CanApplyFastGradient` and `FastLinearGradient` (`impeller/entity/contents/linear_gradient_contents.cc`) take horizontal and vertical gradients whose ends lie on the geometry's coverage, and build their vertices between the gradient's start and end points, so nothing past the ends would be covered. It's unclear why macOS draws the whole stroke from the same calls. ### Code sample
Code sample ```dart import 'dart:typed_data'; import 'dart:ui' as ui; import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart'; const size = 160; /// Strokes a 100x100 square with a linear gradient from [from] to [to], and /// returns how many of its pixels were drawn. Future drawnPixels( double strokeWidth, Offset Function(Rect) from, Offset Function(Rect) to, ) async { const square = Rect.fromLTWH(30, 30, 100, 100); final recorder = ui.PictureRecorder(); Canvas(recorder).drawRect( square, Paint() ..style = PaintingStyle.stroke ..strokeWidth = strokeWidth ..shader = ui.Gradient.linear( from(square), to(square), const [Color(0xffd02020), Color(0xff2040e0)], ), ); final picture = recorder.endRecording(); final image = await picture.toImage(size, size); final bytes = Uint8List.sublistView((await image.toByteData())!); var drawn = 0; for (var p = 3; p < bytes.length; p += 4) { if (bytes[p] > 0) { drawn++; } } picture.dispose(); image.dispose(); return drawn; } Future main() async { WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized(); runApp(const SizedBox()); for (final strokeWidth in [6.0, 24.0]) { // The stroke covers (100 + w)^2 - (100 - w)^2 = 400 w pixels. print('stroke width $strokeWidth, expected ${(400 * strokeWidth).round()}:'); final cases = { // Ends on the square's bounds, as SVG's default gradient units put them. 'horizontal, ends on the square': ( (r) => r.centerLeft, (r) => r.centerRight, ), 'vertical, ends on the square': ( (r) => r.topCenter, (r) => r.bottomCenter, ), 'diagonal, ends on the square': ((r) => r.topLeft, (r) => r.bottomRight), // Ends on the stroke's outer bounds. 'horizontal, ends on the stroke': ( (r) => r.inflate(strokeWidth / 2).centerLeft, (r) => r.inflate(strokeWidth / 2).centerRight, ), }; for (final MapEntry(key: name, value: (from, to)) in cases.entries) { print(' $name: ${await drawnPixels(strokeWidth, from, to)}'); } } print('DONE'); } ```
### Screenshots or Video
Screenshots / Video demonstration Stroked squares, 6 px wide (top) and 24 px (bottom), with horizontal, vertical and diagonal gradients whose ends lie on the squares' bounds, drawn from an SVG's pictures (vector_graphics), through `drawPicture`, on the iOS Simulator (`_simulator.png`) and on macOS (`_macos.png`).
### Logs
Logs ```console flutter: stroke width 6.0, expected 2400: flutter: horizontal, ends on the square: 1164 flutter: vertical, ends on the square: 1164 flutter: diagonal, ends on the square: 2400 flutter: horizontal, ends on the stroke: 2400 flutter: stroke width 24.0, expected 9600: flutter: horizontal, ends on the square: 4224 flutter: vertical, ends on the square: 4224 flutter: diagonal, ends on the square: 9600 flutter: horizontal, ends on the stroke: 9600 flutter: DONE ```
