Doctor output ```console [✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.50.0, on macOS 26.7.2 25G332 darwin-arm64, locale en-IT) [368ms] • Flutter version 3.50.0 on channel stable at /Users/d.accornero/Applications/flutter • Upstream repository https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git • Framework revision ab2912035e (4 days ago), 2026-11-09 08:50:21 -0800 • Engine revision 371f77202a • Dart version 3.14.0 • DevTools version 2.61.0 • Feature flags: enable-web, no-enable-linux-desktop, enable-macos-desktop, no-enable-windows-desktop, enable-android, enable-ios, cli-animations, enable-native-assets, enable-record-use, enable-swift-package-manager, omit-legacy-version-file, enable-lldb-debugging, enable-uiscene-migration [✓] Android toolchain - develop for Android devices (Android SDK version 36.1.0) [546ms] • Android SDK at /Users/d.accornero/Library/Android/sdk • Emulator version 37.2.13.0 (build_id 16740729) (CL:N/A) • Platform android-37.0, build-tools 36.1.0 • ANDROID_HOME = /Users/d.accornero/Library/Android/sdk • Java binary at: /Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home/bin/java This is the JDK bundled with the latest Android Studio installation on this machine. title: [data_assets] Support fragment shaders from build hooks
body:
We should support reporting (compiled) fragment shaders in build hooks as data assets.

Multiple pieces are already in place:

* fragment shaders are loaded from the asset bundle as ordinary data assets already
* `impellerc` is already available in build hooks: https://github.com/flutter/core-packages/tree/main/packages/flutter_hook_config

Things that are missing:

1. `flutter_hook_config` target platform to pass the right flags to `impellerc` or a list of flags that would need to be passed to impellerc for the target
   * A target OS leaves the hook in control of the arguments
   * A impellerArguments means that flutter_tool controls the arguments. This means it has the freedom to evolve and ensure newer arguments are passed. So, this might be the better option.
2. An extra if to evict outdated shaders if a data asset filename ends in `.frag` (the same treatment as https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/187654)
3. A convenience package for calling `impellerc`.

The thing that I don't like about this design is the special casing for eviction. And the wish to have normal flutter assets to be OS-independent but to have shaders OS-dependent.

-------

An alternative design would be to not use `DataAsset` from `package:data_assets` but to introduce a `ShaderAsset` in `package:flutter_shaders` in a new package in https://github.com/flutter/core-packages/tree/main

That would make it explicit that:

1. the target platform may be used for `ShaderAsset`.
2. Avoid the need for a checking a file name.

We could then possibly do the same for the `ShaderBundleAsset`, and if we have a dedicated package we could have moved the `impellerc` to the `input.config.flutterShaders.impellerc`. And then we'd have `input.config.flutterShaders.targetPlatform` or `input.config.flutterShaders.impellerArguments`.

The only thing I don't like about this alternative design is that the loading is done from the `RootBundle` so it leaks out that under the hood it's normal data assets. And you have two asset types folding into data assets with potential name conflicts.

--------

A third alternative would be to have `ShaderAsset` not be the compiled frag file but the source file and keep compiling in Flutter itself.

--------

@bdero Any thoughts/ideas? Which alternative appeals more to you? Did you not have a need to know the target platform or `impellerc` flags for the shader bundles?

Context:

* https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/146264

title: [image_picker] iOS camera preview is upside down on iPhone Duo inner (unfolded) display
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an app that calls `ImagePicker().pickImage(source: ImageSource.camera)` on an iPhone Duo (iOS 27.2.1), with the phone unfolded (inner display).
2. Hold the phone upright in portrait.
3. Look at the live camera preview in the system camera screen opened by the picker.

### Expected results

The live preview is the right way up, as it is on the outer display, on other iPhones and in Safari's own camera upload.

### Actual results

What we checked:

- Folded (outer display), same build: preview correct.
- iPhone 13 (iOS 26.6.2), same build: preview correct.
- Safari on the iPhone Duo, inner display, `<input type="file" accept="image/*">` → Take Photo: preview correct.
- `image_picker_ios` 0.8.13+10 and 0.8.13+6: both affected.
- Removing `UIInterfaceOrientationPortraitUpsideDown` from `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad`: no change.
- iPhone orientations are Portrait, LandscapeLeft, LandscapeRight. The app uses `UIApplicationSceneManifest` with `FlutterSceneDelegate`.
- The app worked correctly on an iPhone 15 with an earlier Flutter version.

final picked = await ImagePicker().pickImage(

);

title: [Impeller] Vulkan onscreen swapchains bypass GPU submission tracking for HostBuffer
body:
Blocker for https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/192937

In Impeller's Vulkan backend, the host buffer uses a fixed-size ring of buffer slots so the CPU can prepare new frames while the GPU is still drawing earlier ones. To avoid overwriting a slot the GPU is still reading, the buffer relies on a submission tracker to know when each GPU workload finishes. Offscreen rendering goes through that tracker, but onscreen frame presentation submits its work directly to the graphics queue with its own synchronization and never reports it to the tracker.

Normal onscreen rendering avoids this bug because the swapchain already limits how many frames can be in flight at once, keeping it below the ring buffer's slot count. However, if an app takes several `toImage` or `toImageSync` snapshots in quick succession right after drawing an onscreen frame, and those snapshots reset the shared host buffer (as proposed in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/192937), the ring buffer can wrap around and overwrite data the GPU is still reading for the onscreen frame. For Flutter developers, that could show up as corrupted rendering, flickering geometry, or Vulkan driver faults when capturing multiple snapshots from a live scene.

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196064 fixes two separate bugs: making the Vulkan surface context forward the submission tracker at all, and preventing snapshots from advancing the ring buffer twice per capture. Because onscreen swapchains still bypass the tracker when presenting, forwarding the tracker in that PR is necessary for offscreen work but not sufficient to make onscreen frames visible to the host buffer.

Concretely, `SurfaceContextVK::SubmitOnscreen` hands `final_cmd_buffer` to `swapchain_->AddFinalCommandBuffer(...)`. `KHRSwapchainImplVK::Present` submits it directly via `context.GetGraphicsQueue()->Submit(submit_info, *sync->acquire)`, and `AHBSwapchainImplVK::Present` submits via `SubmitSignalForPresentReady` instead of going through `CommandQueueVK::Submit`. Because `RenderToTarget` calls `HostBuffer::Reset()` before `Present()`, `submission_tracker_->LatestSubmission()` does not include the onscreen submission. With `kHostBufferArenaSize = 4` in `HostBuffer`, three rapid `toImage` snapshots calling `ResetTransientsBuffers()` on the shared onscreen `AiksContext` can advance `frame_index_` to wrap back to slot 0 while the onscreen frame is still in flight.

title: [Android] TalkBack swipe navigation skips a platform view whose root view is not important for accessibility
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms android --org com.example bug`, replace `lib/main.dart` and `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/bug/MainActivity.kt` with the code below.
2. Run on an Android device and turn TalkBack on before the app starts.
3. Swipe right (next item) from "Flutter button above".
4. Swipe left (previous item) from "Flutter button below".

The platform view's root is a plain `FrameLayout` that holds three `TextView`s. The same happens with `useHybridComposition = false` (`AndroidView`, texture layer hybrid composition).

### Expected results

TalkBack stops on the platform view content ("Native text 1", "Native text 2", "Native text 3") between the two Flutter buttons, as it does when the platform view's root is a `WebView`.

### Actual results

TalkBack swipes from "Flutter button above" straight to "Flutter button below", in both directions. The native text is never read. Touch exploration over it gives only a short sound.

Same result under hybrid composition (HC) and texture layer hybrid composition (TLHC), on 3.47.2 and 3.50.0. Only roots that are important for accessibility on their own work:

| Platform view root | Read by TalkBack |
|---|---|
| `FrameLayout` > `LinearLayout` > 3 × `TextView` | ❌ |
| single `TextView` | ❌ |
| `FrameLayout` > `WebView` | ❌ |
| `WebView` | ✅ |
| `FrameLayout` forced to `YES` (workaround below) | ✅ |

<details><summary>uiautomator dumps</summary>

The full dump has the native views. The compressed dump, which matches what TalkBack sees, has Flutter's platform view node with no children:

```
uiautomator dump                              uiautomator dump --compressed
View '' [0,425][1080,1175]                    View '' [0,425][1080,1175]
  FrameLayout '' [0,425][1080,1175]             (no children)
    LinearLayout '' [0,425][1080,1175]
      TextView 'Native text 1'
      TextView 'Native text 2'
      TextView 'Native text 3'
```

</details>

### Cause

- `AccessibilityBridge` links the platform view with `result.addChild(embeddedView)` and sets it to `IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_AUTO` (in `createAccessibilityNodeInfo` and `updateSemantics`).
- Under `AUTO`, a plain container is not important. A `TextView` sets itself to `YES` in its constructor, but the engine overwrites that.
- TalkBack gets no node for a view that is not important, so the child link is dead and the whole subtree is missing.

This is the case left over from #113626: its fix, #168939, added the `AUTO` call, which works for roots that are important on their own, such as `WebView`.

### Proposed fix

Use `IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_YES` instead of `AUTO` in both places. The bridge has already added the view as a child, so the view must be reported to every service. Removal still sets `NO_HIDE_DESCENDANTS`. I intend to also open a PR with this fix.

<details><summary>Workaround for plugin authors</summary>

Return a root that keeps `YES` whenever the bridge sets `AUTO`. TalkBack then reads the platform view as one item.

```kotlin
class Root(context: Context) : FrameLayout(context) {
    override fun setImportantForAccessibility(mode: Int) =
        super.setImportantForAccessibility(
            if (mode == IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_AUTO) IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_YES else mode,
        )
}
```

</details>

### Code sample

<details><summary>Code sample</summary>

Full project with all root-view variants, both composition modes and a script that records the dumps and TalkBack swipe order: https://github.com/ddfreiling/flutter-platform-view-a11y-repro

`lib/main.dart`:

```dart
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/gestures.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

// true: hybrid composition (PlatformViewLink + initExpensiveAndroidView).
// false: texture layer hybrid composition (AndroidView). Both fail the same way.
const useHybridComposition = true;

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: ReproPage()));

class ReproPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const ReproPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      body: SafeArea(
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
          children: [
            ElevatedButton(onPressed: () {}, child: const Text('Flutter button above')),
            SizedBox(height: 250, child: _platformView()),
            ElevatedButton(onPressed: () {}, child: const Text('Flutter button below')),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }

  Widget _platformView() {
    const viewType = 'repro/native';
    if (!useHybridComposition) return const AndroidView(viewType: viewType);
    return PlatformViewLink(
      viewType: viewType,
      surfaceFactory: (context, controller) => AndroidViewSurface(
        controller: controller as AndroidViewController,
        gestureRecognizers: const <Factory<OneSequenceGestureRecognizer>>{},
        hitTestBehavior: PlatformViewHitTestBehavior.opaque,
      ),
      onCreatePlatformView: (params) => PlatformViewsService.initExpensiveAndroidView(
        id: params.id,
        viewType: viewType,
        layoutDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
        onFocus: () => params.onFocusChanged(true),
      )
        ..addOnPlatformViewCreatedListener(params.onPlatformViewCreated)
        ..create(),
    );
  }
}
```

`android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/bug/MainActivity.kt`:

```kotlin
package com.example.bug

import android.content.Context
import android.widget.FrameLayout
import android.widget.LinearLayout
import android.widget.TextView
import io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivity
import io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterEngine
import io.flutter.plugin.platform.PlatformView
import io.flutter.plugin.platform.PlatformViewFactory

class MainActivity : FlutterActivity() {
    override fun configureFlutterEngine(flutterEngine: FlutterEngine) {
        super.configureFlutterEngine(flutterEngine)
        flutterEngine.platformViewsController.registry.registerViewFactory(
            "repro/native",
            object : PlatformViewFactory(null) {
                override fun create(context: Context, viewId: Int, args: Any?): PlatformView {
                    // A plain container root. Its TextViews are important for accessibility,
                    // the container itself is not.
                    val root = FrameLayout(context).apply {
                        addView(LinearLayout(context).apply {
                            orientation = LinearLayout.VERTICAL
                            for (i in 1..3) addView(TextView(context).apply { text = "Native text $i"; textSize = 20f })
                        })
                    }
                    return object : PlatformView {
                        override fun getView() = root
                        override fun dispose() {}
                    }
                }
            },
        )
    }
}
```

</details>

title: Web: with semantics enabled, TextField loses first keystrokes typed right after focus (alternating attempts)
body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Flutter web app with a `TextField`. Enable semantics (click `flt-semantics-placeholder` "Enable accessibility", or use a screen reader, which enables it).
2. Click the text field and type right after the click (Playwright: mouse.move, press 90 ms, first key at 200-350 ms, 90 ms between keys).
3. Repeat 10 times.

### Expected
The full text appears in the field, as with semantics off.

### Actual
With semantics on, about half of the attempts lose the first characters ("yzw", "zw", "w") or everything, alternating attempt by attempt. Confirmed visually on screen. With semantics off: 20/20 correct, even typing at the instant of the click. The lost keys never reach `HardwareKeyboard`.

### Notes
Suspect: in semantics mode the editing goes through `SemanticsTextEditingStrategy`; the textarea is created/attached by the semantics node on focus and the click lands on the node first. The alternation suggests state that toggles on each focus (node swaps element or loses the listener on blur).

Flutter web, stable channel, Chromium (Playwright 1.52). `flutter doctor -v` output to be added.

title: [tool][web] Wasm dry run is on by default and adds a full extra compilation to every `flutter build web`; help text presents disabling it only as a way to "suppress warnings"
body:
Summary
Since Flutter 3.35 (#163163, #171682), every `flutter build web` without `--wasm` also runs a full dart2wasm compilation in "dry run" mode, concurrently with dart2js. Its output is discarded. The only visible result is one line: "Wasm dry run succeeded. Consider building and testing your application with the `--wasm` flag."
Even on the default counter app this adds ~70% build time, ~2.5× CPU time and ~2× peak memory. On a larger app on a memory-constrained machine it made release builds very slow and the whole system unresponsive. The flag help says "Compiles wasm in dry run mode during JS only compilations. Disable to suppress warnings." It does not say that this is a full second compilation running concurrently with dart2js, or that disabling it removes that cost.

Environment
- Flutter 3.47.9 (stable), Dart 3.13.7
- macOS 15.8.2, Intel x64, 8 GB RAM

Steps to reproduce
1. `flutter create --platforms web sample_app && cd sample_app`
2. `rm -rf .dart_tool/flutter_build && flutter build web --release`
3. `rm -rf .dart_tool/flutter_build && flutter build web --release --no-wasm-dry-run`
4. Compare wall time, CPU time and peak memory of the compiler processes.

Actual results
Fresh `flutter create` app (default counter), build cache cleared before each run:
- `flutter build web --release`: 37.8 s wall, 74.5 s CPU (user+sys), peak RSS of compiler processes 1353 MB (dart2wasm alone: 923 MB)
- `flutter build web --release --no-wasm-dry-run`: 22.0 s wall, 29.4 s CPU, peak RSS 683 MB

The verbose logs show `dart compile wasm` running in the first build and no dart2wasm in the second.

Larger app, same machine:
- dart2js and dart2wasm run at the same time. In Activity Monitor, dart2wasm was the top process at ~164% CPU, with 6 minutes of CPU time in a single build.
- With the dry run: 120 s and 157 s with free memory; 551 s and 725 s under memory pressure (6–8 GB of a 9 GB swap in use), with the machine barely usable the whole time. Without the dry run, a full build from a cleared build cache: 130 s.

With analytics enabled, each dry run is also reported as a `wasm_dry_run_package` event (82 events from this machine in 7 days). The developer pays for a full extra compilation that also serves this telemetry, as stated in #163163 ("track the % of builds that would fail").

How measured: `/usr/bin/time -l` for wall and CPU time; RSS sampled once per second with `ps` (sum of dart2js, dart2wasm, frontend_server and flutter_tools build processes).

Expected results
A plain `flutter build web` should not do a full extra compilation by default. Any of these would solve it:
- make the dry run opt-in (`--wasm-dry-run`), or run it once per project/Flutter version and cache the result;
- run it after dart2js instead of concurrently, so peak memory does not double;
- skip it automatically in release builds or when the machine is low on memory.

The help text for `--[no-]wasm-dry-run` and the build output should say that the dry run is a full dart2wasm compilation, not only a way to "suppress warnings".

Workaround
`flutter build web --release --no-wasm-dry-run`

Attached: `flutter doctor -v`, verbose build logs and measurements for both counter-app runs.
[flutter-wasm-dry-run.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34843984/flutter-wasm-dry-run.zip)

Related: #163163, #171682, #174149

title: [web][Android] Chrome's desktop site, the default on large Android tablets, is detected as Linux
[iOS] viewInsets.bottom drops mid-rise and then re-rises slowly when a third-party keyboard briefly reports a smaller height while showing
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On an iPhone, enable a third-party keyboard extension (seen with the Korean keyboard 한글키 from the App Store) and make it the active keyboard.
2. In a Flutter app, tap a `TextField` so the keyboard shows. Any layout that follows `MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom` makes it visible (e.g. a `Scaffold` with `resizeToAvoidBottomInset`, a bottom sheet with `Padding(viewInsets)`, a `Dialog`).
3. Dismiss the keyboard and tap the field again; repeat.

### Expected results

`viewInsets.bottom` rises monotonically with the keyboard and arrives with it.

### Actual results

In about half of the taps, `viewInsets.bottom` rises, then **drops** by 47–122 pt (median 66 pt) about 110 ms after the tap, and then rises again on a slow ease-in-out curve. It arrives ~70–90 ms after the non-dropping case (median 505–525 ms vs 434 ms from the tap). The keyboard itself does not do this: it keeps following its original spring and arrives at ~458–466 ms, so content first moves down and then trails the keyboard by up to ~210 pt.

With the system Korean keyboard on the same device and build: 0 of 12 taps.

Measured on a real device (iPhone 17 `iPhone18,3`, iOS 27.2, 120 Hz, profile build) with an integration-test harness: 44 taps, 25 dropped. For each tap we logged, on the same clock (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW`, aligned to `FrameTiming.vsyncStart`): every keyboard notification, the engine's keyboard-inset decisions and output (`updateViewportMetricsWithInset:`, swizzled for measurement only), the system keyboard's position (`UIRemoteKeyboardWindow > UIInputSetHostView` presentation layer), and `viewInsets.bottom` per frame.

### What happens (every dropped tap, and in none of the others)

1. ~72 ms after the tap, UIKit posts `WillChangeFrame` + `WillShow` with **begin frame `CGRectZero`** and end frame `(0, 532, 402, 342)`, duration 0.383 s, inside the keyboard's spring animation block (`UIView.inheritedAnimationDuration` = 0.383). Because `begin.y (0) > end.y (532)` is false, the manager records the animation as **not showing**, then starts a spring (k 555.03, c 47.12, m 1) toward 342 pt. Taps that don't drop end here.
2. 110–152 ms after the tap, the keyboard extension reports a transient height: `Did`/`Will` `ChangeFrame` + `Show` with end frame `(0, 733, 402, 141)` — posted **outside** any animation block (`inheritedAnimationDuration` = 0). Direction is again "not showing" (`532 > 733` is false) and the vsync client is alive, so the animation is treated as compounding and only the spring's `toValue` changes, 1026 → 423 px. The spring value is proportional to `toValue - fromValue`, so the reported inset immediately drops to ~141/342 of its value.
3. 12–27 ms later the extension reports 342 pt again (`(0, 733, …141)` → `(0, 532, …342)`), also outside an animation block. Now `733 > 532` is true, the direction differs, so `startKeyBoardAnimation` restarts from the **dropped** current inset (50–97 pt). Since the call isn't inside the keyboard's animation block, `animateWithDuration:` produces a `CABasicAnimation` with the default ease-in-out curve (0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) instead of a `CASpringAnimation`, so the manager falls back to the presentation layer and starts slowly.

Engine-reported and Dart-observed drops matched on all 44 taps (same verdict, same magnitude). On taps without the transient, the engine inset tracks the keyboard closely (median difference ~2 pt at the frame's target time).

The same logic is on master (`5aa30617`), `engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/KeyboardInsetManager.swift`: direction and compounding at lines 151–161, restart at 325, presentation-layer fallback at 407–408, spring setup at 444–456. Observed on 3.47.6 (`FlutterKeyboardInsetManager.mm` lines 77–88, 273–275, 374–379).

- Treat an empty begin frame (`CGRectZero`) on `WillShow` as a showing animation, so the direction check isn't inverted.
- While a show animation is in flight, a frame change that is posted outside an animation block and is followed by a return to the previous height could be ignored or coalesced; at least, lowering `toValue` mid-show should not make the reported inset go down.
- When restarting outside an animation block, reuse the previous spring parameters rather than the default `UIView` curve.

Related: #193343 (same area — a height change mid-animation followed by a hide yields a huge negative inset for one frame; different cause and symptom).

body:
### Steps to reproduce 1. `flutter create --platforms android --empty sheet_repro`, and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below. 2. In `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, inside ``, ask for Impeller's Vulkan backend (the emulator gets OpenGL ES otherwise): ```xml ``` 3. Start an Android emulator with its host GPU (`hw.gpu.mode=host`), and `flutter run` on it. The log shows "Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan)". 4. Tap either item of the bottom navigation bar, which shows a modal bottom sheet. 5. For comparison, set the manifest value to `opengles` and run again. ### Expected results The sheet slides up from the bottom, over the dimmed screen, as with OpenGL ES on the same emulator (screenshot `opengles.png`). ### Actual results The modal barrier dims the screen, but the sheet never shows (screenshot `vulkan.png`). The DEBUG banner, which shows before the tap, disappears too, so nothing above the barrier seems to draw. The route is there: tapping the barrier pops it, and the screen comes back as before. - With OpenGL ES on the same emulator, the sheet and the banner draw. - With Vulkan on the same AVD started with `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` (device "Goldfish GFXStream (SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0))", driver "gfxstream (SwiftShader driver)", Vulkan 1.3), the sheet and the banner draw too. So only the host GPU path fails. - The log shows no Dart exception and no Vulkan validation message (the debug build loads `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`). - We found it in a Widgetbook app, whose Navigation, Addons and Knobs panels are `showModalBottomSheet`s, and narrowed it down to the sample below. - On the same emulator's Vulkan, other canvas content also draws empty or wrong once frames hold a few hundred draws, while SwiftShader draws it, so this may be one more symptom of the host GPU path (gfxstream to MoltenVK) rather than of the sheet itself. ### Code sample

title: Confusing `AccesibilityFeatures` API
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Since https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/180041, web now additionally sets `reduceMotion` which was previously iOS exclusive. 

This makes the API extremely confusing as there are two related properties that behave differently across multiple platform:
* [`disableAnimations`](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/AccessibilityFeatures/disableAnimations.html
* [`reduceMotion`](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/AccessibilityFeatures/reduceMotion.html). 

Furthermore, the documentation for `reduceMotion` seems to be outdated.

title: `flutter run --trace-to-file`: path is resolved on the device, and the flag is hard to use on iOS
body:
### Use case

### Summary
The help text of `--trace-to-file` says: "Write the timeline trace to a file at the specified path." It does not say that the path is passed to the app and that the app writes the file **on the device**. On iOS, the flag is practically not usable with `flutter run`, because the only writable location contains a UUID that changes with each installation.

### Environment
- Flutter 3.44.1 (stable), macOS
- Android 16 device (profile build)
- iOS 26.6 device, connected via USB (profile build)

### Steps to reproduce
1. `flutter create trace_test && cd trace_test`
2. Android, relative path: 
   `flutter run --profile --endless-trace-buffer --trace-to-file=trace.binpb`
   No file is written. logcat shows `E DartVM: Warning: failed to initialize perfetto file timeline recorder trace.binpb: Failed to open timeline file.`
3. Android, absolute path in the app directory:
   `flutter run --profile --endless-trace-buffer --trace-to-file=/data/data/com.example.trace_test/cache/trace.binpb`
   The file is written and can be copied with `adb exec-out run-as com.example.trace_test cat cache/trace.binpb > trace.binpb`.
4. iOS (device via USB): run `flutter run --profile` twice and compare the data container of the app after each run,  for example with the VM service RPC `_createDevFS`, which returns a directory in the container. The UUID in `/private/var/mobile/Containers/Data/Application/<UUID>/` is different after each run. Thus a path given to `--trace-to-file` cannot point to the current container.

### Observed behavior
1. **The path is a device path.** On Android, `flutter run` passes the value as intent extra
   (`adb shell am start ... --es trace-to-file <path>`), on iOS as launch argument (`--trace-to-file="<path>"`). A path on the host (for example `build/trace.binpb`) never produces a file on the host.
2. **Relative paths fail silently.** The working directory of the app process is `/` (checked on Android via `/proc/<pid>/cwd`). With `--trace-to-file=trace.binpb`, no file is written. The only hint is in logcat: `E DartVM: Warning: failed to initialize perfetto file timeline recorder trace.binpb: Failed to open timeline file.` The `flutter run` console shows nothing. On iOS, no file appears in the data container either.
3. **Android works with an absolute path** in the app directory, for example `--trace-to-file=/data/data/<package>/cache/trace.binpb`. The file is written while the app runs and can be copied with `adb exec-out run-as <package> cat cache/trace.binpb > trace.binpb` (profile builds are debuggable).
4. **iOS: no stable writable path.** The app can only write to its data container `/private/var/mobile/Containers/Data/Application/<UUID>/`. The UUID changed between two consecutive `flutter run` invocations, because `flutter run` installs the app each time. Thus the path must be given before the installation, but it is only known after the installation. `xcrun devicectl` does not report it. It can be found, for example, with the VM service RPC `_createDevFS` of the running app or with `po NSHomeDirectory()` in the Xcode debugger. The flag only worked when the already installed app was started without a new installation: `xcrun devicectl device process launch --terminate-existing <bundle id> --trace-to-file=<container>/tmp/trace.binpb` That is no longer `flutter run`.
5. Possibly relevant, not verified: on iOS, flutter_tools builds the argument as `--trace-to-file="$traceToFile"` (`DebuggingOptions.getIOSLaunchArguments`). If the launch arguments are passed without a shell, the quotes become  part of the path.

### flutter doctor -v

```

### Proposal

### Expected behavior / proposal
- Document in the help text that the path is on the device, that it must be absolute and writable by the app, and how to copy the file to the host.
- Show an error in the `flutter run` console if the timeline file cannot be opened.
- Make the flag usable on iOS, for example by accepting a path relative to the app's data container (or `tmp`) and by letting flutter_tools copy the file to the host, or by resolving a placeholder for the container.

[Windows] Rendering stops for good after Modern Standby on a hybrid-GPU laptop; engine threads are idle, no device-loss recovery
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a laptop with hybrid graphics (Intel Iris Xe + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU, NVIDIA Optimus) that supports Modern Standby.
2. Build and run a Flutter Windows desktop app in release mode. The app runs on the NVIDIA GPU (no per-app GPU preference is set, and `nvwgf2umx.dll` is loaded).
3. Leave the app running. Let the laptop go into Modern Standby and wake up several times, with power source changes (plugging and unplugging the charger) in between.
4. After one of the wakes, click or type in the app.

The freeze does not happen on every wake. In our case it happened after about 20 standby cycles over one day. I have not yet reduced it to a `flutter create` app. The app is a normal Material app with no platform views and no external textures.

### Expected results

The app keeps rendering after the system wakes. If the D3D device is lost, the engine creates a new device or context and renders again.

### Actual results

The window shows the last frame forever. Input does nothing. Minimizing and restoring the window does not help. Only a restart of the app helps.

What I measured on the frozen process:

- The Win32 window is not hung. `IsHungAppWindow` is false and `Process.Responding` is true.
- CPU use is about 1% of one core. Nothing spins.
- A real mouse click on a `TextField`, captured from the real screen (not `PrintWindow`), changes no pixel: no focus border and no caret.
- The app's last rendered frame contains output from 08:43. The event log shows `Kernel-Power 506` (entering Modern Standby) at 08:49, and many 506/507/105 events after that. No `4101` display-driver reset event was logged.
- Graphics modules in the process: `d3d11.dll`, `dxgi.dll`, `d3dcompiler_47.dll`, `nvwgf2umx.dll` (ANGLE on D3D11 on the NVIDIA GPU).

I paused each thread and walked its stack with dbghelp (export symbols only). No thread is blocked on a lock. Every thread is in its idle wait:

- Platform thread (owns the window, about 606 s CPU over its lifetime): `NtUserGetMessage < GetMessageW < fast_ssh.exe`. With the merged platform/UI thread, Dart is idle and still gets input.
- Two fml message-loop threads (raster and io, identical stacks): `NtWaitForSingleObject < WaitForSingleObjectEx < flutter_windows.dll` (idle message loop wait).
- Dart IO thread: `ZwRemoveIoCompletion < GetQueuedCompletionStatus < flutter_windows.dll`.
- About 20 worker threads: `SleepConditionVariableSRW < flutter_windows.dll` (idle pool).
- NVIDIA driver threads: `WaitForSingleObjectEx < nvwgf2umx.dll`.

So the engine is not deadlocked. Input is processed, but no frame is ever produced or presented again. This matches a lost D3D device after the dGPU is powered off during standby, with no recovery path. The release build has no console, so I could not capture the ANGLE `device was removed` log line.

This looks like the same root cause as #124194 (open since 2023, still reported on 3.47). I file this separately because the trigger here is ordinary Modern Standby on a hybrid-GPU laptop, not a user disabling the GPU, so any desktop app on such a laptop can hit it during normal use. Please close this as a duplicate if you prefer to track it there. Related: #163732, #88649.

Workaround we are testing: `project.set_gpu_preference(flutter::GpuPreference::LowPowerPreference)` in `windows/runner/main.cpp`, so ANGLE uses the integrated GPU, which stays powered during standby. This avoids the trigger. It does not fix the missing device-loss recovery.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

No minimal sample yet. The only runner change from the template is the window size. `windows/runner/main.cpp` creates the project with `flutter::DartProject project(L"data");` and sets no GPU preference.

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

_No response_

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

Release build, no engine log available. The thread stacks are summarized above.

</details>

[vector_graphics_compiler] An empty self-closing <defs/> is reported as an unhandled element
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Parse an SVG that contains an empty, self-closing `<defs/>` element, which Inkscape and other editors write.
2. Use `warningsAsErrors: true` with `parse`, `parseWithoutOptimizers` or `encodeSvg`, in a debug build.

```dart
import 'package:vector_graphics_compiler/vector_graphics_compiler.dart';

void main() {
  const svg = '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 10 10">'
      '<defs/><rect width="10" height="10" fill="red"/></svg>';
  parseWithoutOptimizers(svg, warningsAsErrors: true);
}
```

### Expected results

The SVG parses, since an empty `<defs/>` is valid and defines nothing. A `<defs>` element with children parses without a warning today.

### Actual results

```
UnimplementedError: unhandled element <defs/>; Picture key:
```

Without `warningsAsErrors`, debug builds print `unhandled element <defs/>; Picture key: ...`, for example through `SvgPicture` in `flutter_svg`. The rendered output is correct in both cases.

### Cause

`SvgParser.startElement` only handles `<defs>` when it has children, so a self-closing one falls through to `unhandledElement`:

https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/66784038cf/packages/vector_graphics_compiler/lib/src/svg/parser.dart#L1115-L1121

### Flutter version

Reproduced with `vector_graphics_compiler` at 66784038cf (1.3.6) on Windows 11, running the snippet above with `dart run --enable-asserts`.

```
Flutter 3.47.7 • channel stable
Framework • revision abaf9c5237
Tools • Dart 3.13.5
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put two `ExpansionTile`s, `initiallyExpanded: true`, inside a `Card` (or any other `Semantics(container: true)`). Give each tile two rows wrapped in `Semantics(label: ..., excludeSemantics: true)`.
2. Run the widget test below (default target platform Android) with `material_ui` 1.6.0, then with 1.7.0 or later.

This came up when we migrated an app from the framework's `ExpansionTile` to `material_ui`: a semantics test of a card with expandable sections started failing.

### Expected results

Each row keeps its own semantics node, so TalkBack can focus one row at a time. That is what the framework's `ExpansionTile` (Flutter 3.50.0) and `material_ui` up to 1.6.0 produce.

If the new tree is intended, a changelog note would help, because migrating from the framework's `ExpansionTile` changes what a screen reader reads with no other sign.

### Actual results

From 1.7.0 on, the rows no longer form nodes. Their labels are joined, newline separated, into the label of the card's node, so TalkBack reads every row of every expanded tile as one item. `find.bySemanticsLabel('A row one')` finds nothing.

Bisected over 1.4.0 to 1.11.0. The only change to `expansion_tile.dart` between 1.6.0 and 1.7.0 is `container: true` on the Android header `Semantics` (live region, `blockNode`), from flutter/packages#12765 for #188298. A copy of 1.11.0 with just that line removed passes the test again. Without a container ancestor, all versions keep the rows apart.

The rows merging upward may be ordinary semantics merging once the header is its own container, and the separate nodes in 1.6.0 a side effect of the header's config. `container: true` on each row's `Semantics` gives the old tree back, which is what we did. flutter/packages#12835 (draft) also changes this header `Semantics`.

[iOS] CJK text in the default text style falls back to Hiragino Sans instead of the system UI font's cascade, rendering one weight step lighter than native
body:
### Steps to reproduce

On iOS, CJK text in the default text style (no `fontFamily`, or an app-bundled `fontFamily` with no CJK glyphs) falls back to a different font than native UIKit text does, so it is one weight step lighter than native at the most common weights (400 and 600).

This looks related to #105014 / #132475 (fixed in 3.41 via Skia), and to #179104, which was closed as a duplicate of #105014. The weights are no longer stuck at 400 on 3.47.8. But the font that CJK falls back to still differs from native.

1. Run the code sample below on an iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.2) with Flutter 3.47.8.
2. Draw the same string natively with `UIFont.systemFont(ofSize:weight:)` for the same weights.
3. Compare the Japanese glyphs.

### Expected results

Japanese text should use the same fallback font as native system-font text. Native UIKit draws `UIFont.systemFont(ofSize:weight:)` Japanese text with `.HiraKakuInterface-W*`:

| weight | native UIKit (system font) | Flutter 3.47.8 (no fontFamily) |
|---|---|---|
| 300 | .HiraKakuInterface-W2 | HiraginoSans-W3 |
| 400 | .HiraKakuInterface-W4 | HiraginoSans-W3 |
| 500 | .HiraKakuInterface-W5 | HiraginoSans-W4 |
| 600 | .HiraKakuInterface-W6 | HiraginoSans-W5 |
| 700 | .HiraKakuInterface-W6 | HiraginoSans-W6 |
| 800 | .HiraKakuInterface-W7 | HiraginoSans-W7 |

### Actual results

Flutter falls back to `Hiragino Sans` (right column above), so 400 and 600 come out one step lighter than native. The glyph metrics also differ: `.HiraKakuInterface` is about 6% narrower and 7% shorter than `Hiragino Sans` at the same font size. The same happens with an app-bundled Latin-only `fontFamily` (e.g. IBM Plex Sans) and no `fontFamilyFallback`.

Explicitly naming `Hiragino Sans` (as `fontFamily` or in `fontFamilyFallback`) gives the right column. Native `UIFontDescriptor` with family `Hiragino Sans` maps weights the same way, so that case is fine.

Setting `fontFamily: '.AppleSystemUIFont'` gives the native (left) column, which suggests the difference is in which font the fallback search starts from.

I logged the typeface SkParagraph picked for each run and measured the pixels. Results were the same on every launch, and there was no fake bold.

### Cause (as far as I can tell)

In Skia's `src/ports/SkFontMgr_mac_ct.cpp`, `onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter` builds a descriptor from the paragraph's first family name (`CupertinoSystemText`, or an app-bundled family such as `IBMPlexSans`) and calls `CTFontCreateWithFontDescriptor`. CoreText does not know these names, so it quietly returns Helvetica. The character fallback (`CTFontCreateForStringWithLanguage`) then follows Helvetica's cascade list, which leads to `Hiragino Sans`. Native text follows the system UI font's cascade list instead, which leads to `.HiraKakuInterface`.

I locally patched `onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter` (about 20 lines). When the requested family doesn't resolve, the patch uses `create_descriptor(CFSTR(".AppleSystemUIFont"), style)` as the base font. I built a local engine (`ios_debug_sim_unopt_arm64`) with it. The "no fontFamily" and "bundled Latin-only fontFamily" cases then matched native exactly (W2/W4/W5/W6/W6/W7). Explicit `Hiragino Sans` cases were unchanged.

My patch decided "doesn't resolve" by comparing the family name of the returned font. That would misfire on localized family names. Checking whether `CTFontDescriptorCreateMatchingFontDescriptor(desc, name_required)` returns null is probably more robust; I haven't tried that variant.

Note that this also changes fallback for other scripts (Chinese, Korean, Thai, Arabic, some symbols) from the Helvetica cascade to the system UI font's cascade. That is arguably more native, but it is a behavior change. If changing Skia is too broad, the same substitution could live on the Flutter side by wrapping the `SkFontMgr` in `txt/src/txt/platform_mac.mm`. I haven't tried that.

I'm happy to provide the patch or more data.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const App());

const weights = [
  FontWeight.w300, FontWeight.w400, FontWeight.w500,
  FontWeight.w600, FontWeight.w700, FontWeight.w800,
];

class App extends StatelessWidget {
  const App({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        backgroundColor: Colors.white,
        body: SafeArea(
          child: Column(
            crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
            children: [
              for (final w in weights)
                Text(
                  '${w.value} 過去 簡単な記録 見出し',
                  style: TextStyle(
                    fontSize: 22,
                    fontWeight: w,
                    color: Colors.black,
                    locale: const Locale('ja', 'JP'),
                  ),
                ),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new Flutter Windows application using Flutter 3.10.4:

   flutter create test_app
   cd test_app

2. Build the Windows release version:

   flutter build windows --release

3. Launch the application on Windows 11 (build 26300):

   .\build\windows\runner\Release\test_app.exe

4. Observe that the process starts successfully (visible in Task Manager) but no window is displayed.

5. Wait 7-8 seconds - the process crashes with exception code 0xc0000409.

6. Check Windows Event Log, Application section, Event ID 1000:
   - Faulting module: flutter_windows.dll
   - Exception code: 0xc0000409 (STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN)
   - Fault offset: 0x0000000000d23188

Environment:
- Windows 11 Pro build 26300
- Flutter 3.10.4 (bundled with application)
- Hardware: AMD Radeon 880M + NVIDIA RTX 5060 Laptop GPU
- Driver versions: AMD 32.0.32015.16001, NVIDIA 32.0.15.9649

Note: This issue affects multiple Flutter applications built with version 3.10.4, including Hiddify v5.5.5 and v5.9.6. Both versions crash at the identical offset 0xd23188 in flutter_windows.dll.


### Expected results

The Flutter Windows application should:

1. Launch successfully - The process should start and display the main window within 2-3 seconds.

2. Remain stable - The application should continue running without crashing, regardless of GPU acceleration status.

3. Handle graphics initialization gracefully - Whether using hardware acceleration (DirectX/ANGLE) or software rendering, the application should adapt to the system configuration.

4. Provide error feedback - If there are compatibility issues with the Windows version or graphics drivers, the application should display a meaningful error message rather than crashing with a low-level exception.

5. Work on latest Windows builds - Flutter applications should be compatible with Windows 11 build 26300 and other recent Windows updates.


### Actual results

The Flutter Windows application exhibits the following behavior:

1. Process starts but no window shown - The application process is visible in Task Manager (PID assigned, memory allocated approximately 50-60MB) but MainWindowHandle equals 0, indicating no window was created.

2. Deterministic crash after 7-8 seconds - The process consistently crashes approximately 7-8 seconds after launch, regardless of user interaction.

3. Stack buffer overrun exception - Windows Event Log records:

   Faulting application name: test_app.exe
   Faulting module name: flutter_windows.dll
   Exception code: 0xc0000409 (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN)
   Fault offset: 0x0000000000d23188

4. BEX64 error reporting - Windows Error Reporting generates fault bucket 1869551482875907604, type 5, Event Name: BEX64.

5. No recovery possible - The application cannot be restarted without repeating the crash. No safe mode or fallback mechanism is available.

6. Identical crash across versions - Both Hiddify v5.5.5 and v5.9.6 (both using Flutter 3.10.4) crash at the exact same offset 0xd23188, confirming this is a Flutter engine bug, not an application-specific issue.

Crash Analysis Summary:
- Exception Code: 0xc0000409
- Exception Type: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN
- Faulting Module: flutter_windows.dll (17.66 MB)
- Crash Offset: 0x0000000000d23188
- Time to Crash: 7-8 seconds
- Frequency: 100 percent (every launch)

title: [Linux] "Gdk-Message: Unable to load  from the cursor theme" is logged at startup
body:
## Environment
- Flutter 3.50.0 (stable) and master (e8ac49ab53c)
- Linux, GNOME on Wayland (also reproducible on X11), GTK 3.24.52
- Any cursor theme (Adwaita, Bibata, …)
- Any Flutter app, including a bare `flutter create app`

## Steps to reproduce
1. `flutter create cursor_warning && cd cursor_warning`
2. `flutter run -d linux`

## Actual result
On startup (and again after a hot restart) the console prints:
`Gdk-Message: 13:54:21.473: Unable to load  from the cursor theme`
Note the double space between load and from: the cursor name being loaded is the empty string.

## Expected result
No GTK/GDK warning is printed. The mouse cursor is the normal default arrow.

## Additional context
The warning is harmless (the cursor works and the app runs), but it is printed for every Flutter Linux app, on both Wayland and X11, with any cursor theme, which makes it look like a real problem and adds noise to logs and CI output. It is not related to the system cursor theme.

## Root cause
My AI agent found this as the root cause:

`FlMouseCursorHandler` is initialized with an empty cursor name:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/fl_mouse_cursor_handler.cc#L128-L130

```cpp
static void fl_mouse_cursor_handler_init(FlMouseCursorHandler* self) {
  self->cursor_name = g_strdup("");
}
```

When the view is realized, setup_cursor() immediately calls cursor_changed_cb(), which passes that name straight to GDK:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/fl_view.cc#L138-L147
```cpp
static void cursor_changed_cb(FlView* self) {
  FlMouseCursorHandler* handler =
      fl_engine_get_mouse_cursor_handler(self->engine);
  const gchar* cursor_name = fl_mouse_cursor_handler_get_cursor_name(handler);
  GdkWindow* window = ...;
  g_autoptr(GdkCursor) cursor =
      gdk_cursor_new_from_name(gdk_window_get_display(window), cursor_name);
  gdk_window_set_cursor(window, cursor);
}
```
`gdk_cursor_new_from_name()` cannot resolve "", so GTK logs the message above. The name only becomes valid after the framework sends the first `activateSystemCursor` call on the flutter/mousecursor channel (normally the first time the pointer enters a `MouseRegion`); at that point `activate_system_cursor()` maps the kind to a real GTK name, or falls back to `kFallbackCursor` ("default").

Since I don't fully understand it I will not open an AI generated PR to fix this, even if it looks like an easy fix

title: [Impeller][Android][Vulkan] Native crashes in `Canvas::AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass` (SIGSEGV) and `Canvas::GetLocalCoverageLimit` (SIGABRT) on Pixel 10 and Honor 400 Lite, Flutter 3.44.0
body:
## Summary

A published Android game (Flutter 3.44.0 stable, Impeller on Vulkan, no fragment shaders, a `CustomPainter` game board plus `flutter_svg` sprites) has 3 native crashes in 28 days in the raster thread, all inside `impeller::Canvas`. They come from Google Play Console / Android vitals (symbolized native traces), so I have no device in hand and **no reproduction**. I am filing it because the two crashing functions read the render pass texture without checking it, and the code is **unchanged in 3.47.9 and 3.50.0**, so upgrading is unlikely to fix it.

- 2 crashes: `SIGSEGV` in `impeller::Canvas::AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass(Entity&, bool)` (reached from `DrawImageRect` and from `drawText`).
- 1 crash: `SIGABRT` in `impeller::Canvas::GetLocalCoverageLimit() const`, through `FML_CHECK(back_texture)` (`fml::LogMessage::~LogMessage` → `fml::KillProcess` → `abort`).
- Crash rate is low (Play perceived crash rate 0.00 %, about 314 active devices over the period), but a hard abort on the raster thread kills the process.

## Devices

| Date | Device | Android | ABI | Signal | Top Flutter frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-06 | Honor 400 Lite (HNABR-M) | 16 (API 36) | arm64-v8a | SIGSEGV | `AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass` ← `DlDispatcherBase::drawText` |
| 2026-11-12 | Google Pixel 10 (frankel) | 17 (API 37) | arm64-v8a | SIGSEGV | `AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass` ← `Canvas::DrawImageRect` ← `DlDispatcherBase::drawImageRect` |
| 2026-11-13 | Google Pixel 10 (frankel) | 17 (API 37) | arm64-v8a | SIGABRT | `GetLocalCoverageLimit` ← `DlDispatcherBase::drawDisplayList` |

The two Pixel 10 crashes are probably the same user. The app is a regular `flutter build appbundle --release`; `libflutter.so` BuildId is `72cf23096728add25ac5f61592212d1e99c68a78` in all three (Flutter 3.44.0, engine revision `4c525dac5ebe5971c5708ef73558ed8edcf4a362`).

## Stack traces (symbolized by Play, truncated after the raster loop)

SIGABRT, Pixel 10:

```
#00 libc.so (abort+160)
#01 libflutter.so (fml::KillProcess()+15712256)
#02 libflutter.so (fml::LogMessage::~LogMessage()+15712256)
#03 libflutter.so (impeller::Canvas::GetLocalCoverageLimit() const+15712256)
#04 libflutter.so (impeller::DlDispatcherBase::drawDisplayList(sk_sp<flutter::DisplayList>, float)+15712256)
#05 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::DispatchOneOp(flutter::DlOpReceiver&, unsigned char const*) const+15712256)
#06 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::Dispatch(flutter::DlOpReceiver&) const+15712256)
#07 libflutter.so (impeller::RenderToTarget(impeller::ContentContext&, impeller::RenderTarget, sk_sp<flutter::DisplayList> const&, impeller::TRect<float>, bool, bool)+15712256)
#08 libflutter.so (flutter::GPUSurfaceVulkanImpeller::AcquireFrame(impeller::TSize<int> const&)::$_0 ...)
#09 libflutter.so (flutter::SurfaceFrame::Submit()+15712256)
#10 libflutter.so (flutter::Rasterizer::DrawToSurfacesUnsafe(...)+15712256)
#11 libflutter.so (flutter::Rasterizer::DrawToSurfaces(...)+15712256)
#12 libflutter.so (flutter::Rasterizer::Draw(...)::$_0 ...)
#13 libflutter.so (flutter::Rasterizer::Draw(std::shared_ptr<flutter::Pipeline<flutter::FrameItem>> const&)+15712256)
...
```

SIGSEGV, Pixel 10 (`drawImageRect`):

```
#00 libflutter.so (OUTLINED_FUNCTION_1079+15712256)
#01 libflutter.so (impeller::Canvas::AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass(impeller::Entity&, bool)+15712256)
#02 libflutter.so (impeller::Canvas::DrawImageRect(std::shared_ptr<impeller::Texture> const&, impeller::TRect<float>, impeller::TRect<float>, impeller::Paint const&, impeller::SamplerDescriptor ...)
#03 libflutter.so (impeller::DlDispatcherBase::drawImageRect(sk_sp<flutter::DlImage>, impeller::TRect<float> const&, impeller::TRect<float> const&, flutter::DlImageSampling, bool, ...)
#04 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::DispatchOneOp(flutter::DlOpReceiver&, unsigned char const*) const+15712256)
#05 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::Dispatch(flutter::DlOpReceiver&, impeller::TRect<float> const&) const+15712256)
#06 libflutter.so (impeller::DlDispatcherBase::drawDisplayList(sk_sp<flutter::DisplayList>, float)+15712256)
#07 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::DispatchOneOp(...))
#08 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::Dispatch(flutter::DlOpReceiver&) const+15712256)
#09 libflutter.so (impeller::RenderToTarget(...)+15712256)
#10 libflutter.so (flutter::GPUSurfaceVulkanImpeller::AcquireFrame(...)::$_0 ...)
#11 libflutter.so (flutter::SurfaceFrame::Submit()+15712256)
...
```

SIGSEGV, Honor 400 Lite (`drawText`):

```
#00 libflutter.so (OUTLINED_FUNCTION_1079+12435456)
#01 libflutter.so (impeller::Canvas::AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass(impeller::Entity&, bool)+12435456)
#02 libflutter.so (impeller::DlDispatcherBase::drawText(std::shared_ptr<flutter::DlText> const&, float, float)+12435456)
#03 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::Dispatch(flutter::DlOpReceiver&, impeller::TRect<float> const&) const+12435456)
#04 libflutter.so (impeller::DlDispatcherBase::drawDisplayList(sk_sp<flutter::DisplayList>, float)+12435456)
#05 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::DispatchOneOp(...))
#06 libflutter.so (flutter::DisplayList::Dispatch(flutter::DlOpReceiver&) const+12435456)
#07 libflutter.so (impeller::RenderToTarget(...)+12435456)
#08 libflutter.so (flutter::GPUSurfaceVulkanImpeller::AcquireFrame(...)::$_0 ...)
#09 libflutter.so (flutter::SurfaceFrame::Submit()+12435456)
...
```

(The `+offset` suffix is the same on every frame of one trace, so it looks like a symbolization artefact. `...` marks arguments I cut for width.)

All three traces share the same shape: `GPUSurfaceVulkanImpeller::AcquireFrame` → `RenderToTarget` → `DisplayList::Dispatch` → a **nested display list** (`DlDispatcherBase::drawDisplayList`) → the crashing `Canvas` call. The game draws its board with `CustomPainter` (`drawImageRect`, text) and some screens use `Opacity`, `ColorFiltered` / `ImageFilter` and `saveLayer`; I do not know which screen was showing at the time of each crash.

## What the source says

`engine/src/flutter/impeller/display_list/canvas.cc` (Flutter 3.44.0):

- `Canvas::GetLocalCoverageLimit()`: `std::shared_ptr<Texture> back_texture = back_render_pass.GetInlinePassContext()->GetTexture(); FML_CHECK(back_texture) << "Context is valid:" << ...IsValid();` → a null pass texture aborts the process, and the Play traces end in exactly this `LogMessage` destructor.
- `Canvas::AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass()`: in the `render_passes_.back().IsApplyingClearColor()` branch, `render_passes_.back().GetInlinePassContext()->GetTexture()->GetSize()` dereferences the same texture **without a null check**, which would be consistent with the SIGSEGV in an outlined function called directly from `AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass`.

My reading (not proven, no device): the render pass texture of the current pass is null, because the allocation of the offscreen / onscreen texture failed (memory pressure, driver or a lost context), and one call site checks it with `FML_CHECK` while the other one does not. I checked the two functions in the Flutter repository at the tags 3.44.0, 3.47.9 and 3.50.0: **both bodies are byte for byte identical** (same SHA-256 of the extracted function text, 36 and 97 lines). None of the 3.47 or 3.50 release notes mentions these signatures.

## Request

1. Does the team know of an Impeller / Vulkan path that leaves the `InlinePassContext` texture null on Pixel 10 (Android 17) or Honor 400 Lite (Android 16)?
2. Would a null check in `AddRenderEntityToCurrentPass` (return instead of dereference, like the `GetRenderPass()` failure a few lines below) and a graceful path instead of `FML_CHECK(back_texture)` in `GetLocalCoverageLimit` be acceptable? A skipped draw or a dropped frame is much better than killing the app.

## Steps to reproduce

None: I only have the Play Console native crash reports. The same game on an emulator (software Vulkan) does not crash. I can test a build on a real Pixel-class phone through Play's internal test track, or try an engine build or a diagnostic flag if someone points me to one.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.44.0 stable, Dart 3.12.0, engine revision `4c525dac5ebe5971c5708ef73558ed8edcf4a362`.
- Android, Impeller (Vulkan, the default), release build, arm64-v8a.
- Pixel 10 on Android 17 (API 37); Honor 400 Lite on Android 16 (API 36).

title: Docs for embedder keyboard implementation are insufficient
body:
This is something of a follow-up to https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/132433. I'm working on an embedder and spent a long time figuring out how to implement keyboard events correctly. I see that some docs were added to KeyEventManager to explain that a raw key message must be sent in addition to calling FlutterEngineSendKeyEvent, but there's no link to this from the embedder docs so looking at the API one would be led to believe calling FlutterEngineSendKeyEvent is sufficient.

1. Could the embedder docs be updated to at least link to KeyEventManager to avoid being misleading?
2. What's the plan for removing `flutter/keyevent`? The raw keyboard API has been deprecated for a long time, and removing it would help to simplify embedder implementation. Is there anything an external contributor can help with?

title: [web] A small looping animation costs more CPU and GPU the more static content is on screen, even behind a RepaintBoundary
Several render objects return true from `paintsChild` for children they don't paint
body:
### Steps to reproduce 1. `flutter create bug` 2. Replace `bug/test/widget_test.dart` with the code sample below. 3. `cd bug` and `flutter test` The `Offstage` test passes; the other tests fail. ### Expected results A parent that does not paint a child returns false from `paintsChild`, as [`RenderOffstage`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/proxy_box.dart#L3869-L3873) does: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/object.dart#L3639-L3665 ### Actual results The following render objects skip painting a child in `paint` but return true from `paintsChild` for it, so code that relies on `paintsChild` treats the child as painted, e.g. [`InkFeature`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/cbf06504c85aebf333d3c80c9b8ee52c859456bc/packages/material_ui/lib/src/material.dart#L714-L745) in `material_ui` keeps painting the ink splash of an `InkWell` that its parent no longer paints. Results on Flutter 3.50.0: | Widget | Render object | Expected `paintsChild` | Actual `paintsChild` | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Offstage` (reference) | `RenderOffstage` | `false` | `false` | Correct | | `IndexedStack` | [`RenderIndexedStack`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/stack.dart#L864-L871) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.
The child is not at `index` and is not painted, but `paintsChild` returns true. | | `Visibility.maintain` | [`_RenderVisibility`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/indexed_stack.dart#L811-L816) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.
`visible` is false and the child is not painted, but `paintsChild` returns true. | | `Flow` | [`RenderFlow`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/flow.dart#L390-L399) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.

The sliver is below the viewport and is not painted, but `paintsChild` returns true. | | `SliverMainAxisGroup` | [`RenderSliverMainAxisGroup`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/sliver_group.dart#L441-L451) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.
The child sliver is below the viewport and is not painted, but `paintsChild` returns true. | | `ListView` | [`RenderSliverMultiBoxAdaptor`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/sliver_multi_box_adaptor.dart#L737-L742) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.
The child is in the cache extent below the viewport and is not painted, but `paintsChild` returns true. | | `SliverVisibility.maintain` | [`_RenderSliverVisibility`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/indexed_stack.dart#L875-L881) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.
`visible` is false and the child is not painted, but `paintsChild` returns true. | | `TwoDimensionalViewport` | [`RenderTwoDimensionalViewport`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/two_dimensional_viewport.dart#L1659-L1668) | `false` | `true` | Wrong.

child = parent; } expect( painted, isFalse, reason: 'A parent that does not paint the child should return false ' 'from paintsChild.', ); }); } } class _Child extends StatelessWidget { const _Child(); title: Several clipping render objects don't implement `describeApproximatePaintClip`
[Flutter GPU] Expose the maximum render target size on GpuContext
body:
### Use case

An app using Flutter GPU that renders into large textures, such as an atlas, can't find out how large a render target the device supports. OpenGL ES only guarantees 2048, while most GPUs support 8192 or more, so today the app either hard-codes a conservative size or creates a texture and finds out by failing, which on some drivers isn't reported cleanly.

Impeller already knows this limit (`Capabilities::GetMaximumRenderPassAttachmentSize()`), but `GpuContext` doesn't expose it.

### Proposal

Add `GpuContext.maxRenderTargetWidth` and `GpuContext.maxRenderTargetHeight`, reporting that capability:

- Vulkan: `maxFramebufferWidth` and `maxFramebufferHeight`.
- OpenGL ES: `GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`.
- Metal: the feature set table's maximum texture size.

```dart
final context = gpu.gpuContext;
final size = min(desiredSize, min(context.maxRenderTargetWidth, context.maxRenderTargetHeight));
```

This needs to be in the engine, since a package can't query the backend's limits.

### Steps to reproduce 1. `flutter create bug` 2. Replace `bug/test/widget_test.dart` with the code sample below. 3. `cd bug` and `flutter test` The test without padding passes; the test with a top padding of 100 fails. ### Expected results The padding does not change the cache area of the list. Once the padding is scrolled past by more than the cache extent, the child's `cacheOrigin` is the same as the viewport's, -250, since `cacheOrigin` is only clamped so that the sliver is not asked for content before its zero scroll offset: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/sliver.dart#L399-L415 ### Actual results [`RenderSliverEdgeInsetsPadding`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/sliver_padding.dart#L133-L141) computes the child's `cacheOrigin` as `min(0, cacheOrigin + beforePadding)` instead of clamping it with `max(cacheOrigin, -scrollOffset)` as [the viewport](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/viewport.dart#L806-L811) does, so once the scroll offset exceeds the cache extent, the child's cache area moves forward by up to `beforePadding`. title: [video_player] Expose the stream's wall-clock time (HLS EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME) and allow seeking by date
[iOS 27] `flutter run` debug hangs at LLDB: JIT breakpoint never resolves ("debugger assist: not detected"), fresh app, Flutter 3.47.9 / Xcode 27.2
body:
### Summary

- `flutter run` (debug, LLDB debugging enabled — the default) **never finishes attaching** on physical iOS 27 devices. It prints `LLDB is taking longer than expected to start debugging the app` and waits forever; the Dart VM Service is never reported, so DevTools / hot reload / tooling cannot connect.
- The JIT breakpoint `NOTIFY_DEBUGGER_ABOUT_RX_PAGES` is set (pending) but **never resolves** (`location added to breakpoint` is never printed). Right after `process continue`, the app logs `Failed to execute code (error: EXC_BAD_ACCESS, debugger assist: not detected)` followed by `Dart execution mode: simulator`, and keeps running in that mode.
- `flutter_tools` is waiting in `_resumeProcess` for `location added to breakpoint`, which never arrives.
- Reproduces with a **fresh `flutter create` app**, on **two different devices** (iOS 27.0.1 and 27.2.1), with **Xcode 26.2 and Xcode 27.2**, on **Flutter 3.44.1 and 3.47.9** (3.47.9 includes #191434 "On iOS 27+ devices, manually process lldb stops"; the log shows the manual-continue path is used — the breakpoint is set without `--auto-continue` and no stop hooks are added).

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS 26.6.2 with Xcode 27.2, Flutter 3.47.9 (stable).
2. `flutter create --platforms ios lldbcheck` (only change: set a development team / bundle id so it can be signed).
3. Connect an iPhone running iOS 27.x by USB (Developer Mode enabled, paired, DDI mounted).
4. `flutter run -v -d <device>`

### Expected results

The app starts, the JIT breakpoint resolves, and `A Dart VM Service on <device> is available at ...` is printed.

### Actual results

- `devicectl device process launch --start-stopped` succeeds, LLDB attaches (`Process N stopped ... SIGSTOP at dyld\`_dyld_start`), `process continue` is sent.
- The breakpoint stays `no locations (pending)`. ~16 s later the app logs `Failed to execute code (error: EXC_BAD_ACCESS, debugger assist: not detected)` and `Dart execution mode: simulator`.
- After 1 minute `LLDB is taking longer than expected...` is printed and the tool never proceeds. The VM Service is never discovered.

### What we tried (all reproduce the hang)

| Variable | Values tried | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Flutter | 3.44.1, 3.47.9 | hang (3.47.9 takes the iOS 27 manual-continue path) |
| Xcode | 26.2 (17C52, LLDB 1703.0.236.21), 27.2 (27B52, LLDB 2103.0.34.407) | hang |
| Device | iPhone 14 (iPhone14,7) iOS 27.0.1 (24A446); iPhone 14 Pro (iPhone15,2) iOS 27.2.1 (24B156) | hang |
| App | large production app; fresh `flutter create` app | hang |
| Connection | USB only; USB + same Wi-Fi as the Mac | hang |
| Device Support symbols | present (`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/iOS DeviceSupport/<model> <version>/…/Symbols`, 6+ GB each), and LLDB receives the right sysroot — so this is not #189284 | hang |

Other observations:

title: Feature Request: Interactive Android Emulator Launch in flutter run
body:
Problem

Currently, when no Android emulator is running, developers typically need to launch one separately before running their Flutter application.

Flutter already provides emulator management commands, but the workflow could be more convenient directly inside "flutter run".

This introduces unnecessary friction, particularly for developers who frequently switch between projects or work primarily from the terminal.

Proposed Solution

Introduce an optional interactive keyboard shortcut ("a") in "flutter run" that allows developers to launch an available Android emulator without leaving the CLI.

Expected behavior:

1. Run "flutter run".
2. If no suitable device is connected, display an option to launch an available Android emulator.
3. Press "a" to launch it.
4. If multiple emulators are available, allow the developer to select one.
5. Wait for the emulator to become ready.
6. Automatically deploy and launch the Flutter application.

Benefits

- Reduces manual setup steps.
- Improves the terminal-based development experience.
- Makes Flutter more approachable for new developers.
- Reuses Flutter's existing emulator discovery and launch infrastructure.
- Provides a convenient workflow similar to other mobile development CLIs.

Compatibility Considerations

- Preserve existing "flutter run" behavior for connected devices.
- Avoid conflicts with existing keyboard shortcuts.
- Support non-interactive environments without blocking execution.
- Provide useful error messages if no emulator is installed or launching fails.
- Initially target Android; other platforms can be considered separately.

Willingness to Contribute

I'm interested in contributing an implementation and tests if this enhancement aligns with Flutter's CLI design goals.

I'd appreciate feedback from the maintainers on the proposed interaction and whether this feature would be suitable for the Flutter tool.

[iOS] VoiceOver focuses nodes with AccessibilityFocusBlockType.blockNode
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample on iOS with VoiceOver on.
2. Swipe right.

### Expected results

VoiceOver stops once, on the button. The inner node has `AccessibilityFocusBlockType.blockNode` so it should be skipped. Android does this: the inner node is not focusable.

### Actual results

VoiceOver stops twice: on the button, then on the inner "Temp" node.

`isAccessibilityElement` in `SemanticsObject.mm` returns true for any node with a label, value or hint and does not check `isAccessibilityFocusBlocked`. The flag is only checked in `accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction`. On Android, `AccessibilityBridge.isFocusable()` checks it.

I checked this on the iOS 26.1 simulator by listing the app's accessibility elements: the inner node has `isAccessibilityElement == YES`. On an Android 12 emulator, the same node has `focusable=false`.

### Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(body: Center(child: Tile()))));

class Tile extends StatelessWidget {
  const Tile({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Semantics(
      button: true,
      label: 'Temp',
      onTap: () {},
      child: Semantics(
        identifier: 'tile.title',
        container: true,
        label: 'Temp',
        accessibilityFocusBlockType: AccessibilityFocusBlockType.blockNode,
        child: const ExcludeSemantics(child: Text('Temp')),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Why it matters

We give the title node its text so Android UI tests (UIAutomator, Appium) can check it and block screen reader focus on it because the button already reads the same name. On iOS, VoiceOver reads the name twice.

title: api.flutter.dev omits <link rel="canonical">, overriding api.dart.dev
body:
Pages on `https://api.flutter.dev` are generated without `<link rel="canonical">` tags ([`dev/tools/create_api_docs.dart#L688-L691`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/7728fa1a03ac89b7af1c66bbbb674a6e7b89ee73/dev/tools/create_api_docs.dart#L688-L691)), causing Google Search Console (`sc-domain:dart.dev`) to report `Duplicate, Google chose different canonical than user` where `https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-*` overrides `https://api.dart.dev/dart-*` for core Dart SDK libraries.

In addition, [`dev/docs/analytics-footer.html#L1`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/7728fa1a03ac89b7af1c66bbbb674a6e7b89ee73/dev/docs/analytics-footer.html#L1) loads `cookienotificationbar.min.js` synchronously without `defer`, blocking HTML parsing at the end of every generated API page.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sh
# Exits 1 (no <link rel="canonical"> emitted on Flutter or mirrored Dart SDK pages):
curl -sL https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/Widget-class.html | grep 'rel="canonical"'
curl -sL https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-core/String-class.html | grep 'rel="canonical"'
```

### Proposed Fix

- Pass `--rel-canonical-prefix=https://api.flutter.dev/flutter` to `dartdoc` in `dev/tools/create_api_docs.dart`.
- Post-process `publishRoot`:
  - Rewrite root `index.html` canonical from `https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/` (which meta-refreshes back to `../index.html`) to `https://api.flutter.dev/`.
  - Strip `<link rel="canonical">` from `flutter/search.html` and `flutter/__404error.html`.
  - Rewrite `<link rel="canonical">` on mirrored non-UI `flutter/dart-*/**` pages and `flutter/dart-*-library.html` redirect stubs (excluding `dart-ui` and `dart-ui_web`) to `https://api.dart.dev/...`.
- Add `defer` to `cookienotificationbar.min.js` in `dev/docs/analytics-footer.html`.
