title: [image_picker] Let apps request location metadata from the Android photo picker
body:
### Use case

Some apps pre-fill a location from a photo's EXIF GPS. A post or report composer, for example, might suggest where an attached photo was taken. On Android 16+ these apps can't get that metadata for photos picked from the gallery with `image_picker`.

From API 36, `image_picker_android` always uses the system photo picker: `ImagePickerUtils.effectiveUsePhotoPicker` returns `true` for SDK >= 36, whatever `useAndroidPhotoPicker` says. The photo picker redacts location metadata by default, and `ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION` doesn't change that on this path. The picked file still has its GPS tags, but the values come back zeroed.

Android now has an opt-in for this. `MediaStore.EXTRA_REQUEST_LOCATION_METADATA_ACCESS` is documented as "an optional intent-extra used to allow apps to request access to the location metadata of the media items selected by the user and returned by `ACTION_PICK_IMAGES`". AndroidX exposes it as `PickVisualMediaRequest.Builder.setLocationMetadataAccessRequested(Boolean)` in `androidx.photopicker:photopicker-activity`. It is available from SDK extension 23 on Android 13+ and ignored where unsupported. The picker may ask the user, and the user's choice is final.

`image_picker` has no way to set this, so on Android 16+ an app has no way at all to get the location of a gallery photo.

Checked against `image_picker` 1.2.3 and `image_picker_android` 0.8.13+25.

Related: #74615 (EXIF missing from Google Photos picks), and #117053 (GPS missing through the photo picker on Android 13, closed as a duplicate of #74615).

- https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/MediaStore#EXTRA_REQUEST_LOCATION_METADATA_ACCESS
- https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/androidx/photopicker/activity/PickVisualMediaRequest.Builder

### Proposal

Add an Android-only opt-in that requests location metadata access whenever the plugin launches the photo picker. It could be a property on `ImagePickerAndroid` next to `useAndroidPhotoPicker`, or a field on the Android picker options.

- Photo picker path (`PickVisualMedia` / `PickMultipleVisualMedia`): request location metadata access, either through `androidx.photopicker`'s `setLocationMetadataAccessRequested(true)` or by adding the extra to the intent the contract creates.
- `ACTION_GET_CONTENT` path (below API 36 without `useAndroidPhotoPicker`): unchanged.

It would be off by default, so existing apps see no change. `ExifDataCopier` already copies the GPS tags into resized images. So once the source file is no longer redacted, the location reaches the app even when `maxWidth`, `maxHeight` or `imageQuality` is set.

title: web2app
Native crash in vendor GLES driver (libGLESv2_mtk.so) through hwui SkiaOpenGLPipeline on a PowerVR GE8320 device (Android 9 / API 28, Skia path)
body:
## Summary

A Play Console native crash report shows the crash happens entirely inside the
vendor MediaTek GLES driver while android's hwui clears a frame — not in Dart,
not in Flutter's renderer, and not in app code. This looks like the known
PowerVR GE8320 driver bug class, hit through Flutter's Skia GL path on API 28
(Impeller's default-on threshold is API 29, so this device stays on Skia).

## Crash report

- Device: Infinix HOT 8 (MediaTek Helio P22, PowerVR GE8320)
- OS: Android 9 (SDK 28)
- Flutter: 3.47.5, release build (R8), arm64
- Occurred: 2 days ago

backtrace:
#00 pc 0x00000000000ba238 /vendor/lib64/egl/libGLESv2_mtk.so
#01 pc 0x00000000000ba3c0 /vendor/lib64/egl/libGLESv2_mtk.so
#02 pc 0x00000000000a73f0 /vendor/lib64/egl/libGLESv2_mtk.so (glUniform4f+128)
#03 pc 0x00000000003fb504 /system/lib64/libhwui.so (GrGLGpu::clearColorAsDraw(...)+460)
#04 pc 0x000000000065d818 /system/lib64/libhwui.so (GrGLGpu::clear(...)+456)
#05 pc 0x000000000065ffd8 /system/lib64/libhwui.so (GrGLGpuRTCommandBuffer::begin()+56)
...
#11 pc 0x00000000001ef954 /system/lib64/libhwui.so (SkiaOpenGLPipeline::draw(...))
#12 pc 0x00000000005d6050 /system/lib64/libhwui.so (CanvasContext::draw()+276)


## Analysis

- Every native frame is in `/vendor/lib64/egl/libGLESv2_mtk.so` or hwui's
  SkiaOpenGLPipeline — the abort originates in the closed-source vendor driver
  during a clear/draw, which no app-side change can patch.
- API 28 < 29, so the device does not get the Impeller default and renders via
  Skia GL, which is the path that trips this driver.
- This matches the known GE8320 driver bug class:
  - https://forums.imgtec.com/t/powervr-ge8320-driver-bug-crash/3831
  - https://discussions.unity.com/t/there-is-a-bug-and-the-crash-in-libglesv2_mtk-so-on-some-devices/877000
  - https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/166248
- Possibly related to the MediaTek fallback work in #193428.

## Ask

Is there any recommended mitigation for Flutter apps on API 28 MediaTek/PowerVR
devices hitting vendor GLES crashes (e.g., forcing a different backend, or is
"known vendor bug, low volume" the expected outcome)? Happy to provide more
samples if useful.

title: [Linux] View disposal clears renderer mutex during composition
body:
Closing a Linux release application can abort when GTK disposes its renderer during an in-flight raster composition.

Observed on Ubuntu 24.04 / x64 with Flutter 3.50.0 (`ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb`, engine `371f77202a73e8dff57a8b3bff75bca55c090aee`).

**Expected:** closing the window keeps composition resources alive until the raster callback releases them.

**Actual:** renderer disposal reaches `g_mutex_clear` while composition still holds the mutex. The process aborts with exit 134:

```text
g_mutex_clear() called on uninitialised or locked mutex
```

GTK can force disposal even while the raster callback holds a strong reference to the view. That reference does not protect the renderer's mutex from disposal. This is a lifetime follow-up to #188659 / #188702.

### Deterministic engine reproduction

[Draft PR #196680](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196680) contains a regression that pauses real OpenGL composition while the main thread destroys the renderer. It uses mocked GL operations and does not require a hardware GPU.

1. Set up a disposable Linux engine checkout at framework revision `ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb`, with engine build dependencies, Xvfb and a working session D-Bus.
2. From PR head `1b5ebe9357bdd0d22d4e7b31592669bc5f6f39f8`, copy only `fl_view_renderer_lifetime_test.cc` and the changes to `testing/mock_gtk.cc` and `testing/mock_gtk.h` into `engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/`. Add `"fl_view_renderer_lifetime_test.cc",` to the test sources in that directory's `BUILD.gn`. Leave the production files unpatched.
3. From `engine/src`, build and run:

```sh
./flutter/tools/gn --runtime-mode=release --unoptimized --no-stripped \
  --enable-unittests --no-lto --no-build-embedder-examples
ninja -C out/host_release_unopt flutter_linux_unittests
cd out/host_release_unopt
xvfb-run -a dbus-run-session -- ./flutter_linux_unittests \
  --gtest_filter=FlViewRendererLifetimeTest.OpenGLDisposeDuringComposite
```

The unpatched-runtime test reproduced the locked-mutex abort (exit 134). With the candidate production changes, all seven renderer lifetime cases and the repeated-engine-disposal case passed (8/8) at that SDK revision. The view-ownership test also covers the reference retained by the production callback.

The relevant source remains affected at upstream `master` revision `a8a9f341b004c0378355b911622cb78a6821199c`. PR #196680 now also queues compositor callback references for GTK-main release. Local Linux arm64 validation at `44516bf689c`: 70 selected Linux tests pass, and 15 real Wayland cases pass twice with no skips. Published callback code fails both added finalization controls; an upstream subsurface-renderer rollback reproduces exit 134 under real Wayland. The PR documents setup and remaining limits, including native-engine/app shutdown, sanitizer coverage, and a preexisting same-size remap gap.

[packages] ☂️ Adopt extensible enums in federated plugins
body:
### Background

Following the acceptance of **RFC 4400000: Extensible enums in federated plugins** (https://github.com/flutter/rfc/pull/44; design doc: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189696), this umbrella issue tracks the migration of eligible closed `enum` types in `flutter/packages` to the extensible constant pattern.

Currently, closed Dart `enum` types in `*_platform_interface` packages prevent platform implementations from introducing platform-specific values without forcing major version bumps or breaking exhaustive `switch` statements in downstream code.

### Target Pattern & Migration Guidelines

Each migrated type should follow the canonical pattern defined in the RFC:
- **`final class` wrapper** around a `final String name` identifier, with a private `._(this.name)` constructor for core constants and a public `.fromString(this.name)` constructor for platform/custom constants.
- **Value equality & debugging:** `operator ==` and `hashCode` based on `name` (with `identical` fast-path), plus `toString()` returning `TypeName.$name`.
- **Discovery via `knownValues`:** Expose `static const List<...> knownValues` (never `values`, to avoid implying exhaustiveness).
- **Non-breaking `switch` handling:** Update downstream `switch` statements/expressions to include a `_ =>` / `default:` fallback.
- **Platform-specific constants:** Expose platform-only values via `extension` on the core type in the corresponding platform package (e.g., `extension WebImageFormats on ImageFormatGroup`).

### Rollout Order (Federated Plugins)

1. **Prep PRs (when needed):** Remove any downstream usage of `.values` in tests/code so `*_platform_interface` changes don't break CI.
2. **Platform interface (`*_platform_interface`):** Migrate the type(s), update tests, bump version (major if breaking, e.g., removing `.values` or changing `.name()` to `.name`), and publish.
3. **Platform implementations & app-facing package:** Update `pubspec.yaml` constraints to the new platform interface version, add platform-specific extensions where applicable, and update docs/tests.

---

### Tracking Checklist

#### `camera` (`ImageFormatGroup`)
- [ ] `[camera_android_camerax]` Remove `ImageFormatGroup.values` usage in tests (prep)
- [ ] `[camera_platform_interface]` Migrate `ImageFormatGroup` to extensible constant class
- [ ] `[camera_android]` Update for extensible `ImageFormatGroup`
- [ ] `[camera_android_camerax]` Update for extensible `ImageFormatGroup`
- [ ] `[camera_avfoundation]` Update for extensible `ImageFormatGroup`
- [ ] `[camera_web]` Update for extensible `ImageFormatGroup` (and expose `rgba8888`)
- [ ] `[camera_windows]` Update for extensible `ImageFormatGroup`
- [ ] `[camera]` Update `camera_platform_interface` constraint, docs, and tests

*(Additional plugins and enums will be added here as they are scoped.)*

title: iOS: checked semantics nodes are presented as UISwitch, and the switch value is read before the activation's semantics update
body:
Flutter 3.44.9 stable, iPhone 14.

**1. A node with `checked:` is always a switch on iOS.** `accessibility_bridge.mm` `CreateObject` returns `FlutterSwitchSemanticsObject` for any node whose toggled or checked state is set (outside a mutually exclusive group). Its `accessibilityValue` returns the native `UISwitch`'s "on"/"off" and ignores the node's `value`. A checkbox-style row with a custom label, value and an assertive `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement` ("Step 2 done") is spoken by VoiceOver as "switch button, off", and on double-tap VoiceOver says "on" over the announcement. Expected: a checked-state node is presented as a checkbox-like element (button trait plus a checked value), not a switch, or the node's own `value` is honoured.

**2. A switch whose value changes after an async step is read stale.** A `Switch` whose `value` is only updated once a Future completes (a network save) is read by VoiceOver immediately after the double-tap. `FlutterSwitchSemanticsObject.accessibilityValue` computes the state from the node at that moment, so VoiceOver speaks the old state, the opposite of what the switch shows a moment later. TalkBack on Android waits for the state-change event and is correct. Expected: VoiceOver announces the settled value, as a native `UISwitch` does when its own value changes.

**Repro:** a `Semantics(container: true, excludeSemantics: true, checked: done, onTap: …, label: 'Step 2. Chop the onion')` row; and a `SwitchListTile` whose `value` comes from a provider refreshed after `await Future.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 500))`. Run on an iOS device with VoiceOver and double-tap each.

title: [Android] Any non-IOException thrown while decoding an image aborts the process (FML_CHECK in android_image_generator.cc)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Boot an Android 16 (API 36) emulator. `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT` must be exactly 36 for `ImageDecoderHeifApi36Impl` to be used.
2. Take any HEIC photo that carries a rotation, such as a portrait iPhone photo (`exiftool` shows `Rotation: Rotate 90 CW`). Zero the payload of its `mdat` box with the script below, keeping the `ftyp` and `meta` boxes intact. The header still parses as `image/heif` with a rotation, but neither `ImageDecoder` nor `BitmapFactory` can decode the pixels.
   ```python
   # zero_mdat.py <in.heic> <out.heic>
   import struct, sys
   d = bytearray(open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read())
   pos = 0
   while pos < len(d):
       size, typ = struct.unpack('>I4s', d[pos:pos + 8]); hdr = 8
       if size == 1: size = struct.unpack('>Q', d[pos + 8:pos + 16])[0]; hdr = 16
       if size == 0: size = len(d) - pos
       if typ == b'mdat': d[pos + hdr:pos + size] = b'\0' * (size - hdr)
       pos += size
   open(sys.argv[2], 'wb').write(d)
   ```
3. Run `flutter create bug`, put the result at `assets/corrupt_rotated.heic`, declare it under `flutter: assets:` in `pubspec.yaml`, and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below.
4. Run `flutter run --release` on the emulator.

### Expected results

The decode failure reaches Dart as an image error: `errorBuilder` is called and the app shows `DECODE_ERROR`. This is the same outcome as when `ImageDecoderDefaultImpl` catches an `IOException` and returns `null`. The process keeps running.

### Actual results

The process aborts with `[FATAL:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_image_generator.cc(113)] Check failed: fml::jni::CheckException(env).` and SIGABRT on the `io` thread (logs below). Dart code can't catch it.

**Cause.** `AndroidImageGenerator::DoDecodeImage` calls `FlutterJNI.decodeImage` and then [`FML_CHECK(fml::jni::CheckException(env))`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/android_image_generator.cc#L113). Any Java throwable that escapes `decodeImage` therefore kills the process. On the Java side, only `IOException` is handled:

- [`ImageDecoderDefaultImpl.decodeImage`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/image/ImageDecoderDefaultImpl.java#L60) catches `IOException` only. `OutOfMemoryError` from the full-size software decode, or any `RuntimeException` from `ImageDecoder`, escapes.
- [`ExifMetadataReader.read`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/image/ExifMetadataReader.java#L37) also catches `IOException` only, while `ExifInterface` can throw runtime exceptions on malformed EXIF.
- [`Metadata.create`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/image/Metadata.java#L35) copies the whole encoded buffer into a Java `byte[]` for every image that reaches this path, which can throw `OutOfMemoryError`.
- On API 36, [`ImageDecoderHeifApi36Impl.decodeImageFallback`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/image/ImageDecoderHeifApi36Impl.java#L50-L55) dereferences the result of `BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray` without a null check when the image has a rotation. That is the `NullPointerException` in this repro.

**Scope.** In production we see this abort on Android 11 through 17, not only on API 36. The API 36 null dereference is just the case that reproduces on demand. The tombstone loses the Java exception type, because `CheckException` clears and logs it before aborting, so the other causes can't be told apart from crash reports. The relevant code is unchanged on `master` as of 3.50.0. #177942 / #177944 fixed one instance of this abort path (an NPE in `Metadata.isHeif` for SVG input) with a single null check, but nothing guards the path as a whole.

**Suggested fix:**
- Catch `Throwable` in `FlutterJNI.decodeImage` (or in `FlutterImageDecoder.decodeImage`), log it, and return `null`. Native code already treats `null` as a failed decode, so `IsValidImageData` or `GetPixels` returns false.
- Null-check the `BitmapFactory` result in `ImageDecoderHeifApi36Impl.decodeImageFallback`.
- Optionally, in `DoDecodeImage`, clear a pending exception and treat it as a decode failure instead of `FML_CHECK`ing.

As a workaround, we rewrite `FlutterJNI.decodeImage` at build time with an AGP ASM transform that wraps it in `catch (Throwable)` and returns `null`. With that in place, the same file shows `DECODE_ERROR` and the app keeps running, but the workaround is fragile across engine upgrades.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Repro()));

class Repro extends StatelessWidget {
  const Repro({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: Image.asset(
            'assets/corrupt_rotated.heic',
            errorBuilder: (context, error, stack) => const Text('DECODE_ERROR'),
          ),
        ),
      );
}
```

```yaml
# pubspec.yaml (added)
flutter:
  assets:
    - assets/corrupt_rotated.heic
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

No visual output: the process aborts before the first frame with the image, so nothing is shown. See the logs.

</details>

title: [camera] Support gain map (HDR) photos
body:
### Use case

HDR displays can show photo highlights brighter than SDR white. The system camera apps on many Android devices save such photos as Ultra HDR JPEGs (an SDR JPEG plus a gain map), and iOS saves photos with a gain map as well. These files still look correct on SDR displays and in apps that ignore the gain map.

The `camera` plugin always saves a plain SDR JPEG, so apps built with it cannot take photos that look as bright on HDR displays as the system camera's.

### Proposal

Add an opt-in for gain map photos, shaped like the zero-shutter-lag API:

- `CameraPlatform.isGainMapPhotoSupported(cameraId)` (default `false`)
- `CameraPlatform.setGainMapPhotoEnabled(cameraId, enabled)` (default throws `UnimplementedError`)
- the same two methods on `CameraController`

On Android, `camera_android_camerax` can implement it with CameraX `ImageCapture.OUTPUT_FORMAT_JPEG_ULTRA_HDR`, which cameras report through `ImageCapture.getImageCaptureCapabilities(cameraInfo).getSupportedOutputFormats()`. Other implementations keep returning `false` until they support it.

title: [Impeller] Support multi-surface frames in GPUTracerVK
body:
When Android renders platform views using Hybrid Composition or HCPP, the root Flutter surface and any overlay surfaces share a single GPU context and tracer. The Vulkan GPU tracer assumes only one frame can be active at a time, so acquiring and presenting multiple surfaces within a single Flutter frame corrupts the traced frame boundaries.

Under HCPP, the overlay surface starts and finishes its traced frame before the root surface finishes encoding and submitting its work, which triggers a debug assertion on overlapping frame starts and drops the root surface's GPU work from the trace. Under Hybrid Composition, each overlay surface emits its own GPU frame time event that dilutes the reported average, and frames that acquire an overlay surface without submitting it leave the tracer stuck mid-frame and hit the debug assertion on the next frame.

Specifically, `AndroidSurfaceVKImpeller` shares a single `ContextVK` and `GPUTracerVK` across surfaces, and `GPUTracerVK` gates frame tracking with a single `in_frame_` boolean toggled by `MarkFrameStart` and `MarkFrameEnd`. In https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196822, GPU frame time metrics were disabled for the affected HCPP and Hybrid Composition benchmarks (`createAndroidHCPPScrollPerfTest` and `createAndroidViewScrollPerfTest` in `dev/devicelab/lib/tasks/perf_tests.dart`). Once `GPUTracerVK` supports multi-surface frames, re-enabling those metrics is in scope for this issue.

Related:
- https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/196096
- https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196339
- https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196822

title: `systemFontsDidChange` callbacks should not have a one-frame delay
body:
After https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/117123, the framework only sends `systemFontsDidChange` to listeners during the next animation phase under the assumption that embedders only send system font update notifications to the framework during `.idle` phase. 

In https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/184332, the assert was removed because the web engine sends system font update notifications in a microtask, but it didn't change the implementation.

### Expected behavior
`systemFontsDidChange` gets dispatched to listeners as soon as the framework gets out of the `.idle` phase (during this phase layout artifacts should not be invalidated). If the embedder sends a system font update notification during the mid frame microtask phase, `systemFontsDidChange` should be dispatched without delay. 

### Actual behavior
The notification will be delayed until the next animation phase, which is unnecessary and the behavior is less predictable. RenderObjects could have picked up new system fonts as soon as they are allowed to update themselves.

`flutter test` with several integration test files on a physical iOS device (Xcode 26): every launch after the first hangs — "The Dart VM Service     was not discovered", because the CoreDevice log forwarders are closed after the first launch
body:
### Steps to reproduce

 1. `flutter create repro && cd repro`, add `integration_test` as a dev dependency.
 2.  Create two trivial files, `integration_test/a_test.dart` and `integration_test/b_test.dart`, each:
   ```dart
   import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
   import 'package:integration_test/integration_test.dart';
   void main() {
     IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
     testWidgets('ok', (t) async => expect(1, 1));
   }   
   ```
3. With Xcode 26 and a USB-connected iPhone (CoreDevice), run:
   `flutter test integration_test/a_test.dart integration_test/b_test.dart -d <iphone-udid>`


### Expected results

Both files run; `+2: All tests passed!`.

### Actual results

### Actual results

The first file passes. For the second, the app is built, installed, launched and attached by lldb, and the Dart VM starts (`Dart execution mode: JIT`), but then:

```
The Dart VM Service was not discovered after 60 seconds. This is taking much longer than expected...
```

and the tool waits indefinitely. When the process is interrupted, it prints `All tests passed!` with the first file's count only (`+1`), then `test package returned with exit code 1` — so a CI job that greps for "All tests passed" reports green while the second file never ran.

Each file run alone in its own `flutter test` invocation passes. An Android device runs both files in one invocation without trouble.

### Cause (from reading flutter_tools at 3.47.7 and current master)

- With Xcode ≥ 26, iOS CoreDevice logs come from `devicectl` + `lldb` (`ios/devices.dart`, `IOSDeviceLogReader.logSources`, primary source `devicectlAndLldb`). The VM Service URL is found by `ProtocolDiscovery` from these logs (`protocol_discovery.dart`, "VM Service URL on device"); in our runs the mDNS path contributed nothing.
- `IOSDevice` holds one `IOSCoreDeviceLauncher` for its lifetime (`final IOSCoreDeviceLauncher _coreDeviceLauncher`), and the launcher holds one `coreDeviceLogForwarder` and one `lldbLogForwarder`, both `final`, created once (`ios/core_devices.dart`).
- After the first test file, `IntegrationTestTestDevice.kill()` calls `device.dispose()` → each `IOSDeviceLogReader.dispose()` → `CoreDeviceLoggingSource.dispose()` → `lldbLogForwarder.exit()` and `coreDeviceLogForwarder.exit()`.
- `exit()` closes the forwarder's broadcast `StreamController` (`IOSCoreDeviceLogForwarder.exit()` in core_devices.dart; `LLDBLogForwarder.exit()` in lldb.dart). The controller is `final` and never recreated; `addLog` drops lines once it is closed.
- The second launch reuses the same launcher, so the new log reader subscribes to closed streams (its `onDone` closes the reader's own controller), no log line reaches `ProtocolDiscovery`, and the VM Service URL is never found.

### Suggested fix (one of)

- Create fresh forwarders per launch (e.g. make `coreDeviceLogForwarder` / `lldbLogForwarder` replaceable and reset them at the start of `launchAppWithLLDBDebugger` / `launchAppWithoutDebugger`), or
- Have `exit()` stop the process but not close the shared controller (let each reader cancel its own subscription), or
- Recreate the `StreamController` in `exit()` after closing it.

A regression test: two consecutive `startApp` calls on one `IOSDevice` (CoreDevice, Xcode 26) with a `dispose()` between them; the second must receive log lines.

### Secondary problem

On interruption, the runner reports `All tests passed!` counting only completed files. A file that never started should count as a failure (or at least not be reported as passed).

### Flutter doctor / versions

- Flutter 3.47.7 • channel stable • framework revision abaf9c5237 (2026-10-08); also checked against `master` on 2026-11-17 — same code.
- Xcode 26.4 (17E192); macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), Intel x86_64.
- iPhone 16 Pro Max, iOS 26.6.2 (23G90), USB.

Verbose log of the two-file run attached (environment lines and identifiers removed). The minimal repro above was run as written on Flutter 3.47.7 and reproduces: first file passes, second hangs; the second file alone passes.

title: [web] "ViewInsets cannot be negative" at startup under Chrome's mobile device emulation: physical size is computed with a stale `visualViewport.scale`
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms web repro` (default `web/index.html`, which has no `<meta name="viewport">`).
2. `flutter run -d web-server --web-port 8092` (debug).
3. Open it in Chromium with mobile device emulation: the DevTools command Chrome's device toolbar sends for a phone (`Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` with `mobile: true`). The code sample below does it with Playwright and a raw CDP session. Playwright's own Pixel 7 preset (`devices['Pixel 7']`, which sets `isMobile: true`) gives the same result.

### Expected results

The app starts without errors.

### Actual results

It fails while the app starts: 3 out of 3 runs with the raw CDP command, 5 out of 5 with the Playwright preset:

```
Assertion failed: org-dartlang-sdk:///lib/_engine/engine/window.dart:347:7
_viewInsets.isNonNegative
"ViewInsets cannot be negative. This is usually caused by an incorrect physicalSize calculation when the keyboard is being dismissed."
    at [_computeOnScreenKeyboardInsets]
    at [_handleBrowserResize]
```

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

The app is the default `flutter create` counter app, unchanged. The browser side, with Playwright and a raw CDP session (the same `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` call Chrome's device toolbar makes):

```js
const { chromium } = require('playwright');
const browser = await chromium.launch();
const page = await (await browser.newContext()).newPage();
const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
await cdp.send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', { width: 412, height: 839, deviceScaleFactor: 2.625, mobile: true });
page.on('pageerror', e => console.log(e.message));
await page.goto('http://localhost:8092/');
```

</details>

### What happens

Without a viewport tag, Chromium's mobile emulation first lays the page out 980 px wide (here 981×1996 at `visualViewport.scale` 0.4204). When the engine inserts its own tag (`FullPageEmbeddingStrategy._applyViewportMeta`), the page is laid out again at 412×839, scale 1, and `_handleBrowserResize` runs.

`FullPageDimensionsProvider.computePhysicalSize()` reads `EngineFlutterDisplay.instance.devicePixelRatio`, which is `window.devicePixelRatio * visualViewport.scale`, before it reads `visualViewport.width`/`height`. At that point the browser still reports the old scale. Reading the width forces layout, and the scale becomes 1. `computeKeyboardInsets()` then reads the ratio again, now with scale 1. So the same resize uses two different pixel ratios.

I logged the getters the engine reads during that resize:

```
dpr=2.625  vv.scale=0.4204   <- computePhysicalSize reads the ratio
vv.w=412   vv.h=839          <- layout happens here
dpr=2.625  vv.scale=1        <- computeKeyboardInsets reads the ratio
vv.h=839
```

Physical height: 839 × 2.625 × 0.4204 ≈ 926. Keyboard inset: 926 − 839 × 2.625 ≈ −1276.

With a viewport tag in `index.html` from the start, there is no zoomed-out layout and no error (3 out of 3).

In release builds the assertion is compiled out, but the physical size is still wrong until the next metrics change.

On real Chrome for Android it doesn't happen, at least with Chrome 91 on an Android 12 emulator (5 out of 5 runs started cleanly): no `resize` event fires when the engine inserts its viewport tag, so this code path doesn't run then. Chrome's device emulation does fire one. So this mainly hits developers who open a debug build in the DevTools device toolbar, and test tools that emulate phones. The read order in `computePhysicalSize` is still fragile on its own.

The order is the same on master today (`full_page_dimensions_provider.dart`, `computePhysicalSize`). Reading `visualViewport.width`/`height` before the pixel ratio, or computing both from one snapshot, should fix it. I'm happy to send a PR.

Related but different trigger: #193639.

title: OverflowBox(fit: OverflowBoxFit.deferToChild): getDryLayout disagrees with layout when minWidth/maxWidth/minHeight/maxHeight override the incoming constraints
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Run this widget test (`flutter test`). It turns on Flutter's own `debugCheckIntrinsicSizes` check, which every
framework test already runs with (`packages/flutter/test/flutter_test_config.dart`):

```dart
import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

void main() {
  testWidgets('OverflowBox deferToChild: dry layout matches layout', (WidgetTester tester) async {
    debugCheckIntrinsicSizes = true;
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      const Directionality(
        textDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
        child: Align(
          alignment: Alignment.topLeft,
          child: OverflowBox(
            fit: OverflowBoxFit.deferToChild,
            minWidth: 200,
            child: SizedBox(width: 50, height: 50),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
    debugCheckIntrinsicSizes = false;
    expect(tester.takeException(), isNull);
  });
}
```

### Expected results

The test passes: `OverflowBox` lays itself out at 200x50, and `getDryLayout` gives the same size, as the
`RenderBox.computeDryLayout` docs require ("The size returned by this method must match the [size] that the
[RenderBox] will compute for itself in [performLayout]").

### Actual results

Flutter's own check throws:

```
The size given to the RenderConstrainedOverflowBox class differs from the size computed by computeDryLayout.
The size computed in performLayout is Size(200.0, 50.0), which is different from Size(50.0, 50.0), which was computed by computeDryLayout.
...
If you are not writing your own RenderBox subclass, then this is not your fault.
```

The same widget with the default `fit: OverflowBoxFit.max` passes.

### Where it shows up

We hit this in generated layouts before we found the cause. A title with `maxWidth: 451` that wraps to two lines sat
under an `OverflowBox(fit: OverflowBoxFit.deferToChild)` in a grid column 954 wide, and the grid asked its children
for their dry layout to size its rows. The `OverflowBox` answered the child's dry size under the column's
constraints (one line, 44 tall) instead of under its own (two lines, 88 tall). So the row came out a line short, and
the next paragraph was painted over the title's second line. We work around it today by overriding
`computeDryLayout` in a subclass, the same way as the fix below.

### Cause

`RenderConstrainedOverflowBox.computeDryLayout` asks the child for its dry size under the **incoming** constraints:

```dart
OverflowBoxFit.deferToChild => child?.getDryLayout(constraints) ?? constraints.smallest,
```

`performLayout` lays the child out under the **inner** constraints and then constrains the result to the incoming ones:

```dart
child!.layout(_getInnerConstraints(constraints), parentUsesSize: true);
...
case OverflowBoxFit.deferToChild:
  size = constraints.constrain(child!.size);
```

`computeDryBaseline` in the same class already uses `_getInnerConstraints(constraints)` for the child, but it gets the
box's own size from `getDryLayout(constraints)`, so dry baselines are off as well. The code dates from #129095,
which added `deferToChild`; its tests don't call `getDryLayout`.

Reproduces on Flutter 3.50.0 (current stable), 3.47.8 and 3.38.5. The line is unchanged on master as of today.

### Suggested fix

```dart
OverflowBoxFit.deferToChild => constraints.constrain(
  child?.getDryLayout(_getInnerConstraints(constraints)) ?? constraints.smallest,
),
```

This mirrors `performLayout`. With this change, a new test in `test/widgets/overflow_box_test.dart` (four cases:
min above the child, max below the incoming max, a tight incoming width, a child larger than the incoming max) passes
and fails without it. On 3.47.8, the whole `packages/flutter` suite (916 files, 20,884 tests) gives the same failures
with and without the change: 70 golden pixel mismatches local to my machine, none new. `dart analyze` and `dart format` are
clean.
Happy to send the PR.

### Flutter doctor

Flutter 3.50.0 (stable, framework revision ab2912035e), macOS. Also reproduced on 3.47.8 and 3.38.5.

title: [Linux] Accessible node extents in ATK_XY_PARENT coordinates include the ancestors' origin
TextField calls Clipboard.hasStrings on every frame while the Android soft keyboard is opening
body:
### Steps to reproduce

# TextField calls `Clipboard.hasStrings` on every frame while the Android soft keyboard is opening

## Summary

On Android, a normal `TextField` probes the clipboard once when it is created. If the clipboard already contains text, that probe marks the field as pasteable. After that, `EditableTextState.didUpdateWidget` calls `Clipboard.hasStrings()` again on **every rebuild**.

Opening the soft keyboard changes `MediaQuery.viewInsets` and rebuilds the route on every animation frame. Each of those frames calls `Clipboard.hasStrings()`. Android implements that call with `ClipboardManager.hasPrimaryClip()` and `ClipboardManager.getPrimaryClipDescription()`. Xiaomi, Huawei, vivo, and other Chinese app-store scanners record those calls as clipboard access. A login screen that only shows the keyboard is therefore reported as “frantically collecting clipboard information,” even though the app never calls `Clipboard.getData` and the user never taps Paste.

This is still present in Flutter 3.50.0, released 11 November 2026. The same loop is in 3.41.9.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy any text on the device, so the clipboard is non-empty.
2. Run the sample below on an Android device.
3. Tap the text field and let the soft keyboard animate open.
4. Watch logcat, or a privacy proxy that hooks `ClipboardManager.getPrimaryClipDescription`.

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: KeyboardClipboardPage()));

class KeyboardClipboardPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const KeyboardClipboardPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const Scaffold(
      resizeToAvoidBottomInset: true,
      body: Padding(
        padding: EdgeInsets.all(24),
        child: TextField(
          decoration: InputDecoration(hintText: 'Tap to show the keyboard'),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

No `Clipboard` API is used in application code. `enableInteractiveSelection` is left at its default.

## Expected results

`Clipboard.hasStrings()` runs only when the user does something that needs the paste affordance, such as opening the selection menu or tapping Paste.

Showing the soft keyboard, animating `viewInsets`, or rebuilding the page must not query the clipboard on every frame.

## Actual results

While the keyboard animates, `getPrimaryClipDescription` is called many times per second. A typical stack is:

```text
android.content.ClipboardManager.getPrimaryClipDescription
io.flutter.plugin.platform.PlatformPlugin.clipboardHasStrings
io.flutter.embedding.engine.systemchannels.PlatformChannel
Clipboard.hasStrings
ClipboardStatusNotifier.update
EditableTextState.didUpdateWidget
```

App-store review tools describe this as frequent clipboard collection during login, with no user consent for that frequency and no product need for it. vivo has rejected apps for this behavior. See also the report quoted on [#190654](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190654).

## Cause

`EditableTextState.initState` always listens to `ClipboardStatusNotifier`. The first listener calls `update()` while the status is `unknown`, and `update()` calls `Clipboard.hasStrings()`.

On Android, `PlatformPlugin.clipboardHasStrings()` does not read the clip text, but it does call `hasPrimaryClip()` and `getPrimaryClipDescription()`. Those two calls are exactly what the store scanners count.

If that call returns true, `pasteEnabled` stays true. `didUpdateWidget` then does this on every rebuild. This is the code in the `3.50.0` tag:

```dart
final bool canPaste = widget.selectionControls is TextSelectionHandleControls
    ? pasteEnabled
    : widget.selectionControls?.canPaste(this) ?? false;
if (widget.selectionEnabled && pasteEnabled && canPaste) {
  clipboardStatus.update();
}
```

`update()` calls `Clipboard.hasStrings()` again even when the status is already `pasteable`. `ValueNotifier` does not notify listeners if the value is unchanged, but the platform call has already happened. The keyboard inset animation rebuilds the focused route once per frame, so the call repeats for the whole animation. The same thing happens while the user is typing, because each `TextEditingValue` change rebuilds `EditableText`.

`ClipboardStatusNotifier` also calls `update()` on `AppLifecycleState.resumed`, so every field that is currently mounted probes the clipboard again when the app returns to the foreground.

## What does not fix it

- Replacing the field with a plain `TextField`. A plain `TextField` is the widget that does this.
- `Clipboard.hasStrings` instead of `Clipboard.getData`. The engine already avoids reading the clip contents. Compliance tools still flag `getPrimaryClipDescription`.
- Upgrading from 3.41.9 to 3.50.0. The `didUpdateWidget` loop is unchanged.
- `enableInteractiveSelection: false` removes copy and paste, which is not acceptable for a login field. On current stable it also does not stop the `initState` listener: adding the listener still calls `hasStrings()` once per field, and resume calls it again. This was rechecked on 3.47.8 in [#190654](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190654).

## Suggested fix

Do not call `Clipboard.hasStrings()` from `didUpdateWidget`.

Query at most once when a selectable field gains focus, or only when the selection menu is about to be shown. Do not query again because `viewInsets` changed or because the user typed a character.

Please also skip the probe for fields that cannot paste (`readOnly`, or `enableInteractiveSelection: false`).

[#190707](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/190707) is the right direction: one check when focus is gained, none on build, none on resume for an unfocused field, and a menu that updates when the in-flight check completes. It was still open on 4 November 2026 and is not in 3.50.0. The keyboard-animation loop above should be covered by that patch, not only the unfocused `initState` case.

An application-level flag such as `clipboardStatusPolicy: proactive | onMenu | never` would let stores that forbid background probes keep Paste, without forking the framework.

## Workaround we are using

We keep the clipboard status from remaining `pasteable`, so `pasteEnabled` stays false and `didUpdateWidget` stops calling `update()`. The menu reads the clipboard once when the user long-presses, and shows Paste only if that single check succeeds. This stops the per-frame calls, but it is easy to get wrong: a password field has no cut or copy, so if Paste is suppressed the whole menu is empty.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.50.0 stable (11 November 2026), and the same loop in 3.41.9
- Android, reproduced on Xiaomi / MIUI. The same `getPrimaryClipDescription` stack is reported on Huawei and vivo
- A non-empty clipboard is required to enter the per-frame loop. An empty clipboard still costs the initial `hasStrings()` call

## Related

- [#190654](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190654) — open. `hasStrings` on `TextField` init and on resume, without a paste action. Confirmed on master in August 2026. The keyboard-frame loop is the same `didUpdateWidget` path, and it is what store reviews measure as “frequent.”
- [#190707](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/190707) — open, not in 3.50.0. Limits the check to a focused, editable, selectable field.
- [#179840](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/179840) — draft. Removes the repeated `getPrimaryClipDescription` calls from `didUpdateWidget`.
- [#101196](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/101196), [#141960](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/141960), [#151076](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/151076), [#167913](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/167913) — the same compliance report since 2022, on MIUI, Xiaomi, Huawei, vivo, and iOS.


### Expected results

TextField do not calls Clipboard.hasStrings on every frame

### Actual results

TextField calls Clipboard.hasStrings on every frame

### Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: KeyboardClipboardPage()));

class KeyboardClipboardPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const KeyboardClipboardPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const Scaffold(
      resizeToAvoidBottomInset: true,
      body: Padding(
        padding: EdgeInsets.all(24),
        child: TextField(
          decoration: InputDecoration(hintText: 'Tap to show the keyboard'),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

title: [macOS] Embedder crashes on AppKit AX query (tracking-area collection) after an invalid semantics update — Flutter 3.44.9 release build
body:
### Summary

A release-mode macOS app built with **Flutter 3.44.9** (engine revision `5a2a6a42cce67f965cf540fcecf616faca624aa1`, framework uuid `4c4c4491-5555-3144-a13d-98496080a6b4`, Dart 3.12.2) crashes on the main thread when AppKit collects tracking areas on a mouse move. Every crash re-enters the engine from `___collectTrackingAreasForTargetAndWinLoc_block_invoke` and dies inside `FlutterMacOS` on what looks like a stale accessibility/platform node.

This is a follow-up to #193588 (closed by the inactivity bot on 2026-11-13, not fixed). That report describes exactly this trigger: *“accessibility in use (VoiceOver, an AX client …, or just AppKit's own tracking-area collection on a mouse move)”*, on Flutter 3.44.8.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Flutter 3.44.9 release-mode macOS app (universal, code-signed, no dSYM shipped) on macOS 27.x.
2. No accessibility client needs to be enabled — AppKit's own tracking-area collection is enough.
3. Move the pointer over the window. The process dies within 28 s to a few minutes, no dialog, no Dart exception.

I cannot attach a minimal `main.dart`: the app is closed source. What I can offer is the crash evidence from four incidents, two different builds, two macOS versions.

### Crash signature

Thread 0 (main), identical call path in all four reports:

```
0  FlutterMacOS  +11666496 / +11666576 / +11775528   ← fault
1  FlutterMacOS  +11666616   (repeated twice in 1.51.1 → recursion)
2  FlutterMacOS  +11666616
3  FlutterMacOS  +215308
4  FlutterMacOS  +215044
5  AppKit        ___collectTrackingAreasForTargetAndWinLoc_block_invoke + 172
6  CoreFoundation __NSARRAY_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_BLOCK__
7  CoreFoundation -[__NSArrayM enumerateObjectsWithOptions:usingBlock:]
8  AppKit        -[_NSTrackingAreaAKManager _updateActiveTrackingAreasForWindowLocation:modifierFlags:]
9  AppKit        -[_NSTrackingAreaAKManager _mouseMoved:]
10 AppKit        _routeMouseMovedEvent
```

Fault details across the four incidents — same instruction class (a byte read), different garbage, worsening over time:

| app build / OS | uptime before crash | `x0` | `far` | `esr` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.50.0 / macOS 27.0 | 2 h 56 min | `0` | `0xffffffffffffffff` | `0x92000004` |
| 1.51.0 / macOS 27.2 | 8 min 27 s | `0x654b74726f53676e` (printable ASCII, i.e. string bytes) | `x0 + 0x40` | `0x92000004` |
| 1.51.0 / macOS 27.2 | 35 s | same | same | `0x92000004` |
| 1.51.1 / macOS 27.2.1 | 28 s | `0x75b35c9e00` (live heap pointer) | `0x124` | `0x92000006` |

Two runs of the same build produced byte-identical `x0`/`far` (ASLR bases differed), so the corruption is reproducible; switching builds changes the value but not the path. Reading string content as an object pointer, and `far − x0 = 0x40`, is consistent with a field load on a reused/freed platform node.

### Why I think this is #193588 rather than a mouse-tracking embedder bug

- The crash is always reached from AppKit's tracking-area collection, which performs AX queries — the trigger listed in #193588.
- Frames 3–4 (`+215044`, `+215308`) are in the embedder's Objective-C surface; registers in the faulting frame point at `OBJC_CLASS_$_FlutterViewController` / `NSResponder` selectors, i.e. platform-node/AX delegate code.
- The recurring recursion (`+11666616` twice) is the child-walk pattern described in #195399 (`FlutterPlatformNodeDelegate::ChildAtIndex` during tree traversal, Windows, open, P2).

### What I already checked about the fix

- Framework-side trigger fix #193372 (`packages/flutter/lib/src/semantics/semantics.dart`) merged 2026-10-19. It is **absent** at tags `3.44.9` and `3.47.9`, present on `master`.
- Engine-side recovery (#193588) never landed; #193588 was closed by the inactivity bot.

### Questions

1. Is there still a planned engine-side fix so a failed `AXTree` update cannot leave dangling platform nodes (the #193588 scope)?
2. Would a build from `master` (or the next stable after 3.47.9) stop this crash given the #193372 trigger fix? I can test a nightly build and report back with new `.ips` files.
3. If this needs a different tracker/label (`team-macos` vs accessibility), please point me at it.

### Environment

- macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), Mac17,7 (Apple M5 Max, 36 GB), SIP enabled.
- App: MeshCore 1.51.1 build 81, `com.liamcottle.meshcore.macos`, universal, signed (`A2Q8595W43`), no dSYM.
- Engine: `FlutterMacOS.framework` uuid `4c4c4491-5555-3144-a13d-98496080a6b4`, Dart 3.12.2, i.e. Flutter 3.44.9.
- No `flutter doctor -v` from this machine: the app is a distributed binary, not a local Flutter checkout.

Full `.ips` reports (four incidents) can be pasted or attached on request.

### Steps to reproduce

### Expected results

Three MOVE records in chronological order, each with its own coordinates, timestamp, and pressure. The middle position preserves the bend in the stroke.

Only the current sample (10, 0) is emitted. The regression test on Flutter main `4d19bda07a` fails: `expected:<864> but was:<288>` bytes. ### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux (Impeller OpenGLES backend, "Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLESSDF)"), run the code sample below.
2. Look at the rows filled with a `LinearGradient`.
3. Compare with Flutter 3.47.4, or with Impeller disabled.

### Expected results

Each row shows a smooth gradient from #0557AB to #06165A across its full width, as on Flutter 3.47.4 and as on 3.50.0 with Impeller disabled.


### Actual results

On 3.50.0 with Impeller (GLES), every **rect / rounded-rect** gradient fill is correct up to some x and then snaps to the end color with a hard edge. The same gradient on a non-rect **path** renders correctly.

The cutoff does not depend on height. It falls where `x × width ≈ 65536`, which is the fp16 limit (65504):

```
3.50.0 (Impeller):    0557ab 0552a5 054d9f 054899 054493 053f8d 063a87 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a
3.50.0 (no Impeller): 0456aa 0552a4 054d9f 054899 054393 053f8d 053a87 053581 05307b 052b75 05276f 052269 051d63 05185d 06165a 06165a
```

| Config | Rect / RRect / drawRect | Gradient on a non-rect Path |
|---|---|---|
| 3.47.4, Impeller | ✅ | ✅ |
| 3.47.4, Skia | ✅ | ✅ |
| **3.50.0, Impeller** | ❌ snaps to end color | ✅ |
| 3.50.0, Skia | ✅ | ✅ |

**Radial gradients** are affected as well, about 256 px from the center (where √65504 ≈ 256). A `RadialGradient` with a 1200 px radius on a 600 × 600 box, sampled every 50 px outward from the center:

```
3.50.0 (Impeller): 0557ab 0554a8 0551a4 054fa1 054c9d 05499a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a 06165a
expected:          0557ab 0554a8 0551a4 054fa1 054c9d 05499a 054797 054493 054190 053f8d 053c89 053986
```

In a real app this shows up as a full-window splash gradient collapsing into two flat color blocks, and wide gradient progress bars getting a hard edge part-way along.

### Cause

Gradients are now drawn by UberSDF (#190874, relanded in #192124). `impeller/entity/shaders/uber_sdf_common.glsl` declares `precision mediump float;`, and the gradient parameter `t`, `gradient_delta` and `inv_gradient_length` are all unqualified, so they are mediump. The linear `dot()` is about distance × gradient length, and the radial `length()` squares the position. Where mediump is fp16, both overflow 65504, `t` clamps, and the end color is sampled. The dedicated gradient shaders that UberSDF replaced (e.g. `linear_gradient_uniform_fill.frag`) did this math in `highp`.

The SSBO variant (#192962) isn't used on GLES, so Linux (and presumably Windows) always take this path. I've only verified this on Linux.

**On master:** after #196392, the linear `dot()` takes the highp varying directly, so on this driver it is promoted to highp and probably no longer overflows. I haven't built master to confirm that. The radial `length()` still runs on a mediump copy of the position (checked in `impellerc --opengl-es` output), so radial is still affected.

**Fix:** declare the gradient uniforms, the gradient position, `t` and the `getGradientColor()` parameter `highp`. I'll open a PR for this. I verified it by patching the embedded GLES shader in the 3.50.0 `libflutter_linux_gtk.so` the same way, and the linear and radial cases above render correctly with the patch.


### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

const gradient = LinearGradient(
  colors: [Color(0xFF0557AB), Color(0xFF06165A)],
);

const radial = RadialGradient(
  center: Alignment.centerLeft,
  radius: 2,
  colors: [Color(0xFF0557AB), Color(0xFF06165A)],
);

class PathPainter extends CustomPainter {
  @override
  void paint(Canvas canvas, Size size) {
    // Not a plain rect, so it doesn't go through UberSDF: renders correctly.
    final path = Path()
      ..moveTo(0, 0)
      ..lineTo(size.width, 0)
      ..lineTo(size.width, size.height)
      ..lineTo(size.width / 2, size.height - 1)
      ..lineTo(0, size.height)
      ..close();
    canvas.drawPath(
      path,
      Paint()..shader = gradient.createShader(Offset.zero & size),
    );
  }

  @override
  bool shouldRepaint(covariant CustomPainter oldDelegate) => false;
}

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        backgroundColor: Colors.black,
        body: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            // Broken on 3.50 + Impeller GLES: hard edge at x ≈ 65536 / 800 ≈ 82.
            Container(
              width: 800,
              height: 60,
              decoration: const BoxDecoration(gradient: gradient),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            // Broken: rounded rect.
            Container(
              width: 800,
              height: 60,
              decoration: BoxDecoration(
                gradient: gradient,
                borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8),
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            // Correct: same gradient on a non-rect path.
            CustomPaint(size: const Size(800, 60), painter: PathPainter()),
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            // Broken: radial, snaps to the end color ~256 px from the center.
            Container(
              width: 600,
              height: 300,
              decoration: const BoxDecoration(gradient: radial),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    ),
  );
}
```

title: [Impeller] Bounded BackdropFilter blur does nothing inside a translated save layer

[material_ui, cupertino_ui] MaterialUiCompatibilityBridge subtree usage breaks Navigator routes and bridge deprecations break --fatal-infos
body:
Two gaps affect apps using `MaterialUiCompatibilityBridge` and `CupertinoUiCompatibilityBridge` during the 3.50 standalone UI migration:

1. **Subtree usage breaks Navigator routes**: Both `material_ui`'s `README.md` and `MaterialUiCompatibilityBridge` dartdoc show wrapping an individual subtree (`body: MaterialUiCompatibilityBridge(child: LegacyPackageWidget())`). When a legacy child pushes a dialog, picker, bottom sheet, or popup menu onto `Navigator`, `CapturedThemes` captures `legacy.Theme` (`InheritedTheme`) but does not capture `Localizations` (`_LocalizationsScope`), throwing `No MaterialLocalizations found`. Only app-wide placement via `MaterialApp.builder` covers routes.
2. **Deprecated bridge causes `--fatal-infos` failures**: Both bridge classes and constructors carry `@Deprecated`, so following the migration guide adds `deprecated_member_use` diagnostics unless suppressed with `// ignore: deprecated_member_use`. Additionally, `MaterialUiCompatibilityBridge` alone omits non-primary `CupertinoThemeData` fields (`barBackgroundColor`) unless nested with `CupertinoUiCompatibilityBridge`.

title: [flutter_localizations] dart fix rules produce ambiguous_import errors for GlobalMaterialLocalizations and GlobalCupertinoLocalizations
body:
In Flutter 3.50.0 (after https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/192954), running `dart fix --apply` on files that import `package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart` and reference `GlobalMaterialLocalizations` or `GlobalCupertinoLocalizations` produces uncompilable code.

`packages/flutter_localizations/lib/fix_data/fix_material_localizations.yaml` and `packages/flutter_localizations/lib/fix_data/fix_cupertino_localizations.yaml` add `import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';` and `import 'package:cupertino_ui/cupertino_ui.dart';` via `replacedBy` without removing or hiding `import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';`. Because both libraries export classes named `GlobalMaterialLocalizations` and `GlobalCupertinoLocalizations`, Dart fails with `ambiguous_import`.

This broken dual-import output is present in `packages/flutter_localizations/test_fixes/material_localizations.dart.expect` and `packages/flutter_localizations/test_fixes/cupertino_localizations.dart.expect` (excluded from analysis by `.dartignore`). The transform also adds `cupertino_ui` imports even when `cupertino_ui` is not a direct `pubspec.yaml` dependency, triggering `depend_on_referenced_packages`.

title: [tool] DevFS upload keeps retrying with no delay after it gives up, exhausting local ports
[Linux] FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software aborts with "Impeller DlText cannot be drawn to a Skia canvas" because Impeller stays enabled
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms=linux bug && cd bug` (Flutter 3.50.0 stable, no changes)
2. `flutter build linux --release`
3. `FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software ./build/linux/*/release/bundle/bug`

### Expected results

The app runs on the software renderer that `FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software` selects (#166307).

### Actual results

The process aborts drawing the first frame:

```console
$ FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software ./build/linux/arm64/release/bundle/bug
** (com.example.bug:506): WARNING **: Using the software renderer. Not all features are supported. This is not recommended.
To switch back to the default renderer, unset the FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER environment variable.
[FATAL:flutter/display_list/skia/dl_sk_dispatcher.cc(328)] Check failed: blob. Impeller DlText cannot be drawn to a Skia canvas.
Aborted
```

The same bundle with the variable unset runs on Impeller (`Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLESSDF)`). With the variable set and the runner calling `fl_dart_project_set_enable_impeller(project, FALSE)` before `fl_view_new`, it runs on the software renderer without the abort.

### Cause

`fl_engine_new_full` (`shell/platform/linux/fl_engine.cc`) reads `FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER` and picks `kSoftware`, but `fl_engine_start` still adds `--enable-impeller` whenever `fl_dart_project_get_enable_impeller` is true, which is the default. The embedder's `kSoftware` branch (`InferSoftwarePlatformViewCreationCallback`) ignores `enable_impeller` and creates a Skia software surface, but `settings.enable_impeller` stays set, so text is recorded as Impeller `DlText` and then hits the `FML_CHECK` in `DlSkCanvasDispatcher::drawText`.

`FLUTTER_ENGINE_SWITCHES` is compiled out of release builds, so a user of a published app can't pass `--enable-impeller=false` to work around this. The software renderer is the fallback users get pointed to when a GPU driver misbehaves (for example #191775, where the reporter hit this same abort as a side note, and #195885 on NVIDIA), and on 3.50 that fallback aborts for every app that hasn't opted out of Impeller in its runner.

A possible fix: in `fl_engine_start`, don't add `--enable-impeller` when `renderer_type == kSoftware` (or have the embedder force `settings.enable_impeller = false` for a `kSoftware` renderer config).

### Code sample

The default `flutter create` app.

### Flutter Doctor output

```console
Flutter 3.50.0 • channel stable • https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git
Framework • revision ab2912035e • 2026-11-09
Engine • revision 371f77202a
```

Reproduced on Ubuntu 22.04 arm64 under Xvfb (Mesa 23.2.1), release build. `master` has the same logic in `fl_engine.cc`.

[web] Disposed EnginePlatformDispatcher is retained by its document click listener
body:
`EnginePlatformDispatcher` installs a capturing document click listener during construction. Its `dispose()` does not remove that callback, leaving old dispatchers reachable after Flutter web hot restart.

### Reproduction

Run the attached ordinary Flutter web app and hot restart it 15 times in the same page. Hold the CanvasKit and DDC cleanups constant so their separate retention paths cannot hide the listener's effect. Keep only `WeakRef`s to the retiring dispatchers and run GC before checking them.

Without #196787, all 15 retired dispatchers remain alive; there are 16 capturing click registrations and no corresponding removals. With #196787, the 15 old listeners are removed and all retired dispatchers are collected. Post-GC JavaScript heap growth from restart 2 to 15 falls from 154.24 to 24.03 MiB in this fixture. The fixed run has a later plateau; the initial growth is still present.

Flutter source `22e676c57e1e6d04c2289a47368ea4093bbc3c18`; Dart `3.15.0-edge.e1671c00019972a92e16247dc254ad3eaa48c2b6`; macOS 27.2, Apple M4 Pro, Chrome 157.0.8103.80.

[Desktop evidence: fixtures, scripts, per-restart JSON/CSV and PNG/SVG graphs](https://github.com/LeonMollNetlight/flutter/blob/1992af0035c506ae44aa99faa5fcfe03a4f3d87f/docs/research/hot-restart-2026-11-19/EVIDENCE.md). Values are medians of three fresh-page runs per variant.

This is Flutter web engine cleanup and does not depend on DartPad or on a user generating an accessibility-navigation click. The DDC native-extension retention has its own fix in https://dart-review.googlesource.com/c/sdk/+/578301.
![Desktop hot-restart measurement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonMollNetlight/flutter/1992af0035c506ae44aa99faa5fcfe03a4f3d87f/docs/research/hot-restart-2026-11-19/flutter-retention.png)

title: [web] CanvasKit retains WebGL contexts across hot restarts and recreates evicted contexts
body:
An ordinary Flutter web debug app retains old CanvasKit contexts after hot restart. Once Chrome starts evicting contexts, callbacks from retired surfaces create more contexts and the main-thread animation cadence drops.

### Reproduction

1. Start the attached animated `CustomPaint` app with `flutter run -d web-server` and open it in Chrome.
2. Trigger 15 full hot restarts through the Flutter machine protocol, keeping the same page and CanvasKit instance.
3. Track `getContext('webgl*')` calls and context state; sample `requestAnimationFrame` cadence after each restart.

The original SDK ends with 16 active tracked contexts and a median 3344 contexts created. Cadence falls from about 60 to 9.4 rAF calls/s. With #196786 alone, active contexts remain at 2 and cadence ends at 59.9 calls/s. Both conditions reuse CanvasKit. rAF is a main-thread measurement, not compositor presentation.

Flutter source `22e676c57e1e6d04c2289a47368ea4093bbc3c18`; Dart `3.15.0-edge.e1671c00019972a92e16247dc254ad3eaa48c2b6`; macOS 27.2, Apple M4 Pro, Chrome 157.0.8103.80.

[Desktop evidence: fixtures, scripts, per-restart JSON/CSV and PNG/SVG graphs](https://github.com/LeonMollNetlight/flutter/blob/1992af0035c506ae44aa99faa5fcfe03a4f3d87f/docs/research/hot-restart-2026-11-19/EVIDENCE.md). Values are medians of three fresh-page runs per variant.

The DDC and document-listener leaks are separate: applying the CanvasKit change alone does not stop the JavaScript heap growth. #128059 reports an older context-loss assertion; this reproduction does not establish that it has the same cause.
![Desktop hot-restart measurement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonMollNetlight/flutter/1992af0035c506ae44aa99faa5fcfe03a4f3d87f/docs/research/hot-restart-2026-11-19/flutter-cadence.png)

title: [webview_flutter_wkwebview] Allow apps to set WKWebView content insets / obscuredContentInsets (opt out of forced zero contentInset)
body:
### Use case

On iOS 26 the system tab bar is translucent (Liquid Glass) and floats over the content. We want a `WebViewWidget`
to extend under the tab bar so the page scrolls behind the glass, like Safari and native apps do, while the end of
the document and `position: fixed` elements stay above the bar.

WebKit supports this natively:
- `WKWebView.obscuredContentInsets` (iOS 26, public) keeps fixed elements / `100vh` inside the visible area;
- `scrollView.contentInset` adds scroll room so the last content can scroll above the bar.

`webview_flutter_wkwebview` has no API for either. We access the native `WKWebView` via
`WebKitWebViewController.webViewIdentifier` + `FWFWebViewFlutterWKWebViewExternalAPI` and set them ourselves.
`obscuredContentInsets` works, but `scrollView.contentInset` is reset to zero on every frame change by
`WebViewImpl.frame` (`WebViewProxyAPIDelegate.swift`, with `contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior = .never`), so we have to
re-apply it with KVO after each reset. This is intentional plugin behavior (flutter/plugins#2343, restored in 2.9.1),
but it leaves no supported way to give the page scroll room under translucent bars.

### Proposal

Any of these on `WebKitWebViewController` (iOS):
1. `setObscuredContentInsets(EdgeInsets)` for iOS 26+ (maps to `WKWebView.obscuredContentInsets`), and
2. `setContentInset(EdgeInsets)` / `setScrollIndicatorInsets(EdgeInsets)` that the plugin keeps (instead of forcing
   zero on frame change), or
3. an opt-out flag for the forced zero `contentInset`, similar to the Android opt-out for inset changes
   (flutter/packages#11192).

Default behavior stays unchanged (insets = 0), so existing apps are not affected.

### Environment
- webview_flutter_wkwebview 3.27.0 (latest 3.27.2), Flutter 3.47.9, iOS 26 / 27 (iPhone, simulator).

title: [web] iOS Safari auto-zooms the page when a TextField is focused without semantics (default text editing input has no 16px floor)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

This is a follow-up to #192327. That issue and its fix (#192328) covered the **semantics** text input. The same auto-zoom still happens on the **default (non-semantics) text editing path**, which is the path most users go through.

1. Create a Flutter web app with a `TextField` whose font size is below 16px. The Material default (`bodyLarge`) is 16px, but 14px is common in app themes. See the code sample.
2. Do **not** enable semantics.
3. `flutter build web`, deploy, and open the app in Safari on an iPhone.
4. Tap the text field and type something.
5. Dismiss the keyboard.

### Expected results

Focusing the field opens the keyboard without changing the page zoom, as it did before Flutter 3.47.

### Actual results

iOS Safari zooms the whole page in when the field is focused, and the page stays zoomed after the keyboard is dismissed. The Flutter view stays enlarged and shifted, with content cut off on the right edge, until the user pinches back out manually.

**Cause.** Two changes combine:

- #182047 (in 3.47.0) changed the `flt-viewport` meta tag from `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no` to `maximum-scale=5.0`. iOS Safari respects `maximum-scale=1.0` for auto-zoom on focus, so before this change the zoom was suppressed.
- The hidden `<input>` / `<textarea>` used by the default text editing strategy copies the framework's font size, with no minimum: `EditableTextStyle.applyToDomElement` sets `style.font = cssFont`, built from `fontSize` ([text_editing.dart at 3.50.0](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L2950-L2959)). When that size is under 16px, iOS Safari auto-zooms on focus.

#192328 added `_applyIosMinimumFontSize` in `semantics/text_field.dart` only. In 3.50.0 and on `master`, `text_editing/text_editing.dart` has no equivalent, so apps without semantics still get the zoom. The [web accessibility docs](https://docs.flutter.dev/ui/accessibility/web-accessibility) also describe the 16px floor as applying to "hidden semantic" inputs only.

**Suggested fix.** Apply the same iOS floor (`max(16, frameworkFontSize)`, as a `font-size` longhand after the `font` shorthand) to the default strategy's editing element in `EditableTextStyle.applyToDomElement`, or wherever the style is applied for `DefaultTextEditingStrategy` and its iOS subclass. The element is transparent, so the larger size isn't visible.

**Current workaround.** In `web/index.html`, on iOS only, rewrite the engine's `meta[name="viewport"]` content back to `maximum-scale=1.0` with a `MutationObserver`. iOS still allows user pinch-zoom with that value; only the zoom on focus is suppressed.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MyApp());

class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MyApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: SafeArea(
          child: Padding(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(24),
            child: Column(
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
              children: const [
                Text('Tap the field, type, then close the keyboard'),
                SizedBox(height: 16),
                TextField(
                  style: TextStyle(fontSize: 14),
                  decoration: InputDecoration(hintText: 'Name'),
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

We saw this in a production app; the screenshots contain customer branding, so they aren't attached here. They show: (1) the page at normal scale, (2) the field focused with the keyboard open, and (3) after the keyboard is dismissed, the whole page left zoomed in and cut off on the right.

### Logs

No errors in the console.

### Flutter Doctor output

```
Flutter 3.47.8 • channel stable
Framework • revision 737ba8f885 • 2026-10-22
```

Reported by users on iOS 27 (Safari). Starting from 3.50.0, the code involved (`text_editing.dart`, and `maximum-scale=5.0` in `full_page_embedding_strategy.dart`) is unchanged on the non-semantics path, so the bug should still be present on 3.50.0 and `master`.

title: [Impeller] GLES: skip glInvalidateFramebuffer when there are no attachments to discard
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Flutter app with Impeller on the GLES backend in an Android emulator whose GPU renderer is gfxstream (e.g. emulator 37.2.13 / 37.3.9, `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` or `-gpu swangle`, AVD `system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64`, Linux x86_64 host).
2. Render any frame where the pass discards no attachments.

### Expected results

Nothing happens at the end of the pass, or Impeller skips the invalidate when there is nothing to invalidate.

### Actual results

At the end of a render pass, `RenderPassGLES` calls `gl.InvalidateFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, attachment_count, attachments.data())` even when `attachment_count == 0` (`engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/render_pass_gles.cc`, the `InvalidateFramebuffer.IsAvailable()` block, ~line 888 on `main`; line 720 in 3.47.6).

A zero count is legal in GLES 3.0, but the emulator's gfxstream GLES 3 translator traps on it (libc++ hardened empty-vector `ud2`), and qemu dies with `SIGILL {si_code=ILL_ILLOPN}` in `libgfxstream_backend.so`. The emulator bug is being reported to Google separately. Skipping the call when `attachment_count == 0` costs nothing and avoids the crash on any driver with the same fragility.

We work around it by capping the emulator guest at GLES 2.

### Code sample

Not app-specific: any Impeller GLES frame whose render pass has nothing to discard.

### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.47.6 (stable); the code path is unchanged on `main`.

title: [Impeller][Android][HCPP] SIGBUS in ASurfaceTransaction_setOnComplete binder callback when FlutterEngine is destroyed right after rendering
body:
Destroying a Flutter engine while a frame is still being presented on Android can cause a native crash when an asynchronous completion callback runs after the engine's rendering resources have already been freed.

When `FlutterEngine` is destroyed immediately after rendering a frame while a `SurfaceControl` transaction is still in flight, a `SIGBUS (BUS_ADRALN)` use-after-free can occur on an Android Binder pool thread. This happens because `SurfaceTransaction::Apply` in `engine/src/flutter/impeller/toolkit/android/surface_transaction.cc` registers a `TransactionInFlightData` completion callback via `ASurfaceTransaction_setOnComplete`, which is invoked asynchronously by `TransactionCompletedListener::onTransactionCompleted` after the captured `libflutter.so` objects have already been torn down. This transaction path is only used when HCPP (`EnableHcpp=true`) is enabled, so disabling HCPP avoids the issue.

This was found while preparing https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/197002 to reproduce https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/196094. Running the repro on a Pixel 9 (Mali-G715) did not reproduce that PowerVR driver hang, but instead encountered this crash.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Check out the draft PR https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/197002 (which adds `engineTeardownTest` to `dev/integration_tests/android_hardware_smoke_test`, with `io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableHcpp=true` and `ImpellerBackend=vulkan` in `AndroidManifest.xml`).
2. Connect a non-Pixel-10 Android device (e.g., Pixel 9 / Mali-G715 on Android 15; Pixel 10 hits the separate PowerVR `vkDestroyDevice` hang first).
3. Run the `engineTeardownTest` instrumented test:

```sh
cd dev/integration_tests/android_hardware_smoke_test
flutter create --platform=android --no-overwrite .
flutter pub get
cd android
./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest \
  -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=com.example.android_hardware_smoke_test.FlutterActivityTest#engineTeardownTest
```

Tested on a Pixel 9 (`tokay`), Android 15 (`google/tokay/tokay:15/BP1A.250505.005/13277524:user/release-keys`), Mali-G715 (`v1.r51p0-00eac0`). Reproduced on cycle 4 of 10.

## Expected results

`FlutterEngine.destroy()` waits for or safely detaches any in-flight `ASurfaceTransaction` completion callbacks, and the activity tears down cleanly on every cycle.

## Actual results

The process crashes on a Binder pool thread with `SIGBUS (BUS_ADRALN)` inside the `ASurfaceTransaction_setOnComplete` completion callback:


[web][tool] web/assets/ files silently overwrite Flutter assets in build/web/assets/
body:
Files in an app's `web/assets/` directory end up in the same folder as Flutter's own assets, `build/web/assets/`. When two files land at the same path, the `web/` file silently replaces Flutter's. This happens on every `flutter build web`, not only with `--web-content-hash`.

- **A pubspec asset can be silently replaced.** Flutter puts each asset at `build/web/assets/<key>`, so the asset `images/logo.png` and the file `web/assets/images/logo.png` both land at `build/web/assets/images/logo.png`. The `web/` file wins, and nothing is printed.
- **Flutter's generated files can be replaced too.** A file in `web/assets/` named `FontManifest.json`, `AssetManifest.bin`, `AssetManifest.bin.json` or `NOTICES`, or one under `fonts/`, `shaders/` or `packages/`, overwrites the file Flutter generated.
- **With `--web-content-hash`, these files ship without a hash.** The docs and the build's serving tip say to serve `assets/**` with `immutable` caching. Files from `web/assets/` would then be cached for a year under names that never change.

**Repro** (Flutter 3.50.0 or master):

1. Declare `images/logo.png` under `flutter: assets:` in `pubspec.yaml`.
2. Add a different file at `web/assets/images/logo.png`.
3. Run `flutter build web`. `build/web/assets/images/logo.png` is the `web/` copy, and there is no warning.

**Cause:** `WebReleaseBundle.build` first copies the pubspec assets with `copyAssets` ([targets/web.dart#L1273](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ec58d3f3224/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/targets/web.dart#L1273)). With the flag on, it then hashes them ([#L1287](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ec58d3f3224/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/targets/web.dart#L1287)). Last, it copies every file from `web/` over the top with `copySync` ([#L1313-L1325](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ec58d3f3224/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/targets/web.dart#L1313-L1325)).

**Open questions for the web team:**

1. Should `flutter build web` warn whenever `web/assets/` has files, or only when one actually overwrites a Flutter file?
2. Should it fail the build when a `web/` file would replace a pubspec asset or a generated manifest?
3. Should `--web-content-hash` make the warning an error, since those files are always a caching risk under that flag?

Automatically hashing `web/assets/` is not an option. Those files are usually referenced by hardcoded URLs in `index.html` or CSS, and renaming them would break those references.

A candidate implementation (a warning when `--web-content-hash` is on, with 3 tests) is pushed at `kevmoo:issue-196990`. It is waiting on these answers before it becomes a PR.

Found by @mdebbar in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196908#discussion_r4629131805. Part of https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/149031.
