[Impeller] "Frame bounds are not present in the atlas": glyphs skipped for one frame during a route slide transition (3.50.0, Android Vulkan)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Observed in a production app (profile build) on a Pixel 7a, not yet reduced to a standalone repro that fails reliably. Scenario:

1. Cold start the app (all four occurrences so far were on the first launch after a fresh install).
2. A drag gesture pushes a full-screen route with a vertical `SlideTransition` (enters from the bottom, `Curves.easeOutCubic`, ~180 ms drag then settle).
3. The route body is a scrollable column of Material cards with `Text` in several sizes and weights (labels, numeric values with units).
4. While the route slides in, the lower cards move up from underneath an opaque bottom navigation bar.

Structure sketch (shows the shape of the scene; **not verified** to reproduce on its own):

```dart
Navigator.of(context).push(PageRouteBuilder<void>(
  transitionDuration: const Duration(milliseconds: 300),
  pageBuilder: (_, __, ___) => Scaffold(
    body: ListView(children: [
      for (var i = 0; i < 6; i++)
        Card(child: Column(children: [
          Text('Card $i', style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 18, fontWeight: FontWeight.w600)),
          const Text('117.8 V · 3.68 V/cell', style: TextStyle(fontSize: 22, fontWeight: FontWeight.w700)),
          const Text('Odometer 7475 km · 134 V · 2400 Wh · 3500 W', style: TextStyle(fontSize: 13)),
        ])),
    ]),
    bottomNavigationBar: const ColoredBox(color: Color(0xFF111318), child: SizedBox(height: 110)),
  ),
  transitionsBuilder: (_, animation, __, child) => SlideTransition(
    position: Tween(begin: const Offset(0, 1), end: Offset.zero)
        .chain(CurveTween(curve: Curves.easeOutCubic))
        .animate(animation),
    child: child,
  ),
));
```

### Expected results

No Impeller validation errors; every glyph of every visible text frame is drawn.

### Actual results

In one frame during the slide, Impeller logs a burst of validation errors from `text_contents.cc(211)`, all with the same `FontGlyphAtlas` pointer and within 1 ms on the raster thread:

```
E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/impeller/entity/contents/text_contents.cc(211)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Frame bounds are not present in the atlas 0xb400007492ee4c50
(x11 within 1 ms)
```

In 3.50.0 this branch does `continue`, so each line is one glyph skipped in that frame (11 glyphs in one occurrence, 19 in another). The comment above that branch says a slow lookup into the glyph atlas hash table should be performed when `frame_bounds.is_placeholder` is true, but the code only logs and skips the glyph.

Frequency (same app, same scripted gesture sequence, synthetic pointer events through `GestureBinding`, thermal status 0):

| Flutter | Runs with the error | Entries per run |
|---|---|---|
| 3.50.0 stable | 4 of 21 (3 of 6 without screen recording, 1 of 13 with `adb shell screenrecord`, 0 of 2 more without recording) | 19, 11, 11, 11 |
| 3.47.9 stable | 0 of 10 | - |

Always the same moment: the first time this route is shown after launch (0.46 s after the drag starts in the timestamped occurrence; in the other three, by log order, during the same slide). Later slides of the same route in the same run never log it.

Visible effect: I recorded the screen at 90 fps with a device-clock overlay synced to logcat. In the recorded occurrence every visible glyph is present in the frames around the error and matches the same moment on 3.47.9. At that moment a line of small text is still under the opaque bottom bar, so the skipped glyphs were probably hidden there. I can't rule out a visible missing glyph in another run.

Possibly related: #192140 / #192141 (glyph packer coordinates truncated above the int16 range; the fix was not in 3.50.0) and #188904 (glyph atlas errors with COLR text under zoom; different messages: `lazy_glyph_atlas.cc(72)`, `text_contents.cc(258)`).

### Logs

```
I flutter : [IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_vk_impeller.cc(74)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
```

No other errors, warnings or crashes in the run.

title: [web] Autofill value of the focused field is lost when the form wakes up from dormant state
[web] Stale aria-owns after a Material Tooltip hides: button keeps pointing at the removed overlay node (axe aria-valid-attr-value)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms=web repro`, replace `lib/main.dart` with the sample below (it calls `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`, so the semantics DOM exists without a screen reader).
2. `flutter build web` and serve `build/web`.
3. Hover the `IconButton` until the tooltip shows.
4. Move the pointer away and wait until the tooltip is gone.
5. Inspect the button's `flt-semantics` element, or run axe-core on the page.

### Expected results

Once the tooltip is hidden and its overlay semantics node is removed from the DOM, the button no longer references it. No `aria-owns` attribute is left behind, or at least none that points to an id that does not exist.

### Actual results

The button keeps `aria-owns` pointing at the removed tooltip node for the rest of the session:

```html
<!-- after the tooltip has been hidden; style attributes trimmed -->
<flt-semantics id="flt-semantic-node-4" role="button" tabindex="0" flt-tappable="" aria-owns="flt-semantic-node-5">New group</flt-semantics>
<!-- document.getElementById('flt-semantic-node-5') === null -->
```

axe-core then reports `aria-valid-attr-value` (impact: critical) on the button. Every page with a Material tooltip fails an automated accessibility audit once a tooltip has been shown.

Measured with Playwright (Chrome 158 headless shell) and axe-core 4.10.3. I left out axe's `document-title` result, which comes from the template and is unrelated.

| State | `aria-owns` on the button | target exists | axe violations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before hover | none | - | none |
| tooltip visible | `flt-semantic-node-5` | yes | `region` (moderate) on `#flt-semantic-node-5` |
| after pointer left | `flt-semantic-node-5` | **no** | `aria-valid-attr-value` (critical) on `#flt-semantic-node-4` |

**Where it seems to come from.** In the web engine, `aria-owns` on the traversal parent is only maintained from the traversal child's own update. `_updateTraversalParent` adds the child id when the child gets a `traversalParent`, and removes it only when that same child later receives an update with `traversalParent == -1`:
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6363fc7e1481e380a9f210d67b58ca9529e27461/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/semantics.dart#L977-L1000

When the tooltip closes, the overlay child is not updated. It is detached and removed in `_finalizeTree`, which disposes it without touching the parent's `aria-owns`:
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6363fc7e1481e380a9f210d67b58ca9529e27461/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/semantics.dart#L3277-L3280

So the id stays on the parent. A possible fix: when a node with `traversalParent != -1` is removed, drop its id from the parent's `aria-owns` (and remove the attribute entirely when the list becomes empty, instead of setting `aria-owns=""`).

The framework side already re-sends the traversal parent on detach (#186118, included in 3.50.0), so this looks engine-only. The code is unchanged on `master` (6363fc7e1481e380a9f210d67b58ca9529e27461); reproduced on 3.50.0 stable.

Related, but not the same symptom:
- #196492: while the tooltip is visible, the same `aria-owns` doubles the button's accessible name. That report notes the stale reference in passing; this issue covers what happens after the tooltip hides.
- #195016: the same detach problem on other embedders (closed without a response).

Our workaround: a small tooltip widget that shows the bubble in a plain `OverlayEntry` wrapped in `ExcludeSemantics` instead of going through `OverlayPortal`. The button carries its own label. `excludeFromSemantics: true` on `Tooltip` does not help. I checked a `Tooltip(message: ..., excludeFromSemantics: true, child: IconButton(...))` variant with the same script, and the wrapper node still ends up with a dangling `aria-owns` and the same critical `aria-valid-attr-value` after the tooltip hides.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const MyApp());
  // Build the semantics DOM without waiting for an assistive technology.
  SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics();
}

class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MyApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: IconButton(
            icon: const Icon(Icons.add),
            tooltip: 'New group',
            onPressed: () {},
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

Nothing changes visually. The evidence is the DOM and the axe output.

</details>

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```console
== before hover
aria-owns: []
axe violations: [document-title]
== tooltip visible
aria-owns: [{"id":"flt-semantic-node-4","role":"button","ariaOwns":"flt-semantic-node-5","missing":[]}]
axe violations: [document-title, {"id":"region","impact":"moderate","nodes":["#flt-semantic-node-5"]}]
== after pointer left

[macOS] Expose NSEvent.clickCount and the system double-click interval to Dart pointer events
body:
### Use case

On desktop, a double click usually means "open" or "edit": a row in a table, a card, a file. An app cannot detect it reliably today. Its only option is to time two presses with its own timeout and its own distance limit.

That falls short of the platform in two ways:

1. **The user's setting is ignored.** macOS lets the user choose the double-click speed (System Settings → Accessibility → Pointer Control). `NSEvent.doubleClickInterval` reports it, and AppKit applies it when it computes `NSEvent.clickCount`. A Flutter app has to hard-code a value instead (for example `kDoubleTapTimeout`, 300 ms, or its own 500 ms). Users with a slow setting, often for accessibility reasons, cannot double-click in Flutter apps the way they can in native ones.
2. **The app has to do the OS's work, and it breaks when the layout moves.** A common pattern is "the first click selects and shows details, the second click opens". If the first click changes the layout (a side panel opens, the list gets narrower, a filter row wraps, the rows move down), the second press lands on a different widget. The app sees two single clicks on two rows. AppKit does not have this problem: it counts clicks by time and position at the event level, before any hit test.

### What happens today

The macOS embedder converts each `NSEvent` into a `FlutterPointerEvent` in `FlutterViewController.mm` (`dispatchMouseEvent:phase:`, around line 703 on Flutter 3.47.2). It passes phase, timestamp, position, device, kind and buttons, but not `event.clickCount`. `FlutterPointerEvent` in `embedder.h` and `PointerData` in `lib/ui/window/pointer_data.h` have no field for it either. So the information is dropped in the engine, and no framework change alone can recover it.

The same applies to Windows (`GetDoubleClickTime`, `WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK`) and to Linux/GTK (`gtk-double-click-time`, `GDK_2BUTTON_PRESS`). macOS is the case I have verified in the source.

### Proposal

- Add a click count to the pointer data: `clickCount` on `PointerDownEvent` / `PointerUpEvent`, filled by each desktop embedder from the platform's own counting (`NSEvent.clickCount` on macOS). Platforms without such a count would report 1.
- Optionally, expose the system double-click interval (for example on `PlatformDispatcher`, like other platform settings), so that framework recognizers can use it instead of `kDoubleTapTimeout`.

With that, an app or `DoubleTapGestureRecognizer` could react to `clickCount == 2` without delaying single clicks and without guessing the timeout.

### Related

- #110300: tap without delay when a double tap is also handled (open)
- #106170: making the 300 ms double-tap delay configurable (open)

These are about the framework's waiting. This issue is about the information the platform already has but the engine does not pass on.

body:
### Steps to reproduce A Flutter Linux app that loads a Rust library through `dart:ffi` crashes when the Rust code captures a backtrace or panics. I ran into it through flutter_rust_bridge, which captures a backtrace for every Rust error, so the first error from Rust closed the app. Repro: https://github.com/Maksim-Nikolaev/flutter-unwinder-repro 1. `flutter create --platforms=linux` and add a tiny Rust `cdylib` (code below) that the app loads with `dart:ffi` at startup. 2. Call `capture_backtrace()`, which runs `std::backtrace::Backtrace::force_capture()`. 3. Or call `panic_and_catch()`, which panics inside `std::panic::catch_unwind`. The repro's `./check.sh` builds the app and runs both cases on a private Xvfb. ### Expected results The backtrace is captured and the panic is caught. The app keeps running. ### Actual results The app crashes in both cases: | Engine library | Rust backtrace | Rust panic in `catch_unwind` | |---|---|---| | Flutter 3.50.0 stock | crash, SIGSEGV | crash, SIGABRT (`failed to initiate panic, error 3`) | | stock + runner links `libgcc_s` first (workaround) | works | works | | engine built with the fix below | works | works | **Why:** `libflutter_linux_gtk.so` links LLVM's libunwind statically and exports some of its `_Unwind_*` functions, but not `_Unwind_Backtrace`. Because the engine library is loaded before `libgcc_s`, a library loaded later ends up with **two unwinders mixed together** (diagram under "Screenshots or Video"). libgcc walks the stack and passes its own context to Rust; Rust reads it with the engine's `_Unwind_GetIP`, which expects LLVM's format, and crashes in `unw_get_reg`. A panic goes to the engine's `_Unwind_RaiseException`, which fails with `_URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR`, so Rust aborts. ```console $ nm -D --defined-only bundle/lib/libflutter_linux_gtk.so | grep _Unwind_ _Unwind_DeleteException _Unwind_ForcedUnwind _Unwind_GetGR _Unwind_GetIP _Unwind_GetLanguageSpecificData _Unwind_GetRegionStart _Unwind_RaiseException _Unwind_Resume _Unwind_SetGR _Unwind_SetIP ``` (plus the `unw_*` API, 31 unwinder symbols in total.) **Workaround** In the app's `linux/runner/CMakeLists.txt`, link `libgcc_s` before the engine so every `_Unwind_*` symbol comes from one unwinder: ```cmake target_link_options(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "LINKER:--no-as-needed" "-lgcc_s" "LINKER:--as-needed") ``` **Possible fix** Keep the statically linked unwinder private. In `engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/BUILD.gn`: ```diff shared_library("flutter_linux_gtk") { deps = [ ":flutter_linux" ] - ldflags = [ "-Wl,-rpath,\$ORIGIN" ] + ldflags = [ + "-Wl,-rpath,\$ORIGIN", + "-Wl,--exclude-libs,libunwind.a", + ] ``` I built the 3.50.0 engine with this change: the library exports no `_Unwind_*` / `unw_*` symbols any more, the app starts with Impeller as usual, and both cases in the repro pass without the workaround. I only tested x86_64. Happy to send a PR if this approach is OK. ### Code sample
Code sample `native/src/lib.rs` (crate type `cdylib`, edition 2021, no dependencies): ```rust use std::backtrace::Backtrace; use std::panic; #[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn capture_backtrace() -> usize { let backtrace = Backtrace::force_capture(); backtrace.to_string().len() } #[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn panic_and_catch() -> i32 { panic::set_hook(Box::new(|_| {})); let result = panic::catch_unwind(|| { panic!("repro panic"); }); match result { Ok(()) => 0, Err(_) => 1, } } ``` `lib/main.dart`: ```dart import 'dart:ffi'; import 'dart:io'; import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart' hide Size; typedef _CaptureBacktrace = Size Function(); typedef _CaptureBacktraceDart = int Function(); typedef _PanicAndCatch = Int32 Function(); typedef _PanicAndCatchDart = int Function(); void main() { runApp(const Center(child: Text('repro', textDirection: TextDirection.ltr))); final bundle = File(Platform.resolvedExecutable).parent.path; final library = DynamicLibrary.open('$bundle/lib/librepro_native.so'); final captureBacktrace = library .lookupFunction<_CaptureBacktrace, _CaptureBacktraceDart>( 'capture_backtrace', ); final panicAndCatch = library .lookupFunction<_PanicAndCatch, _PanicAndCatchDart>('panic_and_catch'); final mode = Platform.environment['REPRO_MODE'] ?? 'backtrace'; if (mode == 'backtrace') { stderr.writeln('REPRO backtrace ok ${captureBacktrace()}'); } else { stderr.writeln( panicAndCatch() == 1 ? 'REPRO panic caught' : 'REPRO panic not caught', ); } exit(0); } ``` Added to `linux/CMakeLists.txt` (after the `FLUTTER_LIBRARY` install): ```cmake set(REPRO_NATIVE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../native") set(REPRO_NATIVE_LIBRARY "${REPRO_NATIVE_DIR}/target/release/librepro_native.so") add_custom_target(repro_native ALL COMMAND cargo build --release --manifest-path "${REPRO_NATIVE_DIR}/Cargo.toml" BYPRODUCTS "${REPRO_NATIVE_LIBRARY}" USES_TERMINAL) add_dependencies(${BINARY_NAME} repro_native) install(FILES "${REPRO_NATIVE_LIBRARY}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}" COMPONENT Runtime) ```

(Backtrace::force_capture)"] rust -- "_Unwind_Backtrace" --> gcc["libgcc_s.so.1

[Android] Autofill structure omits the input type, so password managers do not save obscureText passwords
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On Android, set 1Password as the autofill service (Settings > Passwords, passkeys & accounts > Preferred service).
2. Build a sign-in form: an `AutofillGroup` with a `TextField` (`autofillHints: [AutofillHints.email]`) and a `TextField` (`obscureText: true`, `autofillHints: [AutofillHints.password]`).
3. Type an address and a password, sign in, and call `TextInput.finishAutofillContext()`.
4. Accept 1Password's offer to save the login.

### Expected results

1Password saves the address and the password.

### Actual results

1Password saves the address only; the password is missing.

### Cause

`TextInputPlugin.onProvideAutofillVirtualStructure` reports each field's id, hints, autofill type, visibility, hint text, dimensions and value, but never its input type:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/b34b017b48ad/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/plugin/editing/TextInputPlugin.java#L821-L866

So every Flutter field reaches the autofill service as plain text, `obscureText` included. 1Password requires a password input type before it treats a field as a password. Its staff said so for filling in #105241, which was closed after 1Password worked around the filling side; saving still drops the password. The same method already receives `obscureText` per field (`TextInputChannel.Configuration`), and `inputTypeFromTextInputType` already turns it into `TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_PASSWORD` for the IME (L338-L345).

### Proposed fix

In the per-field loop of `onProvideAutofillVirtualStructure`, after `setAutofillType`:

```java
child.setInputType(
    inputTypeFromTextInputType(
        config.inputType,
        config.obscureText,
        config.autocorrect,
        config.enableSuggestions,
        config.enableIMEPersonalizedLearning,
        config.textCapitalization));
child.setDataIsSensitive(config.obscureText);
```

This is what a native `EditText` with `inputType="textPassword"` reports, so autofill services that key on the input type (1Password does) recognise the field.

### Environment

Pixel 9 Pro, Android 17, 1Password 8.12.46, Flutter 3.47.7 stable; the code above is unchanged on master (b34b017b48ad) and in 3.50.1.

Related: #105241 (1Password filling, closed), #194470 and #196059 (hint text in the same structure).

title: SegmentedButton with direction: Axis.vertical reports horizontal intrinsic sizes
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a `SegmentedButton` with `direction: Axis.vertical` and three segments.
2. Ask its render box for intrinsic sizes, e.g. by wrapping it in `IntrinsicWidth`,
   or in a dialog that measures its content.

### Expected results

For a vertical button, the intrinsic width is the widest segment, and the
intrinsic height is the sum of the segment heights, the same as the size it
actually lays out to.

### Actual results

The four intrinsic methods of `_RenderSegmentedButton`
(`packages/flutter/lib/src/material/segmented_button.dart`) ignore `direction`:
`computeMin/MaxIntrinsicWidth` return `widest * childCount`, and
`computeMin/MaxIntrinsicHeight` return the tallest single segment. Layout itself
is vertical, so the intrinsics disagree with the laid-out size:

| | intrinsic width × height | laid-out size |
|---|---|---|
| 1 segment | 138.6 × 48.0 | 138.6 × 48.0 |
| 3 segments | **415.8 × 48.0** | 138.6 × 144.0 |

As a result, an `IntrinsicWidth` parent (or any dialog that sizes itself from
its content) becomes N times too wide, and an intrinsic height is too short.
This is most visible with large text scales, where the inflated width pushes
the content past the available width.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

Widget buttons(int count) => MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: SegmentedButton<int>(
            key: const Key('segments'),
            direction: Axis.vertical,
            segments: [
              for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
                ButtonSegment(value: i, label: const Text('Choice')),
            ],
            selected: const {0},
            onSelectionChanged: (_) {},
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );

void main() {
  testWidgets('vertical SegmentedButton intrinsics follow its direction', (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(buttons(1));
    final one = tester.renderObject<RenderBox>(find.byKey(const Key('segments')));
    final width1 = one.getMaxIntrinsicWidth(double.infinity);

    await tester.pumpWidget(buttons(3));
    final three = tester.renderObject<RenderBox>(find.byKey(const Key('segments')));
    final width3 = three.getMaxIntrinsicWidth(double.infinity);
    final height3 = three.getMaxIntrinsicHeight(width3);

    expect(width3, closeTo(width1, 0.01));                 // fails: 415.8 vs 138.6
    expect(height3, greaterThanOrEqualTo(three.size.height - 0.01)); // fails: 48 vs 144
  });
}
```

</details>

Visible variant: wrap the button in `IntrinsicWidth(child: …)` inside `Center`;
the outlined button is three times wider than its labels.

### Suggested fix

In the four intrinsic methods, swap the multiplier when
`direction == Axis.vertical`: widths take the maximum without `* childCount`,
heights take the maximum `* childCount` (dividers included as in layout).

### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.47.2 (stable). Same code on `master` as of 2026-11-20.

title: flutter test: any local client that reaches the harness port first becomes the test process ("type '_Map<String, dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'List<dynamic>'")
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create app && cd app`
2. Save `poke.mjs` (Node 24, global `WebSocket`):

   ```js
   const port = process.argv[2];
   const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/`);
   ws.onopen = () => { ws.send(JSON.stringify({hello: "not the tester"})); setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 3000); };
   ```

3. Save `run.sh`, which connects to the harness port as soon as `--verbose` prints it:

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   flutter test --verbose test/widget_test.dart 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do
     echo "$line"
     case "$line" in *"test harness socket server is running at port:"*)
       node poke.mjs "${line##*port:}" & ;;
     esac
   done
   ```

4. `bash run.sh`

### Expected results

The harness accepts only the `flutter_tester` process it spawned. A stray connection is rejected, and the test file loads and passes.

### Actual results

```
Failed to load ".../app/test/widget_test.dart": type '_Map<String, dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'List<dynamic>' in type cast
00:00 +0 -1: Some tests failed.
```

It fails on the first try. Without the poke, the same file passes (`+1: All tests passed!`).

### Why it matters

We hit this signature with no deliberate poke, in full `flutter test --concurrency 4` runs on a busy macOS machine. It shows up as a random "failed to load" on an unrelated file, and it passes when that file is rerun.

`FlutterTesterTestDevice.remoteChannel` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart`, around line 282) takes `await _server!.first` as the tester's connection with no check. The server is bound with `HttpServer.bind(host, 0)`. On macOS we measured a `127.0.0.1:0` bind being handed a port that another process held on `[::1]` only, about 1 in 17,000 binds. That gives a client meant for another process a path onto the harness socket. We have not identified which process connected in the natural sightings.

### Suggested fix

- Pass a per-run random token to the tester (alongside `SERVER_PORT`), and have `remoteChannel` accept only a request whose path carries that token. Reject and keep listening for anything else.
- Separately, when the tester dies after the suite starts, `flutter_platform.dart` reports `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream.`, which hides the tester's real exit reason.

### Flutter version

Flutter 3.47.9, stable, framework `c197ca5199e9ee5661e865596c9c07294dfab51c`. macOS 27.2.1.

title: [Impeller] Short-lived apps using the Vulkan backend never persist the Vulkan shader cache
body:
Impeller's Vulkan backend on Android writes its pipeline cache to disk only once every 50 rasterized frames. Apps that are usually opened briefly may never reach that point, so they never write a pipeline cache, and every launch has to compile pipelines from scratch. This results in much slower startup times for these applications, which becomes even apparent on lower-grade hardware.

We should also persist the Vulkan shader cache on application backgrounding and exit so short-lived apps experience faster subsequent launches.

title: [Impeller] Vulkan pipeline cache can miss async-compiled pipelines because the dirty flag is set on request
body:
In PipelineLibraryVK (impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/pipeline_library_vk.cc), cache_dirty_ is set in GetPipeline when a pipeline is requested, before it's compiled. Compiles are usually asynchronous (compile_queue_ for graphics pipelines, the worker task runner for compute). So the periodic save in DidAcquireSurfaceFrame can run before a requested pipeline has finished compiling:

  1. A pipeline is requested, which sets cache_dirty_ = true and queues the compile.
  2. The 50-frame save runs. It clears cache_dirty_ and reads the Vulkan pipeline cache, which doesn't include the new
  pipeline yet.
  3. The compile finishes and the pipeline is added to the Vulkan pipeline cache, but nothing marks the cache dirty again.

[macOS] Text field semantics label and hint never reach VoiceOver (AXTextField has no title, description or placeholder)
body:
## Summary
On macOS, a Flutter text field is exposed to accessibility clients as an AXTextField with no AXTitle, AXDescription or AXPlaceholderValue, whatever `Semantics(label:)`, `InputDecoration.labelText/hintText` or a placeholder say. VoiceOver announces only "text field" (zh: "文本栏"). The same semantics tree names the field correctly on Windows and in `flutter test` semantics.

## Version
Flutter 3.47.7 (stable), macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6), arm64, Profile build.

## Minimal reproduction
```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: SizedBox(
            width: 300,
            child: Semantics(
              label: 'Add task',
              child: TextField(decoration: InputDecoration(hintText: 'Add task')),
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    ));
```
1. `flutter build macos --profile`, launch.
2. Turn on VoiceOver (or set `AXEnhancedUserInterface` on the app element), read the tree with the Accessibility Inspector or `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue`.
3. The AXTextField has only AXRole, AXRoleDescription, AXValue (the text), AXEnabled, AXFocused; no title, description or placeholder.

Expected: the field's name (`label`, or `hint` as AXPlaceholderValue) as on other platforms.

## Cause (engine)
`shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterTextInputSemanticsObject.mm`: `FlutterTextPlatformNode` returns a hidden `FlutterTextField` (NSTextField) as its native accessible. That class only overrides `setAccessibilityFocused:` and `frame`; `updateString:withSelection:` copies `kValue` into `stringValue`. Nothing copies the node's name (`kName`) or `kPlaceholder`/hint into `accessibilityLabel`/`accessibilityTitle`/`accessibilityPlaceholderValue`. Source: https://api.flutter.dev/macos-embedder/_flutter_text_input_semantics_object_8mm_source.html

Possible fix: in `FlutterTextPlatformNode` (or on each update), set `appkit_text_field_.accessibilityLabel` from the node's name and `accessibilityPlaceholderValue` from its hint.

title: [Android] Platform view hidden under another route replays every queued frame, oldest first, when shown again (ImageReaderSurfaceProducer)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Show a platform view that uses the virtual-display path: an `AndroidView`
   (`PlatformViewsService.initAndroidView`) whose native view is a
   `SurfaceView` drawing continuously or on demand.
2. Push an opaque route on top of it (`MaterialPageRoute`). The platform view
   stays mounted and is still laid out, but is no longer painted.
3. While it is covered, change the size the platform view is laid out at
   several times. In a real app this happens naturally: each time the app is
   left and resumed, the window insets change (the system navigation bar
   comes and goes), so the covered page relays out.
4. Pop the covering route.

The sample below does steps 1–4 with one button.


### Expected results

The platform view shows its current frame at its current size.

### Actual results

The view plays back old frames: frames at the earlier sizes and with old
content, one per frame, oldest first. It looks like the content is shaking or
running backwards.

In a production app (a MapLibre map under a navigation screen), 30
leave/return cycles resized the covered view 113 times. `adb logcat` shows one
`Resize VirtualDisplay flutter-vd#N to W H` per resize. Popping the route then
showed seconds of shaking. When the covered view was held at a fixed size (no
resizes while covered), popping the route showed no shaking.

### Why (from reading the engine source)

`FlutterRenderer.ImageReaderSurfaceProducer`
(`engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/renderer/FlutterRenderer.java`,
line numbers from master as of 20 Nov 2026; the code is the same in 3.41.9):

- `setSize()` (line 866) sets `createNewReader = true` (line 875), so every
  resize gets a new `ImageReader`, appended to `imageReaderQueue`.
- Each `PerImageReader` keeps up to 2 images (line 580).
- `dequeueImage()` (line 686) walks `imageReaderQueue` from the **oldest**
  reader (line 690) and takes one image per frame. A reader is pruned only
  once it is empty (`canPrune`, line 598; `pruneImageReaderQueue`, line 638).
  While images remain, it requests another frame.
- `dequeueImage()` only runs when the texture is painted. A platform view
  under an opaque route, or in an `Offstage` subtree, is not painted, so
  nothing is dequeued while it is hidden and readers pile up. When it is
  painted again, every queued image from every stale reader is shown in
  order before the current one.

### Suggested fix

When dequeuing, skip to the newest reader that has an image and close the
older readers and their images. A stale reader's images are never wanted
once a newer reader has produced a frame. Alternatively, drop older readers'
queued images as soon as a newer reader delivers its first image.

### Workaround

While a platform view is not on screen (`TickerMode` off), a small
`RenderProxyBox` lays it out at its last on-screen size, so `setSize` is
never called while it is hidden. In the frame it is shown again, the real
size is applied.

### Code sample

Minimal project, no plugins: https://github.com/archiemans/flutter_vd_repro

- `CounterView.kt`: a `SurfaceView` drawing about 60 frames a second, with
  an ever-increasing frame number, its surface size and a changing
  background colour.
- `lib/main.dart`: the view in a plain `AndroidView` (virtual display;
  logcat shows `flutter-vd#0`). **Run repro** covers it with an opaque
  `MaterialPageRoute` and shrinks it 40 times, 150 ms apart. All 40 resizes
  reach the engine (`Resize VirtualDisplay flutter-vd#0` × 40, 5 heights).
- After **Back**, the frame number jumps back to earlier values and the size
  flips between the old heights before it counts up again.



### Screenshots or Video

`vd_stale_frames_back.mp4` (attached; also in the repository): live counter, **Run repro**, 40 hidden
resizes, **Back**, then the replay of stale frames.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/232dedce-c3b6-45f6-940b-831e69e1c7ea


### Logs




### Flutter Doctor output

Framework • revision 00b0c91f06 • 2026-04-29
Engine • revision 42d3d75a56
Dart 3.11.5
Device: motorola moto g stylus 5G - 2024, Android 15 (API 35)

[Impeller] iOS: glyphs stay blank for the life of the engine after a GPU restart discards a glyph-atlas upload
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a release build of any Flutter app that shows text on an iPhone (Impeller, Metal; here an iPhone 15 Pro on iOS 27, build installed from TestFlight).
2. Navigate to a screen whose text uses glyphs that were not drawn before (new strings, new size or weight), so Impeller has to upload new glyphs to its glyph atlas in that frame.
3. Have a GPU restart happen during that frame. We cannot trigger one on demand. In our case it was caused by iPhone Mirroring: `avconferenced` (the mirroring encoder) hung the GPU, and the kernel restarted it.
4. Look at the screen, then put the app in the background and bring it back, and scroll the text off screen and back.

In about 50 minutes of testing (9 runs), the GPU restarted once, and that was the only run that showed the bug.

### Expected results

After the GPU restart, the next frames draw every glyph. At worst one frame is wrong.

### Actual results

The glyphs that were being uploaded when the GPU restarted stay blank. This lasts for the life of the engine, on every screen that uses those glyphs (same font, size and subpixel position), even after background/foreground and repaints. Example: « Google » is drawn as « Goo le » and « politique » as « politi ue ». Other glyphs and other screens draw fine. Only killing and relaunching the app fixes it.

At that moment, the device log shows:
- kernel: `IOGPUScheduler` `signalHardwareError`, then `GPURestart`;
- the app's Metal command buffers completing with `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim` (the hang came from `avconferenced`, not from the app).

No `Impeller` line appears in the release log. A cleaned-up log excerpt will follow in a comment.

### Why it never recovers (reading the 3.44.7 sources)

- `TypographerContextSkia::CreateGlyphAtlas` records each new glyph's position in the atlas (step 3a, `AddTypefaceGlyphPositionAndBounds`) before the blit command buffer that uploads its pixels is submitted: [typographer_context_skia.cc#L526-L541](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.7/engine/src/flutter/impeller/typographer/backends/skia/typographer_context_skia.cc#L526-L541) (same thing for a new atlas: [L632-L646](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.7/engine/src/flutter/impeller/typographer/backends/skia/typographer_context_skia.cc#L632-L646)).
- `Context::EnqueueCommandBuffer` only reports whether the submit worked, not whether the buffer ran. On Metal, the completed handler only logs the error and `FML_DCHECK`s it: [command_buffer_mtl.mm#L176-L181](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.7/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/metal/command_buffer_mtl.mm#L176-L181). Nothing tells the glyph atlas that its upload was lost.
- On the next frames, `CollectNewGlyphs` finds those glyphs in the atlas and returns `last_atlas` without uploading again: [L505-L507](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.7/engine/src/flutter/impeller/typographer/backends/skia/typographer_context_skia.cc#L505-L507). When the atlas grows, the old texture, blank areas included, is blitted into the new one.
- On iOS, the `LazyGlyphAtlas` and its contexts live in the `ContentContext` of the single `AiksContext`, created once per `IOSContextMetalImpeller`: [ios_context_metal_impeller.mm#L31](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.7/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/ios_context_metal_impeller.mm#L31). Background/foreground does not reset it. `Rasterizer::NotifyLowMemoryWarning` only cleans a Skia `GrDirectContext`: [rasterizer.cc#L171-L189](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.44.7/engine/src/flutter/shell/common/rasterizer.cc#L171-L189).
- The app cannot work around it. A framework relayout or repaint (for example `PaintingBinding.instance.systemFonts` listeners, then `markNeedsPaint`) asks for the same glyph keys and gets the same blank entries. No API resets the glyph atlas.

Suggested fix: when a command buffer that carries glyph-atlas uploads completes with an error, invalidate that atlas, for example by dropping the `GlyphAtlasContext` or bumping its generation. The next frame then rebuilds it from the glyphs it needs. A reset on an app lifecycle change, or on a low-memory warning, would at least give apps a way to recover.

Related, other backends: #187905 (Vulkan, glyph-atlas corruption under memory pressure) and #193927 (macOS, text smearing while another process keeps the GPU busy).

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: TextPage(index: 0)));

/// Each page draws text at a new size, so every navigation uploads new glyphs.
class TextPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const TextPage({super.key, required this.index});

  final int index;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: Column(
            mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
            children: <Widget>[
              Text(
                'Page $index: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog',
                style: TextStyle(fontSize: 11 + index * 0.5),
              ),
              ElevatedButton(
                onPressed: () => Navigator.of(context).push(
                  MaterialPageRoute<void>(
                    builder: (_) => TextPage(index: index + 1),
                  ),
                ),
                child: const Text('Next'),
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      );
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

The missing letters look like the example under « Actual results ».

### Logs

A cleaned-up excerpt of the device log (kernel `IOGPUScheduler` / `GPURestart` and the app's `InnocentVictim` command-buffer errors) will follow in a comment.

### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.44.7 (stable), engine revision 69c8c61792f0, iOS release build with Impeller on Metal (the only renderer on iOS). Device: iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27.

[camera_avfoundation] Add support for responsive capture on iOS
body:
### Use case

Some apps take several photos in quick succession, for example to catch a moving subject. On iOS, each photo capture goes through capture and then processing, and the next capture waits until the previous photo has finished processing.

Since iOS 17, `AVCapturePhotoOutput` offers responsive capture (`isResponsiveCaptureEnabled`): the next capture can start while the previous photo is still processing. Photos are still delivered in capture order. Apps must opt in to it, it uses more memory in the photo output, and it is supported only while zero-shutter-lag is enabled.

`camera_avfoundation` never sets this property, so apps cannot turn it on.

```
Responsive capture off
  Capture:  [ 1 ]                    [ 2 ]
  Process:       [====== 1 ======]        [====== 2 ======]

Responsive capture on
  Capture:  [ 1 ][ 2 ]
  Process:       [====== 1 ======][====== 2 ======]
```
(illustrative, not to scale)

### Proposal

Add an iOS-only, opt-in API to `AVFoundationCamera`:

- `Future<bool> isResponsiveCaptureSupported(int cameraId)`
- `Future<void> setResponsiveCaptureEnabled(int cameraId, bool enabled)`

Notes:

- Only `camera_avfoundation` changes. Android's CameraX already overlaps capture and processing without a setting, so nothing is needed in `camera_platform_interface` or `camera_android_camerax`.
- It only helps apps that call `CameraPlatform.instance.takePicture` again before the previous call returns, because `CameraController.takePicture` does not allow overlapping calls. Apps check that `CameraPlatform.instance` is an `AVFoundationCamera` before calling it.
- It is off by default, so existing behavior does not change.
- Related: zero-shutter-lag support in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190598.

body:

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

    dependency: "direct main"

```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Visual Studio 2026 (18.6 or newer; reproduced on 18.12.1 with MSVC toolset 14.52.37025).
2. Create a Flutter app that depends on `local_auth: ^3.0.2` (resolves `local_auth_windows 2.0.2`).
3. Run `flutter build windows` or `flutter run -d windows`.

### Expected results

The app builds.

### Actual results

The build fails while compiling the `local_auth_windows` plugin with `error STL1011` (see Logs).

**Cause:** `packages/local_auth/local_auth_windows/windows/CMakeLists.txt` (in 2.0.2 and on `main`) still passes `/await` to both the plugin and the test-runner targets:

```cmake
target_compile_features(${PLUGIN_NAME} PRIVATE cxx_std_20)
target_compile_options(${PLUGIN_NAME} PRIVATE /await)
...
target_compile_options(${TEST_RUNNER} PRIVATE /await)
```

Starting with VS 18.6 / MSVC 14.51, `/await` and `<experimental/coroutine>` are hard errors. The targets already build as C++20, so dropping `/await` should let C++/WinRT use the standard `<coroutine>` header (as permission_handler_windows did in Baseflow/flutter-permission-handler#1569).

Related: #186452 (the general VS 18.6 report, closed because it was about third-party plugins; `local_auth_windows` is first-party) and #185597 (running flutter/packages tests with VS 2026).

**Workaround:** add this to the app's `windows/CMakeLists.txt` before `include(flutter/generated_plugins.cmake)`:

```cmake
add_definitions(-D_SILENCE_EXPERIMENTAL_COROUTINE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS)
```

Or set the environment variable `CL=/D_SILENCE_EXPERIMENTAL_COROUTINE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS`. Microsoft says these headers will be removed, so this only works temporarily.

# pubspec.yaml
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  local_auth: ^3.0.2

No Dart code is needed; the plugin fails to compile.

*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException', reason: '-[AXPlatformNodeCocoa startEditing]: unrecognized selector sent to instance 0x...'

title: TestPlatformDispatcher does not forward setSemanticsTreeEnabled to wrapped PlatformDispatcher
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. In `packages/flutter_test`, `TestPlatformDispatcher` implements `dart:ui`'s `PlatformDispatcher` and documents that it "defers all behavior to the given PlatformDispatcher unless explicitly overridden for test purposes."
2. Construct a `TestPlatformDispatcher` wrapping a `Fake` `PlatformDispatcher` that records `setSemanticsTreeEnabled(bool)` calls (see the code sample below).
3. Call `setSemanticsTreeEnabled(true)` followed by `setSemanticsTreeEnabled(false)` on the `TestPlatformDispatcher` (the same path hit in widget tests when `SemanticsBinding.ensureSemantics()` calls `platformDispatcher.setSemanticsTreeEnabled(...)` through `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`'s `TestPlatformDispatcher`).
4. Run the test and inspect the calls recorded by the wrapped `PlatformDispatcher`.

### Expected results

`TestPlatformDispatcher.setSemanticsTreeEnabled(bool enabled)` forwards calls to the wrapped `PlatformDispatcher`, so the fake dispatcher receives `[true, false]` (and widget tests using `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` forward `SemanticsBinding.ensureSemantics()` / `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` notifications to the wrapped dispatcher).

### Actual results

The test fails with `Actual: []` (and passes when `TestPlatformDispatcher` forwards `setSemanticsTreeEnabled`).

Background and cause:
- `PlatformDispatcher.setSemanticsTreeEnabled` was added in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/161265 (merged 2025-03-24) so the framework can notify the engine/platform when semantics generation starts or stops, implementing the contract from related issue https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/158399 (closed; mobile embeddings were fixed there).
- `TestPlatformDispatcher` never received an explicit `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` override (`git log -S setSemanticsTreeEnabled -- packages/flutter_test` shows no prior commit).
- Unimplemented `PlatformDispatcher` members on `TestPlatformDispatcher` fall through to `noSuchMethod`, which returns `null` with the comment: `"This gives us some grace time when the dart:ui side adds something to [PlatformDispatcher], and makes things easier when we do rolls to give us time to catch up."` Calls to `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` are therefore silently swallowed and never reach the wrapped `PlatformDispatcher`.
- Because `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` wraps the real `PlatformDispatcher` in `TestPlatformDispatcher`, `SemanticsBinding.ensureSemantics()` / `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` calls in widget tests are also swallowed before reaching the wrapped dispatcher.
- Existing tests in `packages/flutter/test/semantics/semantics_binding_set_semantics_tree_enabled_test.dart` use a `TestPlatformDispatcherSpy` that overrides `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` without calling `super`, so they did not detect the missing forwarder.
- As precedent for other `PlatformDispatcher` wrappers, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/194311 (merged 2026-10-30) forwards `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` in `_DebugViewMetricsPlatformDispatcher` in `packages/flutter/lib/src/foundation/debug.dart`, but did not address `TestPlatformDispatcher`.

This issue covers only the missing `setSemanticsTreeEnabled` forwarding override in `packages/flutter_test`'s `TestPlatformDispatcher`.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'dart:ui'

title: [flutter_tools] Add -n and -N short flags to flutter test
body:
Passing `-n <regexp>` or `-N <substring>` to `flutter test` exits with `Could not find an option with short name "-n"`, unlike `dart test` ([`test.dart#L146-L158`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart#L146-L158)). Both short flags are unused on `flutter test`, which already mirrors `dart test`'s `-t`, `-x`, `-P`, `-j`, and `-r` abbreviations.

```console
$ flutter test -n smoke
Could not find an option with short name "-n".
```

Developers and coding agents switching between `dart test` and `flutter test` routinely pass `-n` and `-N` to filter a single failing test, burning an extra invocation on exit code `64`.

### Proposed solution

- Add `abbr: 'n'` to `TestCommand._name` and `abbr: 'N'` to `TestCommand._plainName` in [`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart#L146-L158).
- Keep `--platform` without `-p`, since `--platform` on `flutter test` is internal and `verboseOnly` ([`test.dart#L272-L285`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart#L272-L285)).

title: [flutter_tools] flutter test TCP loopback bind fails in sandboxes
body:
Running `flutter test --no-pub` in a network-isolated sandbox fails to load every test suite with a socket error ([`flutter_tester_device.dart#L87-L90`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart#L87-L90)). Even with `--disable-vm-service`, `FlutterTesterTestDevice.start` binds a TCP `HttpServer` on `127.0.0.1:0` for local WebSocket IPC with `flutter_tester`. - **macOS Seatbelt (`sandbox-exec`, e.g. Claude Code's built-in sandbox)**: `HttpServer.bind(host, 0)` ([`flutter_tester_device.dart#L284`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart#L284)) fails immediately with `Failed to load "": Failed to create server socket (OS Error: Operation not permitted, errno = 1)`. - **Linux network namespaces (`unshare -rn` without `lo` brought up)**: the generated test listener ([`flutter_platform.dart#L286-L294`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_platform.dart#L286-L294)) fails in `WebSocket.connect` with `SocketException: Connection failed (OS Error: Network is unreachable, errno = 101), address = 127.0.0.1`. - **Impact**: Sandboxed coding agents on macOS and Linux cannot execute offline widget or unit tests (`flutter test --no-pub`) without disabling the sandbox.
Detailed reproduction & CLI output (Linux unshare -rn and macOS Seatbelt) 1. Create a minimal Flutter package (`flutter create --offline --template=package p && cd p`). 2. Run `flutter test --no-pub` inside an unconfigured Linux network namespace: ```console $ unshare -rn flutter test --no-pub 00:00 +0: loading /tmp/p/test/p_test.dart Shell: [ERROR:flutter/shell/testing/tester_main.cc(622)] Unhandled exception Shell: Exception: SocketException: Connection failed (OS Error: Network is unreachable, errno = 101), address = 127.0.0.1, port = 45103 Shell: Stack trace: #0 _NativeSocket.startConnect (dart:io-patch/socket_patch.dart:849:35) ``` 3. On macOS under a Seatbelt profile that denies `AF_INET` `network-bind` (such as Claude Code `2.1.x` on Flutter `3.50.0` stable): ```text Failed to load "/foo_test.dart": Failed to create server socket (OS Error: Operation not permitted, errno = 1) ```
### Possible directions - Both endpoints of `SERVER_PORT` ([`flutter_tester_device.dart#L138`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart#L138) and [`flutter_platform.dart#L287`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_platform.dart#L287)) are pure Dart inside `flutter_tools` (`flutter_tester` C++ does not consume `SERVER_PORT`). - On POSIX when no explicit TCP port is requested—preserving pre-allocated TCP port support ([`flutter_tester_device.dart#L94-L103`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart#L94-L103)) and TCP on Windows—use a Unix domain socket (`InternetAddressType.unix`) in a temp directory (or fall back to `AF_UNIX` when `AF_INET` `bind` throws `SocketException`), verifying compatibility with macOS Seatbelt `TMPDIR` socket rules.

title: [flutter_tools] shared.sh warns about root on bin/dart and containers
body:
Running `flutter` or Flutter's `bin/dart` as `root` inside a non-Docker container prints a four-line superuser warning on every command ([`bin/internal/shared.sh#L221-L227`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/bin/internal/shared.sh#L221-L227)). Because [`bin/dart`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/afad7960e1f4dafdb28a4c45e5e001d4a1994000/bin/dart#L56-L59) shares the `flutter` launcher script, even plain `dart <script.dart>` warns about `"trying to run flutter as root"`.

- **Container and agent gap**: `shared.sh` only suppresses the check when `/.dockerenv` exists or `CI`, `BOT`, or `CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION` equals `"true"`. Non-Docker root environments—Podman (`/run/.containerenv`), systemd containers (`$container`), gVisor, Firecracker microVMs, and cloud coding-agent sandboxes that set `CLAUDECODE`, `AI_AGENT`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `GEMINI_CLI`, or `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`—print the Clippy banner on every command.
- **Impact**: Tool harnesses that merge `stderr` into `stdout` (or callers using `2>&1`) get four warning lines prepended to every `dart` and `flutter` invocation, polluting script output and burning context on routine CLI calls.

### Steps to reproduce

```console
$ unshare -r bash -c 'CLAUDECODE=1 AI_AGENT=claude-code flutter/bin/dart --version'
   Woah! You appear to be trying to run flutter as root.
   We strongly recommend running the flutter tool without superuser privileges.
  /
📎
Dart SDK version: 3.15.0-162.0.dev (dev) (Wed Nov 18 12:11:42 2026 -0800) on "linux_x64"
```

### Proposed fix

- Skip the superuser warning when `$BIN_NAME == "dart"` (the warning explicitly says `"trying to run flutter as root"`).
- Broaden container detection beyond `/.dockerenv` to include `/run/.containerenv` and non-empty `${container:-}` (superseding stale-closed #55982).
- Suppress the warning when known coding-agent environment variables (`AI_AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `GEMINI_CLI`, `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`, `CURSOR_AGENT`) are set, matching `AiAgent` detection in `package:unified_analytics`.

title: [Impeller][GLES][Android] SIGSEGV in raster thread (BlitCopyBufferToTextureCommandGLES → DeviceBufferGLES::OnGetContents) when activity resumes over keyguard
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Android device where Impeller falls back to OpenGL ES (Vulkan blocked by `IsKnownBadDriver`, e.g. Adreno ≤ 650). Seen on a Redmi Note 9 Pro (Adreno 618), Android 10 (MIUI 12, build QKQ1.191215.002).
2. App's `FlutterActivity` (single-top) is in the foreground; the user turns the screen off, so the lock screen shows and the activity is stopped (surface destroyed).
3. An exact alarm fires a full-screen intent to the same activity. In `onNewIntent` the app calls `setShowWhenLocked(true)` and `setTurnScreenOn(true)`, and the Dart side builds a screen with new text.
4. The activity goes `onStart → onResume → onPause` (~30 ms later, from the keyguard occlusion transition) `→ onResume`.

### Expected results

The screen renders over the lock screen.


### Actual results

About 0.5 s after the second `onResume` the process crashes in the raster thread. It happened 3 out of 3 times with Impeller (two real alarms and one scripted test), and 0 out of 2 times with `io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableImpeller=false` (Skia), with the same lifecycle sequence.

```
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR), fault addr 0x0
Cause: null pointer dereference
pid: …, tid: …, name: 1.raster
backtrace:
  #00 pc 0000000001acc03c  base.apk!libflutter.so (BuildId: 64ede5cb2d018bf680e567c192e6b5ae69822df1)
  #01 pc 0000000001ee3a38  base.apk!libflutter.so (BuildId: 64ede5cb2d018bf680e567c192e6b5ae69822df1)
```

These are from the debug engine (engine 371f77202a73e8dff57a8b3bff75bca55c090aee). We mapped the frames by hand by disassembling around the pcs and matching string references against `impeller/renderer/backend/gles/blit_command_gles.cc`:

- `#01` is in `BlitCopyBufferToTextureCommandGLES::Encode`, at the virtual call `source.GetBuffer()->OnGetContents()`. It comes right after the `GetGLHandle()` check ("Texture was collected before it could be uploaded to the GPU.") and `gl.BindTexture`.
- `#00` is an identical-code-folded `ldr x0,[x0]; ret` getter: `DeviceBufferGLES::OnGetContents()` tail-calls `backing_store_->GetBuffer()` with `backing_store_ == nullptr`. The trailing frame was lost to the tail call.

`OnGetContents()` checks `reactor_` but not `backing_store_`, and `AllocatorGLES::OnCreateBuffer` never stores a null allocation. So the source `DeviceBufferGLES` looks freed (use-after-free) by the time the reactor runs the blit.

Suspected cause: GLES blits are recorded as reactor operations (`BlitPassGLES::OnEncodeCommands` → `reactor_->AddOperation`) and run later, when a context is current. The glyph-atlas upload in `typographer_context_skia.cc` uses a `BufferView` from `data_host_buffer.Emplace(...)`. That view holds a raw (non-owning) `DeviceBuffer*`, and `HostBuffer::Reset()` pops unused per-frame device buffers. While the surface is gone and comes back across the stop/start/pause/resume flap, the deferred upload seems to outlive the host-buffer chunk it points into.

Flutter 3.50.1 has no changes under `impeller/` (checked the 3.50.0...3.50.1 compare), so it's presumably still affected.

### Code sample

There's no minimal sample yet. The trigger is a `FlutterActivity` with `showWhenLocked`/`turnScreenOn` set from `onNewIntent` by an alarm full-screen intent while the screen is off, on an Impeller-GLES device, with the new route showing fresh text. Happy to try a minimal repro if needed.


### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

[Upload media here]

</details>


### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```console
[Paste your logs here]
```

</details>


### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.50.0 • channel stable • framework ab2912035e (2026-11-09) • engine bf601093ad (revision 371f77202a) • Dart 3.14.0
Device: Redmi Note 9 Pro (joyeuse), Android 10 (API 29), Adreno 618, Impeller backend: OpenGL ES (Vulkan blocked by driver_info_vk.cc)
```

Workaround in use: `<meta-data android:name="io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableImpeller" android:value="false" />`. The Impeller opt-out deprecation message asks to report a bug, so this is that report.

Only the family the app draws is worth shipping. The other two should be subset to a
few KB — as they are in the Android build of the same project — or left out entirely,
and should not be listed in FontManifest.json.

### Actual results



MaterialSymbolsOutlined.ttf   10,643,396 -> 3,760        (the family used)
MaterialSymbolsRounded.ttf    15,073,408 -> 15,073,408   (unchanged)
MaterialSymbolsSharp.ttf       8,841,308 ->  8,841,308   (unchanged)

All three are still listed in build/web/assets/FontManifest.json, and on web the
engine downloads every family in that manifest at startup
(_engine/engine/initialization.dart -> _downloadAssetFonts() ->
loadAssetFonts(fetchFontManifest(...)); the skwasm implementation downloads every
FontAsset of every family). So 23.4 MB of icons the app can never draw is fetched on
first paint, and it is in the bundle besides.

flutter build apk --release of the same project subsets all three families to 2-4 KB.
The difference: the package keeps a reference to each family inside a
@pragma('vm:entry-point') method that the app never calls
(Symbols.forceCompileTimeTreeShaking), so the shaker can see them. Android's
recording honours those references; the web one does not.

That it really is the shaking and not a flag that silently did nothing:
- the same web build does rewrite the used font (10.6 MB -> 3.7 KB) and MaterialIcons;
- the tool prints one "Font asset ... was tree-shaken" line per font it subsets and
  prints none for the other two;
- the two shipped files are byte-identical (sha256) to the package's own files;
- with --no-tree-shake-icons all three ship full and no line is printed;
- Android subsets those same two families from the same package.

```dart

import 'package:material_symbols_icons/symbols.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const Directionality(
    textDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
    child: Center(child: Icon(Symbols.star)), // Outlined family only
  ));
}
```

Full project: https://github.com/cedvdb/flutter-web-icon-tree-shaking-repro
It also has a package-free variant (local_package/) that shows the same shipping
behaviour with no third-party code.

Unregistered-instance in the main isolate on iOS and Android with multiple engines (after #194920 fix)
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

shared_preferences

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

iOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock (relevant entries)</summary>

```yaml
shared_preferences: 2.5.6
shared_preferences_android: 2.5.5
shared_preferences_foundation: 2.6.2
workmanager: 0.10.10
workmanager_apple: 0.9.11
flutter_local_notifications: 22.3.3
firebase_messaging: 17.0.1
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

Seen twice, on both platforms. I have no deterministic repro yet.

**iOS (production, App Store build):**

1. Use the legacy `SharedPreferences` API in an app that also starts additional Flutter engines in the same process: `workmanager` background tasks, `flutter_local_notifications` background notification actions (`onDidReceiveBackgroundNotificationResponse`) and `firebase_messaging`.
2. The app is launched by the system in the background (lifecycle `inactive`, not in foreground), so a background engine may register plugins around the same time as the main engine.
3. Call `SharedPreferences.getInstance()` / `reload()` in the main isolate during startup.

**Android (emulator, debug build):**

1. Same app, first build and install on a freshly started emulator.
2. Every `SharedPreferences` call in the main isolate failed (several independent reads through `reload()`, and a `setBool` write). The app kept running.
3. After the app was restarted, the error did not come back.

In both cases the failure lasted for the whole process lifetime and went away after an app restart. This looks like a remaining case of #194920, whose fix (flutter/packages#13576, released in `shared_preferences_android` 2.5.5 and `shared_preferences_foundation` 2.6.2 via flutter/packages#13617) is already included in the versions above.

### Expected results

The main isolate keeps using the registration made by its own engine, and preferences calls keep working regardless of other engines starting or detaching.


### Actual results

Every preferences call in the main isolate throws, until the app is restarted.

iOS:

```
PlatformException(unregistered-instance, LegacyUserDefaultsApi has not been registered., null, null)
```

Android:

```
PlatformException(unregistered-instance, SharedPreferencesApi has not been registered., null, io.flutter.plugins.sharedpreferences.FlutterError: SharedPreferencesApi has not been registered.
```

On iOS all four call sites hit at startup failed in the same second (`SharedPreferences.reload`, reads and writes).

Suspected cause, from reading the iOS 2.6.2 sources (I assume the Android side behaves the same way, since both are generated by the same Pigeon version):

- `SharedPreferencesFoundation._api` is a `late final`, so `LegacyUserDefaultsApiForNativeInterop.getInstance()` resolves the native `LegacyUserDefaultsApiSetup` wrapper once and keeps it for the lifetime of the isolate.
- `pigeonResolveInstance(engineId:affinityKey:)` falls back to `list.last` (the most recent registration) when `PlatformDispatcher.instance.engineId` is null or does not match any registration. If a background engine registered after the main engine, the main isolate can pick up the background engine's wrapper.
- When that background engine is torn down, `detachFromEngine` calls `unregister`, which sets `entry.api = nil` on that wrapper. The main isolate still holds the same wrapper, so `resolveApi()` throws `unregistered-instance` on every call. Only a restart (new isolate, new resolution) clears it, which matches what we saw on both platforms.

Possible fixes: re-resolve the instance when the cached wrapper has been unregistered (instead of caching it forever), and/or never fall back to another engine's registration when the current engine id is known but not yet registered.

### Code sample

<details><summary>Code sample</summary>

No minimal repro yet. The failing calls are plain legacy API calls in the main isolate:

```dart
final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
await prefs.reload();
await prefs.setBool('some_flag', true);
```

</details>

title: TextPainter.layout never returns (infinite loop in SkParagraph TextLine::justify) for TextAlign.justify + ellipsis + maxLines ≥ 2 + a ligature at a narrow width
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create bug --platforms=windows` (any platform; also reproduces in `flutter test`).
2. Bundle a font that has an `fi` ligature. I used Inter (OFL, https://github.com/rsms/inter), `Inter[opsz,wght].ttf`, as an asset with family `Inter`.
3. Replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below and run it.

The trigger is a `TextPainter` (or `Text`) with all of:
- a text containing U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI: `'fiﬁΩÅ'`;
- `TextAlign.justify`;
- `ellipsis: '…'`;
- `maxLines: 2`;
- a width narrower than one glyph cluster: `layout(minWidth: 10.5, maxWidth: 10.5)`.

It was found by a fuzzer for text layout.

### Expected results

`layout` returns, and the app prints `DONE` and exits, as it does when any one of the conditions above is removed.

### Actual results

`layout` never returns. The UI thread spins in native code at 100 % CPU, so the app freezes for good. Because the loop is synchronous and native, no Dart timeout or watchdog can stop it.

Each case was run in its own process (`flutter test --plain-name <case>`) with a 120 s timeout:

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| justify + ellipsis + maxLines 2 + `ﬁ`, with a forced `StrutStyle` | hangs |
| the same without a strut | hangs |
| `TextAlign.start` instead of justify | returns `Size(10.5, 38.0)` |
| `ellipsis: null` | returns `Size(10.5, 38.0)` |
| text without U+FB01 (`'fiΩÅ'`) | returns `Size(10.5, 38.0)` |

Earlier fuzz runs also showed that `maxLines: 1` or `null`, or a plain word, does not hang.

Native stack of the UI thread in a Windows profile build. It is the same in two dumps taken 20 s and 30 s into the hang, symbolized with the engine's `flutter_windows.dll.pdb`:

```
skia::textlayout::TextLine::iterateThroughClustersInGlyphsOrder::<lambda_13>::operator()  TextLine.cpp:953
skia::textlayout::TextLine::iterateThroughClustersInGlyphsOrder                           TextLine.cpp:944
skia::textlayout::TextLine::justify                                                        TextLine.cpp:442
skia::textlayout::ParagraphImpl::formatLines                                               ParagraphImpl.cpp:704
skia::textlayout::ParagraphImpl::layout                                                    ParagraphImpl.cpp:217
… dart::DartEntry::InvokeFunction
```

My guess is that justify walks the clusters of an ellipsized line, the ligature makes one glyph cover two clusters, and the walk never advances. I have not checked this against the Skia source.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

`pubspec.yaml` (add to the `flutter:` section):

```yaml
  fonts:
    - family: Inter
      fonts:
        - asset: fonts/Inter.ttf   # Inter[opsz,wght].ttf from https://github.com/rsms/inter
```

`lib/main.dart`:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  stdout.writeln('layout start');
  final TextPainter painter = TextPainter(
    text: const TextSpan(
      text: 'fiﬁΩÅ', // contains U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI
      style: TextStyle(fontFamily: 'Inter', fontSize: 16),
    ),
    textDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
    textAlign: TextAlign.justify,
    maxLines: 2,
    ellipsis: '…',
    textWidthBasis: TextWidthBasis.longestLine,
  );
  painter.layout(minWidth: 10.5, maxWidth: 10.5); // never returns
  stdout.writeln('DONE ${painter.size}');
  painter.dispose();
  exit(0);
}
```

title: Android] Autofill suggestions do not show when a TextField gets focus during a route transition and a `PageView` animation: the app must wait for the animations before requesting focus
`_buildSemanticsSubtree` null check on `geometry!` for a ListView's `_RenderScrollSemantics` under an offstage route, then `'node.built'` on every frame
body:
## Steps to reproduce

Intermittent. It needs accessibility semantics enabled (iOS Simulator with
`ApplicationAccessibilityEnabled = 1`; no VoiceOver needed).

1. Route A shows a vertical `ListView` (`ListView.separated`). Its items are a
   `PageView` carousel with an auto-advance `Timer`, and rows of horizontal
   `SingleChildScrollView`s. Those rows hold cards with `CachedNetworkImage`
   images and looping `video_player` previews that start and stop with
   `VisibilityDetector`.
2. Scroll the `ListView` down.
3. Tap a card to push an opaque `MaterialPageRoute` (route B, a full-screen
   video). Pop it, then push it again.
4. After a few push/pop cycles, the exception below is thrown during a frame.

I have not been able to reduce this to a minimal sample yet. A simplified
widget test with `ensureSemantics()`, a scrolled `ListView`, a `PageView`
carousel and push/pop did not reproduce it.

## Expected results

No exception from `PipelineOwner.flushSemantics`.

## Actual results

```
Null check operator used on a null value
#0  _RenderObjectSemantics._buildSemanticsSubtree (package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart:6329:61)
#1  _RenderObjectSemantics.ensureSemanticsNode (package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart:6259:7)
#2  PipelineOwner.flushSemantics (package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart:1642:18)
#3  PipelineOwner.flushSemantics (package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart:1659:15)
#4  RendererBinding.drawFrame (package:flutter/src/rendering/binding.dart:699:25)
```

Column 61 is `geometry!` in
`(!(parentData?.mergeIntoParent ?? false) && geometry!.hidden)`.

Because the flush aborts, every later frame fails with:

```
'package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart': Failed assertion: line 5738 pos 12: 'node.built': is not true.
#2  _RenderObjectSemantics.debugCheckForBuilds (package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart:5738:12)
#5  PipelineOwner.flushSemantics.<anonymous closure> (package:flutter/src/rendering/object.dart:1648:34)
```

The node left unbuilt is the root app `Semantics` (`RenderSemanticsAnnotations`
under `WidgetsApp`).

## What I found with temporary logging in `object.dart`

- **The failing node** is the `_RenderScrollSemantics` of route A's `ListView`
  (`_ScrollSemantics ← Scrollable ← ListView ← ...`). Its ancestor chain passes
  through `RenderOffstage` under `_Theater`, so route A is the covered route.
- **Its state at the throw** was `built=true`, `parentDataDirty=false`,
  `geometryDirty=true`, `geometry == null`, `isRoot=false`, relayout boundary
  `up1`.
- **What clears the geometry:** only
  `_RenderObjectSemantics._clearImmediateChildrenGeometry`, called from the
  geometry loop in `PipelineOwner.flushSemantics` (`object.dart:1570`). This
  happens every few seconds while the list is on screen.
- **Timing:** in the captured run, the last clear was at 13:35:41.9 and the
  throw at 13:35:58.4. So the node kept `geometry == null` for about 16 s
  without `ensureGeometry` recomputing it. I think this is because its branch
  had no clean ancestor while route A was offstage.
- **How it becomes a target:** `ensureSemanticsNode` is called on this node
  directly, with no `_buildSemantics` frame in between. In `flushSemantics`
  that only happens through `targets`:
  - either the node itself, which needs `geometryDirty == false`;
  - or a cached `firstAncestorNodeWithCleanGeometry`.

  So it looks like the target came from a `firstAncestorNodeWithCleanGeometry`
  that `computeAncestorInfo` had cached with the same `treeShapeToken`, even
  though the node's geometry was null when it was used. Pending
  `_deferredNodesNeedingSemanticsGeometryUpdate` may be part of it too.
- **What precedes the throw:** in the ~15 ms before it, every `Image` under the
  list (from `CachedNetworkImage` / `OctoImage` and `FadeWidget`) gets
  `markNeedsSemanticsUpdate` through `Semantics.updateRenderObject`. Route A is
  onstage at that point, so this seems to be the push/pop frame.

This looks like it could be in the same area as #190431 (rebuild a semantics
fragment when its sibling conflict changes) and #189902. That fix is in
3.50.0, and this still happens.

## Code sample

No minimal sample yet (see above). Happy to test a patch or add more logging.

## Flutter Doctor output

```
Flutter 3.50.0 • https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git
Framework • revision ab2912035e • 2026-11-09
Engine • revision 371f77202a
Tools • Dart 3.14.0 • DevTools 2.61.0
Device: iPhone 17 Pro Simulator, iOS 26.5
```

title: [web][skwasm] SkwasmParagraphBuilder.build intermittently decodes invalid UTF-8; layout aborts and later hit tests throw
body:
### Steps to reproduce

I can't reproduce this on demand, but it shows up in production error reports. The app is a Flutter web app built with `flutter build web --wasm` (release, skwasm), and it serves Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean text, so it relies heavily on the engine's CJK font fallback.

Since we began collecting web error reports, these are the counts from the last few days. There were about 45 reports from 7 users, all on desktop Chrome 150–158 or Edge 156–157, on Windows and macOS. None came from Android Chrome, which also runs skwasm, or from Safari/Firefox, which run the JS build.

Attempts that did **not** reproduce it:
- Lone UTF-16 surrogates in `Text`. The text just isn't drawn, and nothing throws.
- A stress test that lays out about 1,600 random CJK, Hangul and emoji characters in 80 `Text`s every 40 ms for 600 frames, while the font fallbacks download.
- Clicking and hovering through the real app in a debug `--wasm` build.

### Expected results

Building a paragraph never yields invalid UTF-8, and layout completes.

### Actual results

There are three related symptoms. All of them point at the skwasm side.

**1. `SkwasmParagraphBuilder.build` decodes invalid UTF-8 during layout.** `paragraphBuilderGetUtf8Text` returns bytes that `utf8.decode` rejects in `_addSegmenterData` (`skwasm_impl/paragraph.dart:973`). The text being laid out is ordinary app text. One case was a static string on the app's loading screen, not user data. Stack, with names restored from the unstripped `main.dart.wasm`:

```
FormatException: Missing extension byte (at offset 1)
    at Utf8Decoder.convert

These look like native exceptions crossing the wasm boundary. Separately, one report was `RuntimeError: Aborted()` from `_abort_js` in `skwasm.js`, called from Dart code.

Taken together, this looks like skwasm's linear memory getting corrupted, so a paragraph builder's UTF-8 text buffer is read back as garbage. I haven't been able to find the trigger. If there's a debug or assertions build of skwasm we could ship to catch it, I'm happy to try that.

}

title: [web] Keyboard insets always 0 with hostElement embedding; fields/sheets hidden behind keyboard in Android WebView (WhatsApp in-app browser)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a Flutter web app embedded with `hostElement` (a `position: fixed; inset: 0` div, e.g. `#flutter-host`) via `flutter.js` `engineInitializer.initializeEngine({ hostElement })`.
2. Add a screen with a `TextField` near the bottom, or a bottom sheet containing a `TextField`.
3. Open the deployed page inside an Android WebView-based in-app browser (for example, a link tapped inside a WhatsApp chat).
4. Tap the text field so the soft keyboard opens.

### Expected results

The focused field or sheet stays visible above the keyboard. `MediaQuery.viewInsets.bottom` reflects the keyboard height, so `Scaffold` and bottom sheets move up. This is what happens in Chrome and Safari (Android and iOS).

### Actual results

The field or sheet stays behind the keyboard and the user cannot see what they type.

Android WebView shrinks the whole WebView when the keyboard opens. `window.innerHeight`, the host element and `visualViewport` all shrink together. Chrome and Safari keep the host at full height and shrink only `visualViewport`.

From reading the engine source (3.38.2):
- `CustomElementDimensionsProvider.computeKeyboardInsets` (hostElement embedding) always returns zero, so `viewInsets` stays 0.
- `EngineFlutterView._didResize` keeps the old `_physicalSize` while a text field is being edited on mobile, and expects `computeKeyboardInsets` to report the keyboard.

Together, Flutter keeps laying out at the old, taller height and draws below the visible WebView area. Plain HTML on the same page reflows correctly in the same WebView, so only Flutter content is affected.

### Workaround we use

Compute the inset ourselves as `flutterLayoutHeight - (visualViewport.offsetTop + visualViewport.height)`, where the layout height comes from the implicit view's `RenderView.configuration.logicalConstraints.maxHeight`. We re-sync on `didChangeMetrics` so the inset is not double-counted if Flutter later lays out at the shorter height. Measuring against `host.clientHeight` instead gives 0 in Android WebView, because the host shrinks too. This relies on engine internals and may break on upgrades.

Possible related edge case (unverified): closing the keyboard with Android Back while the field stays focused may leave Flutter laid out at the shorter height until the next host resize.

### Suggested fix

- Report correct keyboard insets in `CustomElementDimensionsProvider.computeKeyboardInsets` when the host/WebView itself shrinks.
- Handle host resizes while a text field is focused on mobile web, so the view does not keep a stale size.

### Local repro in Chrome (no WhatsApp needed)

Android Chrome with `interactive-widget=resizes-content` added to the viewport meta tag resizes the page like a WebView does. Remote-debug with `adb reverse` and `chrome://inspect`.

### Environment

- Flutter 3.38.2 (stable), web (HTML host element embedding)
- Failing: Android WebView-based in-app browser (WhatsApp)
- Working: Android Chrome, iOS Safari, iOS Chrome, iOS WhatsApp (WKWebView)

### Related

Please link or thumbs-up any existing issues about web keyboard insets / `viewInsets` in embedded mode if found during triage.
