[Windows] two tooltips merged into one semantics node, 2nd one's bubble is an orphan
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. windows, with an accessibility client running (Narrator, or anything else that keeps UI Automation on for the app).
2. run the code sample below (`flutter run -d windows`).
3. hover over `B` and wait for its tooltip to show.

### Expected results

no errors, and tooltip B's bubble is in the accessibility tree.

### Actual results

the console repeats this once per frame while the bubble fades in and out:

```
[ERROR:flutter/shell/platform/common/accessibility_bridge.cc(114)] Failed to update ui::AXTree, error: <id> will not be in the tree and is not the new root
```

tooltip A's bubble works fine.

### Cause, as far as I traced it

this is related to #182444. same error, different path: there the bubble gets detached inside a `ListView`.

each `Tooltip` is an `OverlayPortal`, and it wraps its child in `Semantics(traversalParentIdentifier: this)`. the bubble in the overlay carries the matching `traversalChildIdentifier`. on non-web platforms the bubble gets grafted under whichever node holds the parent identifier.

so what happens when both tooltips' configurations land in one semantics node? (here that's the `GestureDetector`'s tap node.) `SemanticsConfiguration.absorb()` keeps only the first identifier:

```dart
if (_traversalChildIdentifier == null) {
  _traversalParentIdentifier ??= child._traversalParentIdentifier;
}
```

that leaves tooltip B's bubble with no traversal parent. `_childrenInHitTestOrder()` drops it, and it isn't in any `childrenInTraversalOrder` either. but it's still dirty and still gets sent with `_addToUpdate()`.. so the update holds a node that no parent lists.

i also checked this in a widget test. with B's tooltip shown, a node with `traversalChildIdentifier` is attached (`visitChildren()` from the root finds it), but you can't reach it through `debugListChildrenInOrder(DebugSemanticsDumpOrder.traversalOrder)`. show A instead, or wrap B in `Semantics(container: true)`, and no such node is left.

workaround: give each tooltip its own semantics node, `Semantics(container: true, child: Tooltip(...))`. it works, but it's kinda something you shouldn't have to know about.

### Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(
  MaterialApp(
    home: Scaffold(
      body: Center(
        child: GestureDetector(
          onTap: () {},
          child: const Row(
            mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
            children: [
              Tooltip(message: 'first', child: Text('A')),
              SizedBox(width: 40),
              Tooltip(message: 'second', child: Text('B')),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    ),
  ),
);
```

### Flutter version

Flutter 3.50.0 stable (framework ab2912035e, engine 371f77202a), Dart 3.14.0, `material_ui` 1.11.0, Windows 11.

thanks for looking into it : )

[web] Undisposed images leak ImageSource and Pictures leak on GC
body:
Garbage-collecting an undisposed [`EngineImage`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/primitives/image.dart#L23-L52) or [`_StaticEngineCodec`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/primitives/codec.dart#L203-L235) never calls `imageSource.release()`, leaking DOM `ImageBitmap` and `` memory on CanvasKit and single-threaded Skwasm. Separately, constructor closures in [`SkwasmPicture`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/skwasm/skwasm_impl/picture.dart#L11-L20) and image-bearing [`CkPicture`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/picture.dart#L23-L33) instances capture `this` inside `UniqueRef`, preventing `FinalizationRegistry` from collecting undisposed pictures. - **`EngineImage` and `_StaticEngineCodec` omit GC `ImageSource` release**: [`EngineImage`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/primitives/image.dart#L23-L52) retains `imageSource` per wrapper and clone (including [`EngineImageShader` clones](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/primitives/shader.dart#L273-L275)), while `CountedRef.onDispose` only disposes `BackendImage`. [`_StaticEngineCodec`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/primitives/codec.dart#L203-L235) lacks a `UniqueRef` finalizer altogether and lacks an `if (_disposed) return;` guard in `dispose()`. - **`FinalizationRegistry` `heldValue -> target` retention cycle on `Picture`**: [`NativeMemoryFinalizer.attach`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/native_memory.dart#L51-L55) registers `CountedRef` as weak `target` and `UniqueRef` as strong `heldValue`. Because constructor initializing formals (`[this.imageTracker]`) are only in scope in initializer lists, constructor-body `onDispose` closures in [`SkwasmPicture.fromHandle`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/skwasm/skwasm_impl/picture.dart#L16-L19) (even when `imageTracker == null`) and [`CkPicture`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/picture.dart#L28-L32) (when `imageTracker != null`) capture `this -> CountedRef`, preventing V8 GC from ever finalizing undisposed pictures. - **Non-idempotent backend image disposal**: [`CkImageDelegate.dispose()`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/image.dart#L24-L26) and [`SkwasmImage.dispose()`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/skwasm/skwasm_impl/image.dart#L24-L26) lack disposal guards. ### Proposed Fix - Tie a single `imageSource.retain()` / `release()` pair to `EngineImage.box` (`CountedRef`), and wrap `_StaticEngineCodec`'s `ImageSource` in `UniqueRef` with idempotent `dispose()` across `EngineCodec`, `CkImageDelegate`, and `SkwasmImage`. - Construct `UniqueRef` `onDispose` callbacks via `static` helpers in `EngineImage`, `_StaticEngineCodec`, `CkPicture`, and `SkwasmPicture` so `heldValue` never captures `this`.
Detailed reproduction & V8 GC / WAT output (AI-assisted) 1. Run a browser unit test on `f25fa15a19b` under Chrome `145` with `--js-flags=--expose-gc`, allocating and dropping undisposed `EngineImage`, `EngineCodec.staticImage`, and `ui.Picture` instances inside `@pragma('dart2js:noInline') @pragma('wasm:never-inline')` helpers followed by `window.gc()` + macrotask turns: ```text REAL_V8_GC_UI [canvaskit]: engineImageClosed=false, staticCodecClosed=false, pictureClosed=false REAL_V8_GC_UI [skwasm]: engineImageClosed=false, staticCodecClosed=false, pictureClosed=false REAL_V8_GC_SKWASM_PICTURE: baseline=0, afterGc=1 // C++ flutter::DisplayList leaked even with imageTracker == null ``` 2. Inspecting compiled `dart2js` JS (`CkPicture_closure`) and `dart2wasm` WAT (``) confirms `$this` / `(ref null $SkwasmPicture)` is stored in the `UniqueRef._onDispose` closure struct. 3. Note on [`MakeLazyImageFromImageBitmap`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/canvaskit_api.dart#L189): its second parameter is `bool hasPremultipliedAlpha` (contrary to the comment in [`canvaskit/renderer.dart#L261-L265`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/f25fa15a19bef01a6de1ed3b4b21dcf49cfa55a1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/renderer.dart#L261-L265)), so CanvasKit never auto-closes `ImageBitmap` on GPU upload.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On the `main` channel, run `examples/multiple_windows` on macOS with windowing enabled:
   `FLUTTER_WINDOWING=true flutter run -d macos`
2. From the main window, press **Regular** 3 times to open 3 regular windows.
3. In each regular window, press **Show Tooltip**, then **Show Popup**, then **Create Modal Dialog**.
4. While a tooltip window and a popup window are open, click with the mouse on another window. The app crashes immediately.

### Last action before the crash

With a tooltip and a popup open, clicking on another window.

Seen 2 times out of 2 manual sessions with this kind of setup. Not reproducible with synthetic taps (`LiveWidgetController.tap`) or with `WindowController.activate()` (300 random calls). It seems to need a real click that changes the key window.

### Expected results

Focus moves to the clicked window.

### Actual results

The app aborts:

```

*** First throw call stack:
 2   CoreFoundation   -[__NSSingleObjectEnumerator description] + 0

[iOS] External keyboard: input language switching breaks in TextField (iPhone, iPad)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample below on a **physical iOS device** (tested on iPhone 16 and iPad Pro 12.9" 4th gen, both on iOS 27.2.1).
2. Connect an external Bluetooth keyboard to the device (Logitech K380 was used for testing).
3. Make sure Korean and English keyboards are both enabled in iOS settings.
4. Type in the autofocused `TextField` and switch the input language using `Ctrl + Space` or `Caps Lock` on the external keyboard while typing.


### Expected results

- The input language switches every time `Ctrl + Space` / `Caps Lock` is pressed, consistently, and the typed characters match the selected language.
- Korean characters are composed correctly (no decomposed jamo).
- The iOS language selection overlay is shown on language switch (on both iPhone and iPad), like it is in native iOS text fields.


### Actual results

**iPhone 16**
- A blue dot is displayed at the top-left of the screen.
- The first 2 language switches work. After that, switching no longer works: after switching to English, Korean is still typed, and the Korean text is not composed properly (the characters are split into separate jamo).
- At 0:31 in the video: while holding the right Ctrl (Option) key on the external keyboard, English is typed. When the key is released, Korean is typed again.

title: [flutter_tools] DataAsset hook output dropped on pubspec collision
body:
With `--enable-dart-data-assets`, declaring the same asset path in both `pubspec.yaml` and a `hook/build.dart` `DataAsset` silently drops the hook output instead of failing the build. The conflict check in [`asset.dart#L537-L548`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c0205700e04b127bbfecdeb6c83d1e0c9c564ed6/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/asset.dart#L537-L548) misses every generated or subdirectory asset, catching only flat package-root files.

- **Reproduction**:
  1. Enable `flutter config --enable-dart-data-assets`.
  2. In a package `foo`, declare `flutter: assets: [assets/id1.txt]` in `pubspec.yaml` and emit `DataAsset(package: 'foo', name: 'assets/id1.txt', file: ...)` from `hook/build.dart` (either generated in `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/` or pointing at `foo/assets/id1.txt`).
  3. Run `flutter build web` (or any target): the build exits `0` and bundles the static `pubspec.yaml` file instead of erroring with `Conflicting assets` (or, if the pubspec entry uses `transformers:`, the untransformed hook output silently overwrites it).
- **Why it happens**:
  - `asset.dart#L537-L548` checks `assetVariants.containsKey(asset)`, where [`_Asset.operator ==`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c0205700e04b127bbfecdeb6c83d1e0c9c564ed6/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/asset.dart#L1628-L1642) compares `baseDir` and `relativeUri` in addition to `entryUri` (`packages/foo/assets/id1.txt`). Hook assets set `baseDir: dirname(filePath)` and `relativeUri: basename(filePath)`, which only equals the pubspec `_Asset` when the file sits directly in `<pkgRoot>/id1.txt` ([`dart_data_asset_conflicting_assets_test.dart#L23-L34`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c0205700e04b127bbfecdeb6c83d1e0c9c564ed6/packages/flutter_tools/test/integration.shard/isolated/dart_data_asset_conflicting_assets_test.dart#L23-L34)). Resolution variants (`2x/`, `3x/`) inside `assetVariants[key]` lists are also skipped, and [`_setIfConfigurationChanged`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c0205700e04b127bbfecdeb6c83d1e0c9c564ed6/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/asset.dart#L728-L737) then drops the duplicate key unless `transformers` differ.
  - Separately on [`asset.dart#L540`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c0205700e04b127bbfecdeb6c83d1e0c9c564ed6/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/asset.dart#L540), `Uri.parse(_fileSystem.path.join('packages', dataAsset.package, dataAsset.name))` uses host path separators, producing `%5C` in `entryUri` on Windows instead of `/` URL segments (compare [`L1522`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c0205700e04b127bbfecdeb6c83d1e0c9c564ed6/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/asset.dart#L1522)).

**Possible directions**: Key the duplicate check on existing `entryUri.path`s across all keys and variant lists, and construct `entryUri` with POSIX path segments (`Uri(pathSegments: ['packages', dataAsset.package, ...dataAsset.name.split('/')])`)—or confirm whether dual declaration should intentionally let the hook win while `DataAsset` remains experimental.

title: [Impeller] Impeller (OpenGLES) rasterises 1.3-1.9x slower than Skia on PowerVR B-Series BXM-4-64 (Allwinner A733), p99 33-41ms
body:
## Summary

On an OEM tablet built around the Allwinner A733 SoC and a PowerVR B-Series BXM-4-64 GPU, the
Impeller **OpenGLES** backend costs 1.3–1.9× more raster time than Skia for identical content,
and the tail behaviour is qualitatively different: p99 raster is 2.3–3.0× Skia's. The UI thread
is not involved — build times are the same on both backends — which matches #193009.

Unlike a "specific widget" regression, this reproduces on a **near-empty page**: a page whose
only per-frame work is one 24×24 square sliding horizontally already rasterises ~30% slower
under Impeller than under Skia.

On a real app (long scrolling list of rounded cards with a gradient background and images) the
same device renders ~30 FPS under Impeller GLES (average raster ≈ 33 ms, >90% of frames over
budget) versus a solid 60 FPS under Skia. The per-frame factor measured here is the mechanism;
the app payload is what pushes it past the 16.6 ms budget.

This is a follow-up to #193009, which was closed by the stale bot for "needs repro info" and
then locked, so it can neither be commented on nor reopened by the reporter. Per the bot's
guidance this report is filed separately, with the minimal reproduction the maintainer asked
for there.

## Environment

```
Flutter 3.47.9 • channel stable • engine 89c39edfdf • Dart 3.13.7
Board:   OEM A733 tablet (board / model names withheld)
SoC:     Allwinner A733
GPU:     Imagination Technologies PowerVR B-Series BXM-4-64, OpenGL ES 3.2 build 24.2@6643903
Android: 15 (SDK 35)
Display: 1200x1920 @ 60 Hz, density 240 (devicePixelRatio 1.5)
Build:   flutter build apk --profile --target-platform android-arm64
```

`flutter doctor -v` (relevant sections):

```
[✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.47.9, on macOS 27.0.1 26A434 darwin-arm64, locale zh-Hans-CN)
    • Flutter version 3.47.9 on channel stable at /Users/<user>/fvm/versions/3.47.9
    • Framework revision c197ca5199 (4 weeks ago), 2026-10-29 10:10:20 -0400
    • Engine revision 89c39edfdf
    • Dart version 3.13.7
    • DevTools version 2.60.0

[✓] Android toolchain - develop for Android devices (Android SDK version 36.0.0)
    • Android SDK at /Users/<user>/Library/Android/sdk
    • Platform android-36, build-tools 36.0.0
    • Java version OpenJDK Runtime Environment Temurin-17.0.20+8 (build 17.0.20+8)

[✓] Connected device (4 available)
    • OEM A733 tablet (mobile) • <device-serial> • android-arm64 • Android 15 (API 35)
```

Engine log at startup (expected after #191808 — the B-series Vulkan denylist):

```
I/flutter: [IMPORTANT:...android_context_vk_impeller.cc(62)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
I/flutter: [IMPORTANT:...android_context_gl_impeller.cc(104)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLES).
```

so the Impeller numbers below are the **GLES** backend; Vulkan is never used on this device.

## Minimal reproduction

Single Dart file, no third-party packages, no network. Four stages, each 4 s, run twice:

1. `blank` — dark page + one 24×24 square sliding horizontally (drives vsync, ~zero content).
2. `cards` — full-screen animated linear gradient + 10 rounded cards (140 dp, each with one
   116 dp image, `ClipRRect`, two text lines), non-scrollable.
3. `scroll` — 300 of those cards in a `ListView.builder` over a static gradient, scrolled
   programmatically by a fixed 22 px per frame (identical content delta on both backends,
   independent of frame rate).
4. `heavy` — animated gradient + 16 small cards (72 dp, 56 dp image), ~12 of them on screen.

The statistics are computed **inside the app** (`PerfRecorder` in `main.dart`, subscribing to
`SchedulerBinding.addTimingsCallback`) and printed to logcat, so no DevTools, VM service or
external analysis script is involved.

### Steps

Same APK, two launches — no rebuild needed to switch backends:

```bash
flutter build apk --profile --target-platform android-arm64
adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-profile.apk

# run 1 — Impeller (on this GPU the engine probes Vulkan, gets denylisted, falls back to GLES)
adb shell am start -n com.example.impeller_repro/.MainActivity
sleep 45 && adb logcat -d | grep 'PERF|'

# run 2 — Skia, same APK
adb shell am force-stop com.example.impeller_repro
adb shell am start --ez enable-impeller false -n com.example.impeller_repro/.MainActivity
sleep 45 && adb logcat -d | grep 'PERF|'
```

### How the numbers are computed

- Every rendered frame yields one `FrameTiming` via `addTimingsCallback`; a 4 s stage collects
  ~230–245 frames, aggregated when the stage ends.
- `build_avg` / `raster_avg` — mean of `FrameTiming.buildDuration` / `rasterDuration` over the
  stage's frames (ms).
- `p50 / p90 / p99` — same durations, sorted, nearest-rank percentile (ms).
- `fps` — frames ÷ wall-clock stage duration. It is *not* 1000 / average frame time, because
  build and raster of consecutive frames overlap in the pipeline.
- `over16` — share of frames whose `totalSpan` (vsync start → raster finish) exceeds 16.667 ms.
- `blank` measures the backend floor: only a 24×24 square moves, the rest of the frame is
  static, and Impeller still re-renders every frame.

## Results

Raster time in ms per frame. Two runs per backend per stage; both raw values shown.

| stage  | backend       | fps   | build avg | raster avg  | raster p90  | raster p99  | frames > 16.6 ms |
| ------ | ------------- | ----- | --------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ---------------- |
| blank  | Impeller GLES | 61/59 | 1.08/0.90 | 3.99/3.30   | 5.21/4.50   | 6.44/11.36  | 0 %              |
| blank  | Skia          | 60/59 | 0.91/0.94 | 3.10/2.53   | 4.24/3.43   | 7.14/5.27   | 0–1 %            |
| cards  | Impeller GLES | 57/57 | 2.48/2.77 | 11.88/10.84 | 13.01/12.70 | 38.03/34.83 | 18 % / 15 %      |
| cards  | Skia          | 60/61 | 3.41/3.15 | 7.31/7.63   | 11.11/11.46 | 16.75/15.80 | 7 % / 12 %       |
| scroll | Impeller GLES | 57/57 | 1.70/1.44 | 12.62/12.00 | 17.30/13.89 | 40.76/35.35 | 52 % / 17 %      |
| scroll | Skia          | 59/59 | 2.08/1.76 | 6.43/6.75   | 9.58/12.19  | 11.78/14.51 | 1 % / 3 %        |
| heavy  | Impeller GLES | 56/56 | 3.86/4.29 | 10.30/10.97 | 13.62/15.27 | 32.98/34.59 | 26 % / 29 %      |
| heavy  | Skia          | 58/59 | 4.20/4.05 | 8.07/6.73   | 11.88/9.89  | 14.91/12.80 | 17 % / 6 %       |

Ratios (raster avg, Impeller ÷ Skia): blank **1.29×**, cards **1.52×**, scroll **1.87×**,
heavy **1.44×**. Ratios for p99: **1.0–2.2×**, **2.1–2.4×**, **2.4–3.5×**, **2.2–2.7×**.

## Observations

- **Build/UI time is identical or better on Impeller** (scroll: 1.44–1.70 ms vs Skia 1.76–2.08
  ms), so this is purely raster-thread cost — the same signature as #193009.
- **Even the near-empty stage is slower.** `blank` has one moving square and no other per-frame
  work, yet Impeller GLES rasterises it ~30% slower than Skia. Impeller re-renders every frame
  in full, so this is close to the backend's floor on this GPU.
- **The tail is the real problem.** Impeller's p99 sits at 33–41 ms in every loaded stage while
  Skia's stays at 12–17 ms. A ~35 ms frame is a visible hitch; in `scroll` the fraction of
  frames over budget went from 1–3 % (Skia) to 17–52 % (Impeller).
- **Cost grows with content.** The gap is smallest for the trivial page and largest for the
  scrolling viewport (1.87×), consistent with the app-level measurement: with the real app's
  payload (larger images, more layers) Impeller GLES lands at ~33 ms average raster and ~30 FPS,
  while Skia holds 60 FPS.
- `RepaintBoundary` tuning was tried on the app side without effect (as reported in #193009),
  and no Dart-side change moves these ratios.
- Absolute numbers drift with device temperature and background load (this board is passively
  cooled); compare backends within one session, or take the median of three runs.

## Why this matters

`flutter.dev/blog/flutter-darts-2026-roadmap` (2026-02-24) states that in 2026 the legacy Skia
backend is removed on **Android 10 and above**, with no exception for low-end / PowerVR devices.
This device runs Android 15. The only current mitigation is `--no-enable-impeller`, i.e. an
opt-out that already emits `[Action Required]: Impeller opt-out deprecated` and will stop
working.

## Related issues

- #193009 — Impeller GLES vs Skia on PowerVR Rogue GE8320 (Flutter 3.47.1): 32.8 ms average
  frame, 100 % over budget, build 1.5 ms, raster 393/400 over budget, Skia 60 FPS. Closed as
  stale without a root cause; this report adds a second SoC family (B-Series BXM), a minimal
  reproducer, and the same backend-vs-backend ratios.
- #181315 — B-series PowerVR denylisted from Vulkan (fixed by #191808). Confirmed working here:
  the engine probes Vulkan, then falls back to GLES.
- #161304 — rendering/performance problems with Impeller on PowerVR devices (family-level).
- #192364 — Impeller Vulkan ~3.5× slower than expected on Adreno 702 (multi-vendor support for
  "Impeller slower than Skia on low-end GPUs").
- #180831 — Impeller worse than Skia with PlatformView/Texture; not used by this repro.

## Request

Could a maintainer confirm whether the B-Series GLES path has any known rasterisation
regression, and whether the ~2.5–3× p99 tail (periodic stalls rather than uniformly slow
frames) points at a specific Impeller GLES behaviour — e.g. per-frame offscreen/backbuffer
handling on PowerVR drivers?

The reproducer is one `main.dart` (~380 lines) plus three 512×512 PNGs loaded with
`Image.asset` (any images of that size reproduce the same load). Code:
https://gist.github.com/lumen-field/9d2dac4ebcbd48a8a054af4e69978097 (`main.dart`, `notes.md`,
`run_bench.sh`). I can attach
the full project as a zip in a comment if that is more convenient.

title: [iOS 27] Debug mode very slow on first screen navigation on physical device (Flutter 3.50.1)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

2. Flutter 3.50.1 stable (Swift Package Manager disabled for the project).

title: [Impeller][Android] Vulkan KHR swapchain stays one buffer behind after a single missed latch (until surface recreation)
body:
### Summary
With Impeller on Vulkan using the default KHR swapchain, a single frame that misses SurfaceFlinger's latch (an orientation change is the usual trigger) can leave **one extra buffer permanently queued** in the BufferQueue. Flutter then produces one frame per vsync and SurfaceFlinger consumes one per vsync, so the queue never drains. Every later frame's GPU work waits a full refresh for a free buffer. The app stays in this slower, higher-latency state until the swapchain is recreated (the next resize, or an app restart). Each rotation "re-rolls" it: the app can become slow or fast again.

### Device and versions
- Samsung Galaxy A16 (SM-A166U, Exynos 1330 / Mali-G68), Android 17 (API 37), 90 Hz
- Flutter 3.50.1 stable (ae9b586f34), Impeller Vulkan, release and profile builds
- A Galaxy S25 never shows it (its frames never miss the latch).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run any continuously animating app (we use a 2D game that draws with `drawRawAtlas` every frame) in release mode on a mid- or low-end Vulkan device.
2. Rotate the device a few times while it animates.
3. Measure raster time (or GPU completion latency) before and after.

### Expected
Raster/GPU-completion time returns to its steady state after the rotation.

### Actual (perfetto, 13 rotations in one trace)
- Before the first rotation: raster p95 about 2.7 ms. After some rotations: 5.0–7.2 ms, and it stays there until the next rotation or a restart.
- Raster CPU time per frame (2.5–2.7 ms), build time and GPU clock (130–170 MHz) are **unchanged** between fast and slow stretches. The extra time is waiting.
- In every slow stretch, SurfaceFlinger's `QueuedBuffer` count is one higher (time-weighted 4.8–4.9 vs 3.3–3.9), and GPU completion latency is pinned at 10.9–11.0 ms (one 90 Hz refresh) vs 3–7 ms. The raster thread blocks on the frame-in-flight fence / `AcquireNextDrawable`.
- Each rotation recreates the swapchain (`CreateSwapchainKHR` 17–44 ms), which empties the queue, so the state can flip either way. A first launch after install has also started stuck and recovered at its first rotation.

### Workaround and why it isn't enough
Setting `io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableHcpp=true` (AHB / SurfaceControl swapchain) removes the problem entirely: raster p95 2.4–2.7 ms in every run, including after 11 rotations. But that path needs API 29+, Vulkan, and the external fence/semaphore extensions. Everything else silently falls back to the KHR swapchain and can still get stuck. There is no app-side setting for the KHR swapchain's image count (`minImageCount = caps.min + 1`), present mode (FIFO) or frame pacing.

### Suggested direction
Detect the stuck state in the KHR swapchain (for example, acquire waits of a full refresh across consecutive frames while CPU and GPU work is unchanged), then drop or skip one frame to drain the queue. Alternatively, use Android frame pacing (`VK_GOOGLE_display_timing` / Swappy), which describes exactly this buffer-stuffing latency: https://developer.android.com/games/sdk/frame-pacing

Perfetto traces are available on request.

title: [Impeller] Vulkan validation error (VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137) during Android engine teardown
body:
### Problem

When an Android Flutter engine is destroyed while rendering is active, Vulkan device destruction runs before all child Vulkan resources have been freed. SurfaceFlinger can retain the transaction completion callback for the most recently presented frame across engine teardown, and that callback previously held a strong reference to the Vulkan texture wrapper, keeping Vulkan objects alive past device destruction.

During teardown, `AHBSwapchainImplVK::Present` has already passed a lambda capturing `std::shared_ptr<AHBTextureSourceVK>` to `ASurfaceTransaction_setOnComplete`. When `vkDestroyDevice()` runs before SurfaceFlinger releases that callback, Vulkan Validation Layers report `VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137` for leaked `VkDeviceMemory`, `VkImage`, `VkImageView`, `VkRenderPass`, and `VkFramebuffer` objects.

### Context

This issue was discovered while investigating the Pixel 10 Vulkan device destruction hang reported in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/196094. To isolate that hang, we created a dedicated engine teardown integration test in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/197002 and shared it with the Pixel driver team. When the Pixel driver team ran the reproduction with Vulkan Validation Layers enabled, they observed these object-leak validation errors at `vkDestroyDevice()`, which we then reproduced locally on a Pixel 10.

### Steps to reproduce

Enable `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` for `com.example.android_hardware_smoke_test` on an Android device (for example, via `adb shell settings put global enable_gpu_debug_layers 1`, `gpu_debug_app com.example.android_hardware_smoke_test`, and `gpu_debug_layers VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`), then run `FlutterActivityTest#engineTeardownTest` from https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/197002 (`dev/integration_tests/android_hardware_smoke_test`) and inspect `adb logcat`.

### Expected results

`vkDestroyDevice()` completes without any Vulkan Validation Layers errors.

### Actual results

Vulkan Validation Layers log `VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137` during teardown (observed on Pixel 10):

```text
Validation Error: [ VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137 ] | MessageID = 0x4872eaa0
vkDestroyDevice(): VkDevice 0xb400006ef11f27b0 has 15 leaked objects that have not been destroyed.
VkDeviceMemory ..., VkImage ..., VkImageView ..., VkRenderPass ..., VkFramebuffer ...
The Vulkan spec states: All child objects created on device that can be destroyed or freed must have been destroyed or freed prior to destroying device
```

title: [iOS 27] "Use Strong Password" does nothing for AutofillHints.newPassword fields; breaks the system sheet until reboot
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an app with `flutter create`. Add the associated-domains entitlement `webcredentials:<domain>`. Serve a matching `apple-app-site-association` on that domain:
   ```json
   { "webcredentials": { "apps": ["<TEAMID>.<bundle id>"] } }
   ```
   The file is also present in Apple's CDN (`app-site-association.cdn-apple.com/a/v1/<domain>`).
2. Replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below. It is an `AutofillGroup` with a `username` field and a `newPassword` field.
3. Run it on a physical iPhone with iOS 27.0.1. Turn on iCloud Keychain / Passwords AutoFill.
4. Type an email, tap the "New password" field, then tap **Use Strong Password** in the system sheet.

### Expected results

The generated password is filled into the field and the sheet closes, the same as in a native UITextField with textContentType = .newPassword.

### Actual results

- The sheet appears, but tapping "Use Strong Password" does nothing. The field stays empty and the sheet stays open.
- No text reaches Dart. The `TextEditingController` listener never sees a non-zero length. The `FocusNode` stays focused.
- After this, **strong passwords stop working in native `UITextField`s too**, both in the same app and after relaunching the app. Only a device restart fixes it. The sheet is hosted by `SafariViewService`, which keeps the same PID across app relaunches, so the broken state appears to live there.

When the Flutter field gets focus, the device log shows this ~2000 times in a burst:

```
SafariViewService(AuthenticationServices)[590] <Error>: Could not retrieve bundle identifier from (null)
```

This line never appears when a native `UITextField` gets focus, and the native field then works.

### What I ruled out (same device, iOS 27.0.1)

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| Safari, website sign-up page | works |
| Native `UITextField` (`.username` + `.newPassword`) added to the same app's window, fresh device boot | works (password filled, 20 chars) |
| The Flutter repro below, Flutter 3.41.8 | fails |
| The same repro, Flutter 3.50.1 (latest stable) | fails |
| Native fields in a `UiKitView`: username + newPassword in **one** platform view, fresh boot | works |
| Native fields in a `UiKitView`: username and newPassword in **two separate** platform views | fails, and breaks the sheet until reboot |
| Flutter `username` field + native `newPassword` in a `UiKitView` | fails (the log line appears on the Flutter field's focus) |

The associated domain is valid. QuickType and the save prompt work, and the AASA is fetched with HTTP 200 by `swcd`. So this looks specific to how the engine exposes autofill fields to UIKit. Each field is a separate `FlutterTextInputView` with a 1×1 / 0×0 frame inside the hidden `_inputHider`. iOS 27's AuthenticationServices apparently cannot resolve the app for that arrangement, and then gets stuck.

### Code sample

<details><summary>lib/main.dart</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: SignUpPage()));

/// Minimal sign-up form. The app has `webcredentials:<domain>` in its
/// entitlements and the domain serves a matching apple-app-site-association.
class SignUpPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const SignUpPage({super.key});
  @override
  State<SignUpPage> createState() => _SignUpPageState();
}

class _SignUpPageState extends State<SignUpPage> {
  final email = TextEditingController();
  final password = TextEditingController();

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    password.addListener(
        () => debugPrint('password length=${password.text.length}'));
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Strong password repro')),
      body: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        child: AutofillGroup(
          child: Column(children: [
            TextField(
              controller: email,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Email'),
              keyboardType: TextInputType.emailAddress,
              autofillHints: const [AutofillHints.username],
            ),
            TextField(
              controller: password,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'New password'),
              obscureText: true,
              autofillHints: const [AutofillHints.newPassword],
            ),
          ]),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

</details>

<details><summary>ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements</summary>

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
	<key>com.apple.developer.associated-domains</key>
	<array>
		<string>webcredentials:<domain></string>
	</array>
</dict>
</plist>
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

[Upload media here]

</details>


### Logs

<details><summary>Device log (idevicesyslog), focus on the Flutter newPassword field</summary>

```
SafariViewService(AuthenticationServices)[590] <Error>: Could not retrieve bundle identifier from (null)
SafariViewService(AuthenticationServices)[590] <Error>: Could not retrieve bundle identifier from (null)
... (~2000 identical lines within 1–2 s)
SafariViewService(UIKitCore)[590] <Notice>: Keyboard scene for <pid>:FBWorkspace-<bundle id>/UISceneHosting-<bundle id>:UIHostedScene-com.apple.SafariViewService-... successfully connected
SafariViewService(UIKitCore)[590] <Fault>: Invalid UIScreen coordinate space conversion: ...
```

Taps on the sheet reach `SafariViewService` (UIEvents dispatched to its window), but nothing is generated or inserted, and nothing is logged afterwards.

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

```
Flutter 3.41.8 • channel stable • framework 02085feb3f • engine 7a53c052bc
also reproduced with Flutter 3.50.1 • framework ae9b586f34 • engine 51379e6df4
Xcode 26.6 (17F113), macOS 26.5.2
Device: iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0.1
```

(Run `flutter doctor -v` and paste it here if the template requires it. Remove your username from the paths.)

### Related

- #72364 / #190614: Flutter autofill saves credentials app-scoped and ignores `webcredentials`. This may be the same root cause: the engine's autofill views are not associated with the app/domain the way `UITextField`s are.
- #193765: generated strong password accepted, but the keyboard cannot reopen afterwards (iOS).

title: [camera_android_camerax] Migrate from deprecated Camera2Interop V1 APIs (CameraX 1.7.0)
body:
### Use case

CameraX 1.7.0 deprecates the Camera2Interop V1 classes that `camera_android_camerax` wraps: `Camera2CameraControl`, `Camera2CameraInfo`, `CaptureRequestOptions` and `Camera2Interop.Extender`.

https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13775 updates the plugin to CameraX 1.7.0 and suppresses the Java deprecation warnings at those call sites, so the plugin keeps building with `-Xlint:all -Werror`. The Pigeon-generated `CameraXLibrary.g.kt` still prints 19 Kotlin deprecation warnings for those classes, which Pigeon can't suppress.

### Proposal

Migrate the plugin to the Camera2Interop V2 API (`Camera2Interop.forUseCase()` / `forCameraControl()` with `setInterop()` / `applyInteropAsync()`, and `Camera2Interop.getCameraId()` / `getCameraCharacteristics()`), then remove the `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")` annotations added in #13775 and the deprecated ProxyApis from the Pigeon definitions.

title: [a11y] have a way to test that text survives the WCAG text spacing overrides
body:
### Use case

WCAG SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA): https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing.html

A user can raise line height to 1.5 times the font size, paragraph spacing to 2 times, letter spacing to 0.12 times and word spacing to 0.16 times. Nothing on screen should get lost when they do.

Since 3.41 Flutter supports this. `MediaQueryData` has `lineHeightScaleFactorOverride`, `letterSpacingOverride`, `wordSpacingOverride` and `paragraphSpacingOverride` ([media_query.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/media_query.dart#L812-L857)), and `Text` and `EditableText` apply the first three ([text.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/text.dart#L735-L748), [editable_text.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/editable_text.dart#L6015-L6020)). Right now only the web engine sets them, from the browser's text spacing.

Currently there's no way for an app author to test that their layouts hold up under these values. No guideline in `flutter_test` looks at the overrides ([accessibility.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter_test/lib/src/accessibility.dart#L785-L824)). A label in a box with a fixed height fits fine at the authored spacing, and at 1.5 line height its last line gets cut off. Nothing tells you.

This would sit next to #170695 (text scaling) and #170705 (clipped text when it gets bigger), but for text spacing.

### Proposal

My proposal is a `flutter_test` guideline that starts with line height:
- Record every paragraph in the widget under test.
- Set `lineHeightScaleFactorOverrideTestValue` to 1.5 on the test platform dispatcher ([window.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter_test/lib/src/window.dart#L557)) and pump.
- Report a paragraph that fit before, but now has text outside its box or more lines than its `maxLines`.

The "fit before" part matters. A `maxLines: 1` label with an ellipsis is already cut off at the authored spacing, and that's not something the spacing caused.

I tried this out with `RenderParagraph.textSize` and `didExceedMaxLines`, and it works. A `Text` in a `SizedBox(height: 20)` gets reported at 1.5. `AppBar`, `TabBar`, `Chip`, `ListTile` and `NavigationBar` all pass, since the Material text styles already sit close to 1.5. So I expect most reports to come from custom layouts.

Letter and word spacing would follow later. The overrides are a single value in logical pixels for all text, so they can't express 0.12 times the font size. The guideline would have to set those on each span itself, based on that span's font size, and lay the paragraph out again.

### Out of scope

- Paragraph spacing. No widget applies `paragraphSpacingOverride` yet (#177953).
- `RichText`, it doesn't read the overrides ([basic.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6d4ace8c225095794bae57aab742f1a4f7b006dd/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/basic.dart#L6475-L6482)). Paragraphs with a `WidgetSpan` or a `TextSpan` subclass get skipped too, the overrides don't reach those spans (#177952).
- Text fields. `EditableText` applies the overrides, but this guideline leaves them alone.
- Text that gets clipped by a parent instead of its own box, or that overlaps its neighbors. The guideline only looks at the paragraph itself.

title: [go_router] Possible `Bad state: No element` in `popRoute` when `matches` is empty (follow-up to #147465)
body:
### What we see

We get occasional Crashlytics reports from production (Android) with this stack trace, on go_router 18.1.3:

```
Bad state: No element
  _Array.last                                          (array.dart:57)
  GoRouterDelegate._findCurrentNavigators              (delegate.dart:123)
  GoRouterDelegate.popRoute                            (delegate.dart:57)
  _RouterState._handleBackButtonDispatcherNotification (router.dart:807)
  _CallbackHookProvider.invokeCallback                 (router.dart:934)
  BackButtonDispatcher.invokeCallback                  (router.dart:1017)
  RootBackButtonDispatcher.didPopRoute                 (router.dart:1112)
  WidgetsBinding.handlePopRoute                        (binding.dart:1116)
```

This looks like #147465, which was closed on the assumption that flutter/packages#8557 fixed it. We may be missing something, but from reading the source it looks to us like that change guarded only one of the two paths:

- `canPop()` returns `false` when `currentConfiguration.matches.isEmpty` (delegate.dart:85 in 18.1.4).
- `_findCurrentNavigators()`, which `popRoute()` calls, still reads `currentConfiguration.matches.last` without that check (delegate.dart:123 in 18.1.4). As far as we can tell, this has been unchanged from 17.5.0 through 18.1.4.

### When it seems to happen

We believe it happens when the Android system back button is pressed very early, before the router has committed its first route. Our app has an async `redirect` at startup, so there is a short window where `matches` is still empty. We have **not** reproduced this locally yet; this is based on the stack trace and on reading the code.

### Workaround we use

We pass our own `backButtonDispatcher` that consumes the back press while no route is committed:

```dart
class GuardedRootBackButtonDispatcher extends RootBackButtonDispatcher {
  @override
  Future<bool> didPopRoute() async {
    if (router.routerDelegate.currentConfiguration.isEmpty) return true;
    return super.didPopRoute();
  }
}
```

### Possible fix

If this analysis is right, an empty check at the start of `_findCurrentNavigators()` (or in `popRoute()`), similar to the one in `canPop()`, might be enough. We're happy to provide more details or test a change.

### Versions

- go_router 18.1.3 (the report), same code in 18.1.4
- Flutter 3.47.9 (stable) in the reporting build, Android

title: [Impeller][Vulkan][Android] SIGSEGV in `SurfaceContextVK::UpdateSurfaceSize` (null `swapchain_`) on resume from background
body:
### Steps to reproduce

We could not reproduce it locally; this is one production crash report. Sequence seen in the breadcrumbs:

1. App (release, Impeller Vulkan, default settings, no `EnableHcpp` in the manifest) goes to the background.
2. It stays in the background for about 46 minutes. The system sends `onTrimMemory` level 80 (TRIM_MEMORY_COMPLETE) 8 times.
3. The app comes to the foreground (started → resumed), goes to the background again 1 s later (paused → stopped), then comes back to the foreground 11 s later.
4. The app crashes about 1 s after the second resume.

### Expected results

The app resumes without a crash. If the swapchain cannot be re-created, the resize is skipped.

### Actual results

SIGSEGV on the raster thread:

```
#0 OUTLINED_FUNCTION_743 (platform_view_android.cc)
#1 flutter::AndroidSurfaceVKImpeller::OnScreenSurfaceResize (android_surface_vk_impeller.cc)
#2 flutter::PlatformViewAndroid::NotifyChanged(...)::$_0::operator() (platform_view_android.cc:243)
#3–8 std::__fl::function / fml::closure
#9  fml::MessageLoopImpl::FlushTasks (message_loop_impl.cc:126)
#10 fml::MessageLoopImpl::RunExpiredTasksNow (message_loop_impl.cc:139)
#11 fml::MessageLoopAndroid::OnEventFired (message_loop_android.cc:91)
#14 android::Looper::pollInner (libutils.so)
#16 ALooper_pollOnce (libandroid.so)
#17 fml::MessageLoopAndroid::Run
#20 fml::Thread::Thread(...)::$_0::operator()
```

Signal: SIGSEGV (11). Frames symbolicated with the engine symbols.

### Analysis

On 3.44.2, `AndroidSurfaceVKImpeller::OnScreenSurfaceResize` calls `SurfaceContextVK::UpdateSurfaceSize`, which dereferences `swapchain_` without a null check:

```cpp
void SurfaceContextVK::UpdateSurfaceSize(const ISize& size) const {
  swapchain_->UpdateSurfaceSize(size);
}
```

`swapchain_` is null after `TeardownSwapchain()` (called on `surfaceDestroyed` when the app goes to the background). It stays null if the next `SetNativeWindow` → `SetSwapchain` fails ("Invalid swapchain"), because `SetSwapchain` returns false without setting it. A following `surfaceChanged` → `NotifyChanged` → `OnScreenSurfaceResize` then crashes. On this device the heavy memory pressure while in the background makes a failed swapchain re-creation likely, but we have no release log to confirm it.

On master, `UpdateSurfaceSize` still has no null check. #196342 makes `NotifyChanged` non-blocking and ordered after surface setup. That helps with ordering, but a failed `SetSwapchain` would still leave `swapchain_` null. Suggested fix: early-return in `SurfaceContextVK::UpdateSurfaceSize` (or in `AndroidSurfaceVKImpeller::OnScreenSurfaceResize`) when there is no swapchain, as `AcquireNextSurface` already does.

### Code sample

None. The crash is in the engine's surface lifecycle; no app code is on the stack. The app uses no Android platform views on that screen (the last route was a chat screen).

### Logs / environment

- Device: Samsung Galaxy A32 (SM-A325F, Mali-G52 MC2), Android 13 (TP1A.220624.014), not rooted, 5.9 GB RAM.
- App: release build from the Play Store, arm64-v8a.
- Rendering: Impeller Vulkan (default), KHR swapchain (HCPP / SurfaceControl not enabled).
- Count: 1 event, 1 user so far.

```

Engine • hash 04efd7c093d4e9281d5526ebcad6ecc60ba8badf (revision 77e2e94772)
Tools • Dart 3.12.2 • DevTools 2.57.0
```

title: [image_picker_ios] A pick call made during the previous pick's file copy receives the previous pick's files
body:
Hi there, and thanks for all the work on image_picker!

### What package does this bug report belong to?

image_picker (image_picker_ios 0.8.13+16, the current release)

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

iOS

### What happens

On iOS the PHPicker closes before the picked files are copied out of the library, so the app screen is live during that copy. For a large item, such as a video that lives only in iCloud, the copy can take a while. If the app makes a second pick call during that copy, the second call receives the first pick's files.

Reading `ImagePickerPlugin.swift`, the path is:

1. The second call runs `cancelInProgressCall()`, which answers the first call with `multiple_request` and clears `callContext`.
2. `launchPHPicker` sets `callContext` to the second call and presents a new picker.
3. When the first copy finishes, the `sendListOperation` in `processPickerResults` calls `sendCallResult(withSavedPathList:)`, which reads `self.callContext`. So the first pick's paths answer the second call while its picker is still open.
4. Whatever the user picks in that second picker is then dropped, because `callContext` is already nil.

`processPickerResults` already captures `currentCallContext` at the start (line 489), it just isn't used for the answer (lines 501 to 509).

### Steps to reproduce

```dart
final picker = ImagePicker();

// 1. Pick a large video that is stored only in iCloud.
final first = picker.pickVideo(source: ImageSource.gallery);

// 2. After the picker closes, while the copy is still running:
final second = await picker.pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery);

// `first` throws multiple_request, and `second` completes with the
// video from the first pick while the new picker is still on screen.
```

### Expected results

The copy answers the call that started it, and a call made while a copy runs either waits or is refused, so the first pick keeps its files.

### A note on how we found it

We found this by reading the source while guarding against double taps in our app, and we have not captured it on a device yet. The Android implementation refuses the second call with `already_active` and keeps the first, which might be a nice model for iOS too.

Happy to help test a fix. Thanks again!

title: `bin/dart.bat` does not add bundled `bin\mingit\cmd` to `PATH`
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Official Windows Flutter release archives bundle MinGit in `<flutter_root>\bin\mingit` ([`archive_creator.dart#L311-L324`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/06f1c24345a29b26fc388ca8072f2b03a36a4d82/dev/bots/prepare_package/archive_creator.dart#L311-L324)).

[`bin/flutter.bat#L21-L30`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/06f1c24345a29b26fc388ca8072f2b03a36a4d82/bin/flutter.bat#L21-L30) and [`bin/flutter-dev.bat#L26-L35`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/06f1c24345a29b26fc388ca8072f2b03a36a4d82/bin/flutter-dev.bat#L26-L35) add `%FLUTTER_ROOT%\bin\mingit\cmd` to `PATH` and check `WHERE /Q git` before calling `bin/internal/shared.bat`, but [`bin/dart.bat#L14-L33`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/06f1c24345a29b26fc388ca8072f2b03a36a4d82/bin/dart.bat#L14-L33) does not.

This means running `dart.bat` can fail in `update_engine_version.ps1` whereas `flutter.bat` would've worked.

### Background

- #57257 introduced `bin/dart.bat` with the `mingit` `PATH` setup inside `bin/internal/shared.bat`, so both `flutter.bat` and `dart.bat` had it.
- #59369 (fixing #57802) moved the `mingit` `PATH` setup out of `shared.bat` (because `shared.bat`'s `SETLOCAL` didn't propagate `PATH` back to the caller) and into `bin/flutter.bat`, omitting `bin/dart.bat`.
- #153892 later copied the `mingit` setup into `bin/flutter-dev.bat`, and #169794 moved the `WHERE /Q git` check out of `shared.bat` back into `flutter.bat` and `flutter-dev.bat`, leaving `bin/dart.bat` without either check.
- A user previously hit this in #138144, which was closed on the assumption that system Git is required (which appears incorrect when using the archive, which explicitly supports the bundled `bin\mingit`).

### Suggested fix

Add the same `mingit_path` `PATH` setup (and `WHERE /Q git` check) from `bin/flutter.bat` to `bin/dart.bat` before calling `bin/internal/shared.bat`.

### Expected results

Both `flutter.bat` and `dart.bat` should work with the bundled `mingit` when using the archive.

### Actual results

`flutter.bat` works, but `dart.bat` fails due to missing Git.

title: [flutter_tools] flutter test --platform chrome hangs indefinitely on Windows due to 404 on /canvaskit/ (path separator mismatch in _localCanvasKitHandler)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On a **Windows 10/11** machine, create or open any Flutter project with a web-compatible widget test (e.g. the default `widget_test.dart`).
2. Run:
   ```bash
   flutter test --platform chrome
Observe the test execution output.



Root cause analysis
During flutter test --platform chrome, the test host page is configured with canvasKitBaseUrl: "/canvaskit/" to load CanvasKit locally instead of from a CDN. However, requests to /canvaskit/canvaskit.js and /canvaskit/canvaskit.wasm return HTTP 404, even though the files exist in <flutter_sdk>/bin/cache/flutter_web_sdk/canvaskit/. Because CanvasKit fails to load, the Flutter app inside the test iframe never initializes and flutter_tools waits forever.

In packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_web_platform.dart, _localCanvasKitHandler checks the path prefix using a hardcoded POSIX forward slash after converting the URI with _fileSystem.path.fromUri:

Dart
final String fullPath = _fileSystem.path.fromUri(request.url);
if (!fullPath.startsWith('canvaskit/')) {
  return shelf.Response.notFound('Not a CanvasKit file request');
}
On Windows, _fileSystem.path.fromUri(request.url) converts URI separators / into backslashes \, producing canvaskit\canvaskit.js. Consequently, fullPath.startsWith('canvaskit/') always evaluates to false on Windows, causing every CanvasKit request to fail with 404 (while passing on Linux/macOS CI).

Suggested fix
Check against the URL path (request.url.path.startsWith('canvaskit/')) or normalize/use platform-aware path segments (e.g., p.split(fullPath).first == 'canvaskit' or fullPath.startsWith('canvaskit${_fileSystem.path.separator}')) before resolving the file inside bin/cache/flutter_web_sdk/.


### Expected results

flutter_tools serves local CanvasKit assets from bin/cache/flutter_web_sdk/canvaskit/, the headless Chrome test page loads CanvasKit successfully, and the widget test suite completes.


### Actual results

Compilation succeeds and headless Chrome launches, but the command prints Running test suite .... and hangs indefinitely without executing any tests.


### Code sample

// test/spike/chrome_smoke_test.dart —  any widget-test on web-app

}

title: [video_player] VideoPlayer ignores a rotationCorrection that arrives after it first builds, so Android portrait videos play sideways
Accessibility bridge assumes every custom action ID has a definition
body:
Two Windows crash dumps from Flutter 3.47.8 show an unhandled `std::bad_alloc` while `AccessibilityBridge::SetStringListAttributesFromFlutterUpdate` copies a custom action label. The dumps identify where the copy failed. The cause of the allocation failure is still unknown.

There is an unchecked lookup in that function. The framework normally sends action definitions with the nodes that reference them. If a node references an ID that has no definition in the update, the lookup reaches the end of the map. A debug assertion checks the result, but the code then reads the label through that iterator.

The bridge should skip an undefined action and keep each valid ID paired with its label. For example, if a node references actions 7, 12, and 3 and the update defines only 7 and 3, accessibility clients should receive 7 and 3 with their respective labels. The node's standard actions should remain available.

The earlier fix for #103808 queues nodes and their action definitions before committing an update. This issue concerns how the bridge handles a missing definition when it processes that update.

title: [Impeller] Release builds crash when drawing a gradient with empty colors and colorStops
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample below in release mode with Impeller (for example `flutter run --release` on Android, or `flutter build linux --release` and launch the bundle).
2. The app crashes on the first frame.

`Gradient.radial` and `Gradient.sweep` crash the same way.

### Expected results

The rectangle is drawn as if the paint had no shader, as on the Skia backend.

### Actual results

The raster thread crashes with `SIGSEGV`.

`Gradient._validateColorStops` only checks that `colors` and `colorStops` have the same length, so two empty lists are accepted. `Paint::ConvertStops` then reads the first and last stop of an empty array; its `FML_DCHECK(stop_count >= 2)` is compiled out in release builds. `ImpellerColorSourceCreate*GradientNew` with `stop_count == 0` reaches the same code.

### Code sample

```dart
import 'dart:ui' as ui;

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const CustomPaint(painter: _EmptyGradientPainter()));

class _EmptyGradientPainter extends CustomPainter {
  const _EmptyGradientPainter();

  @override
  void paint(Canvas canvas, Size size) {
    final Paint paint = Paint()
      ..shader = ui.Gradient.linear(

        const Offset(200, 200),

title: [material_ui] DatePickerThemeData.copyWith and TimePickerThemeData.copyWith reject an InputDecorationThemeData
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

material_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android, iOS, Web, macOS, Linux, Windows (it is a compile error, so every platform)

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

material_ui 1.11.1 (flutter/packages main at 31e61cb00).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take the date picker theme from a `ThemeData` and copy it with the app's input decoration theme:
   `theme.datePickerTheme.copyWith(inputDecorationTheme: theme.inputDecorationTheme)`.
2. Build.

### Expected results

It compiles. Since the input decoration theme was normalized (flutter/flutter#168981 and #171584), the `DatePickerThemeData` and `TimePickerThemeData` constructors take an `InputDecorationTheme` or an `InputDecorationThemeData`, and `ThemeData.inputDecorationTheme` and `DatePickerThemeData.inputDecorationTheme` both return an `InputDecorationThemeData`. `ThemeData.copyWith` and `DropdownMenuThemeData.copyWith` already accept either type.

### Actual results

The `copyWith` methods of `DatePickerThemeData` and `TimePickerThemeData` still type the parameter as `InputDecorationTheme?`, so the build fails:

```
Error: The argument type 'InputDecorationThemeData' can't be assigned to the parameter type 'InputDecorationTheme?'.
```

So you cannot pass the value you get from the same class's own getter back into its `copyWith` (`a.copyWith(inputDecorationTheme: b.inputDecorationTheme)` does not compile).

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

void main() {
  final theme = ThemeData();
  final DatePickerThemeData datePickerTheme = theme.datePickerTheme.copyWith(
    inputDecorationTheme: theme.inputDecorationTheme, // compile error
  );
  final TimePickerThemeData timePickerTheme = theme.timePickerTheme.copyWith(
    inputDecorationTheme: theme.inputDecorationTheme, // compile error
  );
  print('$datePickerTheme $timePickerTheme');
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Videos

Not applicable (compile error).

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```console
Error: The argument type 'InputDecorationThemeData' can't be assigned to the parameter type 'InputDecorationTheme?'.
```

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

<details open><summary>Doctor output</summary>

```console
Flutter 3.47.9 • channel stable
Framework • revision c197ca5199
Tools • Dart 3.13.7
Windows 11
```

</details>

I have a fix with tests ready (change both parameters to `Object?`, as `DropdownMenuThemeData.copyWith` does) and can open the PR.

title: [video_player] _updatePosition sets isCompleted=true after 500ms when duration is Duration.zero
[video_player_android] Support configuring ExoPlayer TsExtractor flags (e.g. FLAG_DETECT_ACCESS_UNITS) for H.264 MPEG-TS streams without AUD
body:
### Use Case

Many embedded hardware devices (dashcams, IP cameras, IoT recorders) generate MPEG-TS (`.ts`) streams containing H.264 video without Access Unit Delimiter (AUD, NAL unit type `9`) NAL units.

While players like VLC / FFmpeg and other system players handle these streams by detecting H.264 frame boundaries from slice headers, `video_player_android` currently cannot play them: ExoPlayer parses SPS/PPS and initializes the `MediaCodec` video decoder, but queues **0 video frames** indefinitely and stays stuck in `STATE_BUFFERING` forever until caller timeout.

### Technical Details (verified on `flutter/packages` `main` @ `31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8`)

1. [`HttpVideoAsset.kt#L60`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8/packages/video_player/video_player_android/android/src/main/kotlin/io/flutter/plugins/videoplayer/HttpVideoAsset.kt#L60) and [`LocalVideoAsset.kt#L16`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8/packages/video_player/video_player_android/android/src/main/kotlin/io/flutter/plugins/videoplayer/LocalVideoAsset.kt#L16) construct `DefaultMediaSourceFactory(context)` without customizing `DefaultExtractorsFactory`.
2. By default, `DefaultExtractorsFactory` creates `TsExtractor` with `tsFlags = 0`, which constructs `H264Reader` with `detectAccessUnits = false`.
3. In Media3 `H264Reader.SampleReader.endNalUnit(...)`, sample emission is gated on:
   ```java
   if (nalUnitType == NAL_UNIT_TYPE_AUD
       || (detectAccessUnits && sliceHeader.isFirstVclNalUnitOfPicture(previousSliceHeader)))
   ```
   When the stream omits AUD (`NAL type 9`) and `detectAccessUnits == false`, no video sample is ever emitted to `MediaCodec` (confirmed via `MediaCodec` stats showing `Qin: 0, Render: 0` while audio decodes normally).
4. Passing a `DefaultExtractorsFactory` configured with `DefaultTsPayloadReaderFactory.FLAG_DETECT_ACCESS_UNITS` resolves this immediately on Android hardware devices with zero dropped frames:
   ```kotlin
   val extractorsFactory =
       DefaultExtractorsFactory()
           .setTsExtractorFlags(DefaultTsPayloadReaderFactory.FLAG_DETECT_ACCESS_UNITS)
   DefaultMediaSourceFactory(context, extractorsFactory)
   ```

### Proposal

I understand `FLAG_DETECT_ACCESS_UNITS` is off by default in Media3 because ISO/IEC 13818-1 expects AUDs and slice-header parsing adds minor CPU overhead for MPEG-TS streams.

Would maintainers prefer:
1. Exposing an opt-in Android configuration option (similar to `backBufferDurationMs` added in `video_player_android` 2.11.0, or an Android-specific extractor/TS flag option) so apps dealing with hardware MPEG-TS streams don't have to fork/vendor `video_player_android`?
2. Or enabling `FLAG_DETECT_ACCESS_UNITS` by default on `DefaultExtractorsFactory` (since it only affects `TsExtractor` / MPEG-TS inputs, not MP4/HLS/DASH)?

I'd be happy to submit a PR with unit tests once the API direction is agreed upon.

title: [video_player_android] ExoPlayer C.TIME_UNSET (-9223372036854775807) overflows to 1ms in Dart Duration
body:
### Summary

When `video_player_android` initializes a stream whose duration is unknown to ExoPlayer (e.g., live streams or MPEG-TS streams without valid PCR duration), `exoPlayer.duration` returns `C.TIME_UNSET` (`-9223372036854775807L`, i.e. `-(2^63 - 1)`).

This sentinel value is forwarded unmodified to Dart and passed directly to `Duration(milliseconds: event.duration)`. In Dart's 64-bit signed integer arithmetic, multiplying by `1000` (milliseconds → microseconds) silently overflows to **`+1000` microseconds (`1ms`)**, so `controller.value.duration` becomes `0:00:00.001000` instead of `Duration.zero` / unknown.

### Root Cause (verified on `flutter/packages` `main` @ `31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8`)

1. Even after #176575 (`video_player_android` 2.12.0), when a stream genuinely has no duration, `initializationFallback` in [`ExoPlayerEventListener.kt`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8/packages/video_player/video_player_android/android/src/main/kotlin/io/flutter/plugins/videoplayer/ExoPlayerEventListener.kt#L22-L28) fires `sendInitialized()` while `exoPlayer.duration` is still `C.TIME_UNSET`.
2. [`TextureExoPlayerEventListener.kt#L54`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8/packages/video_player/video_player_android/android/src/main/kotlin/io/flutter/plugins/videoplayer/texture/TextureExoPlayerEventListener.kt#L54) and [`PlatformViewExoPlayerEventListener.kt#L51`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8/packages/video_player/video_player_android/android/src/main/kotlin/io/flutter/plugins/videoplayer/platformview/PlatformViewExoPlayerEventListener.kt#L51) pass `exoPlayer.duration` directly to `events.onInitialized(...)`.
3. [`android_video_player.dart#L535`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/31e61cb00e9813df45db2681c38970e87d30f2e8/packages/video_player/video_player_android/lib/src/android_video_player.dart#L535) constructs `Duration(milliseconds: event.duration)`:
   ```dart
   // C.TIME_UNSET = -9223372036854775807 = 1 - 2^63
   // (1 - 2^63) * 1000 = 1000 - 1000 * 2^63 ≡ +1000 (mod 2^64)
   print(const Duration(milliseconds: -9223372036854775807));
   // Output: 0:00:00.001000  (1ms!)
   ```

### Impact

- `controller.value.duration` reports a bogus `1ms` (`0:00:00.001000`) instead of `Duration.zero` / unknown.
- Downstream UI and `VideoPlayerController._updatePosition()` treat the video as a 1ms VOD clip: after the first 500ms polling tick, `position` is clamped to `1ms` and `value.isCompleted` flips to `true`, causing players that react to `isCompleted` (e.g., auto-pause / reset to start) to immediately abort playback after 0.5 seconds.

### Related Context

- #102366 reports the identical `0:00:00.001000` (`1ms`) symptom on iOS, where AVFoundation intentionally mirrored Android's `C.TIME_UNSET` sentinel (introduced for #48670).
- #176575 fixed delayed duration availability on Android, but does not sanitize `C.TIME_UNSET` when the stream has no duration at all.

### Question / Proposed Direction

Before opening a PR, could maintainers confirm the preferred contract?
- **Option A**: Normalize `C.TIME_UNSET` (or `< 0`) to `0L` in `video_player_android` (and align iOS/platform interface to avoid `-9223372036854775807` overflow to `1ms`), paired with handling `Duration.zero` properly in `video_player`.
- **Option B**: Explicitly model unknown / live duration in `video_player_platform_interface` (e.g., `Duration.zero` + `isLive` or nullable duration) without breaking existing callers.

Happy to submit a PR with unit tests once the preferred approach is confirmed.

title: [macOS] Disabled widgets lose their accessibility role and label (VoiceOver can't see disabled buttons)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, run any Flutter app (3.48+; reproduced on 3.50.1) with a disabled button, e.g.
   ```dart
   IconButton(onPressed: null, tooltip: 'Undo', icon: const Icon(Icons.undo))
   // or
   Semantics(button: true, enabled: false, label: 'Undo', child: ...)
   ```
2. Inspect it with VoiceOver or Accessibility Inspector.

### Expected results

The disabled button is exposed as an `AXButton` with its label, reported as not enabled (`AXEnabled = false`), as on other platforms and as on Flutter 3.47.

### Actual results

The node exposes no role and no name at all (VoiceOver skips it / Accessibility Inspector shows an unknown role with empty title/description). Enabled buttons are fine.

### Cause (engine source)

`shell/platform/common/accessibility_bridge.cc` sets `ax::mojom::Restriction::kDisabled` on disabled nodes. On macOS, `AXPlatformNodeCocoa -isAccessibilitySelectorAllowed:` (`third_party/accessibility/ax/platform/ax_platform_node_mac.mm`, ~line 813) then returns `NO` for **every** selector when the restriction is `kDisabled`:

```objc
const ax::mojom::Restriction restriction = _node->GetData().GetRestriction();
if (restriction == ax::mojom::Restriction::kDisabled)
  return NO;
```

so getters such as `accessibilityRole`, `accessibilityLabel` and `isAccessibilityEnabled` are blocked too, not only setters/actions.

### Suggested fix

Only block setters / actions for disabled nodes, e.g. return `NO` for `kDisabled` only when the selector is a setter (`set...:`) or an action (`accessibilityPerformPress` etc.), and fall through to `[super isAccessibilitySelectorAllowed:]` for getters, so the node keeps its role and label and reports `isAccessibilityEnabled == NO`.

### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.50.1 (stable), macOS.

title: [iOS][a11y] `FlutterSemanticsScrollView` frame is offset twice when the `FlutterView` is not at the screen origin (add-to-app)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Make an add-to-app host on iOS. Add a `FlutterViewController` as a child view controller. Put its
   view at a non-zero origin on screen, for example below a native header at y = 200:
   ```swift
   addChild(flutterViewController)
   container.addSubview(flutterViewController.view)   // container.frame.origin.y == 200
   flutterViewController.view.frame = container.bounds
   flutterViewController.didMove(toParent: self)
   ```
2. In Dart, show a scrollable that fills the view:
   ```dart
   ListView(children: [for (var i = 0; i < 50; i++) ListTile(title: Text('Item $i'), onTap: () {})])
   ```
3. Turn on accessibility (VoiceOver, Accessibility Inspector, or an XCUITest run).
4. Read the frame of the scroll view, for example in XCUITest:
   ```swift
   print(app.scrollViews.firstMatch.frame)
   ```

### Expected results

The scroll view frame is the same as the scrollable's on-screen rect: origin y = 200.

### Actual results

The scroll view frame origin is y = 400 (the view origin is added twice). The scroll view clips
its children to that wrong frame. So the items above y = 400 report `isHittable == false`, and
XCUITest reports them as not visible. Nested horizontal scrollables move down by the same amount.

Measured in an app with the `FlutterView` at screen y = 225.667 on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator
(iOS 26.0). The `FlutterSemanticsScrollView` has frame `(0, 225.667, 402, 537.333)` inside a
`FlutterView` at `(0, 0)`, whose superview is at screen y = 225.667. The scroll view is on screen at
y = 451.3.

### Cause

`FlutterScrollableSemanticsObject` adds `_scrollView` as a subview of the bridge view. Then
`updateScrollViewGeometry` sets its frame to `self.accessibilityFrame`:

```objc
_scrollView.frame = self.accessibilityFrame;
```

`accessibilityFrame` is in screen coordinates (`ConvertRectToGlobal` ends with
`UIAccessibilityConvertFrameToScreenCoordinates`). `frame` is in the superview's (the bridge
view's) coordinates. The two are the same only when the bridge view is at the screen origin, which
is always true for a full-screen Flutter app. For that reason the bug shows only in add-to-app
layouts.

`contentOffsetInternal` uses the same assumption: it subtracts `_scrollView.frame.origin` from a
point that `ConvertPointToGlobal` returns in window coordinates.

On master (ed05e125a49), `-[FlutterSemanticsScrollView _accessibilityHitTest:withEvent:]`
(#195731) converts the point with `[self convertPoint:point toView:bridgeView]`. That conversion
goes through the wrong frame too, so hit tests on scroll items are still off by the view origin.

### Proposed fix

Set the frame in the bridge view's coordinate space, and compute the content offset in one space:

```objc
- (void)updateScrollViewGeometry {
  UIView* view = self.bridgeView;
  CGRect frame = self.accessibilityFrame;
  UIScreen* screen = view.window.screen;
  if (view && screen) {
    frame = [view convertRect:frame fromCoordinateSpace:screen.coordinateSpace];
  }
  _scrollView.frame = frame;
  ...
}

- (CGPoint)contentOffsetInternal {
  CGPoint result;
  // ConvertPointToGlobal returns window coordinates.
  CGPoint origin = [_scrollView.superview convertPoint:_scrollView.frame.origin toView:nil];
  ...
}
```

A unit test in `SemanticsObjectTest.mm` could put the bridge view at `(0, 100)` in a window. Then
it can check that `scrollView.frame.origin.y` equals the node's local y, not that value plus 100.

### Related

- #195731 fixed the same class of bug for `-[SemanticsObject _accessibilityHitTest:withEvent:]`
  (it now converts the point to screen coordinates before `search:`). Before that change, in the
  same layout, a touch on a control drawn over a full-height scrollable resolved to the
  scrollable.

### Flutter version

Found on 3.47.2 (stable). The code is the same on master at ed05e125a49.

title: [iOS 26][WeChat WKWebView] CanvasKit: first frame paints all content, next repaint drops entire body subtree (layout correct, y-offset jumps to bogus value); normal in Safari, Android OK, skwasm also affected
body:
### Description

On iOS 26.4, a Flutter web app opened inside WeChat's WKWebView paints the
first frame completely correctly, then after ~1s (no user interaction) an
entire repaint drops all body content: only unclipped solid backgrounds
remain (e.g. red Scaffold body). Layout data stays "valid-looking" but the
probe's global y-offset jumps from 64 to 3179 (a value that matches nothing
on screen — the dead screen shows the background at its normal position).

Minimal repro: https://github.com/code10479/ios26_repro

Key facts narrowing the cause:

- **Safari and third-party browsers on the same iPhone render the same page
  perfectly.** Only WeChat's webview (MicroMessenger 8.0.80, WKWebView) is
  affected — so this is not plain iOS 26 WebKit, something about WeChat's
  webview configuration triggers it.
- **Android WeChat renders the same build perfectly** (verified on the same
  day, same tunnel).
- **Older iPhones (14 Pro Max / 15 / 16) are fine.**
- The **skwasm renderer (`--wasm` build) is also affected** — verified with
  nginx access logs that `main.dart.mjs` + `skwasm.*` were really loaded
  (no dart2js fallback). So #185931's skwasm workaround does not help here.
- Widget-level suspects already ruled out by A/B: Card/ListView
  `Clip.none`, AutoTabsRouter default FadeTransition, route transition
  fade, `Opacity(0.99)` saveLayer wrappers, `RepaintBoundary`, permanent
  micro-animation (FadeTransition 0.99↔0.996), pinning
  MediaQuery padding/viewInsets/viewPadding to zero, and a 500ms-timer
  `setState` on a Text inside the dead subtree (the timer fires but the
  text never repaints).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the minimal repro: `flutter build web --wasm --base-href /repro/ --no-web-resources-cdn` (Flutter 3.44.9)
   (full app: `flutter build web --base-href /wechat/ --no-web-resources-cdn`)
2. Serve it over HTTPS (COOP/COEP headers present in our setup, `crossOriginIsolated=true`).
3. Open in WeChat's webview on iPhone 17/18 running iOS 26.4
   (`MicroMessenger/8.0.80`, `iPhone OS 26_4`).
4. Watch the page for ~2 seconds without touching it.

### Expected results

Content stays visible, as it does in Safari on the same device and in
WeChat on Android.

### Actual results

- t=0ms: everything paints (all probe rows, texts, ListViews, Card).
- t≈1000ms: one flash, then **all body content gone** — only the solid red
  background remains. AppBar/`document.title` survive (they are outside the
  dropped layer).
- **Death is atomic: ≤1 frame (33ms).** Frame-by-frame analysis of a 30fps
  screen recording shows the last fully-painted frame and the first dead
  frame are adjacent — no gradual fade, no partial corruption, no
  intermediate state. One repaint simply produces an empty result.
- **It dies while fully idle, ~300ms after the route transition completes.**
  The last alive frame's probe reads `first=done1.00 now=done1.00`
  (animation finished), so this is a static full repaint, not an
  animation-frame glitch.
- **Dart keeps running after death:** ~3s post-mortem `document.title`
  still updates from the same isolate (WeChat's title bar changes), while
  the canvas stays dead.
- Probe: render box size stays `278x20` (layout intact), but
  `localToGlobal(Offset.zero).dy` jumps **64 → 3179** and stays there
  (viewport is 402x776; 3179 matches nothing on screen — the background
  still paints at its normal position, so the reported offset looks
  corrupted rather than real).
- Dragging/scrolling/switching to background does NOT bring content back.
- A `setState` timer on a Text inside the dead subtree keeps firing (an
  HTML overlay written by the same Dart isolate keeps updating) but the
  text itself never repaints.
- `RepaintBoundary.toImage()` of the scaffold rasterizes red-only too
  (from earlier rounds), so the raster itself is missing content.
- No JS errors, no WebGL context loss, `document.fonts.status == 'loaded'`.

### Diagnostic evidence

- Minimal repro (`ios26_repro`): red Scaffold + a "ladder" of nested
  wrappers (ColoredBox → Text → ClipRRect → Opacity0.99 →
  FadeTransition@1.0 → AnimatedOpacity → IndexedStack → Card → Opacity0.5).
  **All rows die together** — no rung in the ladder survives, i.e. no
  single wrapper is the gate.
- HTML overlay probe (pure DOM, unaffected by the bug) logs every second:
  `t/y/p/r1/rsz/w/c/mq/now` — timeline shows y=64 for the first frame,
  y=3179 from 1000ms on, `rsz=0` (no viewport resize), `now=done1.00`
  (route animation already completed).
- Environment: Flutter 3.44.9, `useLocalCanvasKit: true`, local canvaskit
  (no gstatic CDN), viewport 402x776, dpr 3.
- COOP/COEP enabled (`crossOriginIsolated=true`) — does not help.
- Reproduced consistently across 4+ rounds on 11-26/11-27.
- Screen recording (attached): shows the full sequence — page opens, all
  content paints, route animation completes, ~300ms of normal idle, then
  one flash and only the solid background remains for the rest of the
  clip; `document.title` updates several seconds after the canvas is
  already dead.

### Related issues

- #188164 — CanvasKit paints appbar but not body subtree (Android WebView)
- #196532 — CanvasKit drops content near clip edges under scaling (skwasm OK — but skwasm does NOT help in this report)
- #185931 — Safari 26.5 / WebKit 21625 CanvasKit scroll-view gaps (skwasm helps there; here it does not)
- #195025 — Safari CanvasKit WebGL context exhaustion → blank screen

The [source code](https://dart.googlesource.com/external/github.com/flutter/flutter/+/a2c7ed95d144284e0f53b1fa9c5e36d9cb35b0d0/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/time_picker.dart#2499) already has a private `_TimePicker` widget with the comment:

This request is to make the existing time picker widget publicly accessible and supported.
