title: [Android] MediaQuery.padding.top counts the caption bar twice in freeform windows on API 35+ (extra gap above AppBar)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an app with `flutter create bug` and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below.
2. Run it on an Android 15+ (API 35+) device that can show apps in a freeform window with a caption bar. I tested on a Samsung SM-S731N (Android 16 / API 36, One UI 8.0) with Flutter 3.50.1 (latest stable).
3. Open the app in full screen.
4. Open the app in a freeform window (Samsung pop-up view). With adb, for example:
   `adb shell am start --windowingMode 5 -n com.example.bug/.MainActivity`

### Expected results

In a freeform window the system already lays out the FlutterView below the caption bar, so the caption bar doesn't overlap any Flutter content. `MediaQuery.padding.top` should be `0`, and the AppBar should start right below the caption bar.

### Actual results

`MediaQuery.padding.top` (and `viewPadding.top`) is `16.0`, which is 45 px at DPR 2.8125 and exactly the caption bar height. As a result, the AppBar gets an extra 16 dp of top padding right under the caption bar.

| Mode | `padding.top` | FlutterView top in window | Caption bar rect (root insets) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full screen | 34.5 (status bar, correct) | 0 | none |
| Freeform window | **16.0 (should be 0)** | 45 px | `Rect(0, 0 - 1026, 45)` |

I think the cause is [`FlutterViewDelegate.growViewportMetricsToCaptionBar()`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/ae9b586f34a8443573f82ef57c3bf914a908cbf7/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/android/FlutterViewDelegate.java#L54-L69), which runs on API 35+. It reads the caption bar bounding rects from `decorView.getRootWindowInsets()`, which are in window coordinates, and raises `viewPaddingTop` to `rect.bottom` without looking at where the FlutterView is. Here the FlutterView already starts at y = 45 px in the window (its height is the window height minus 45 px), so the caption bar height ends up being applied twice. Only the part of the caption bar that actually overlaps the FlutterView, `max(0, rect.bottom - flutterViewTopInWindow)`, should be added.

This may be related to #161086.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MyApp());

class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MyApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      home: Builder(
        builder: (context) {
          // Read the MediaQuery that AppBar uses (Scaffold removes top padding for body).
          final mediaQuery = MediaQuery.of(context);
          return Scaffold(
            appBar: AppBar(
              backgroundColor: Colors.red,
              foregroundColor: Colors.white,
              title: const Text('AppBar'),
            ),
            body: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
              child: Text(
                'padding.top: ${mediaQuery.padding.top}\n'
                'viewPadding.top: ${mediaQuery.viewPadding.top}\n'
                'size: ${mediaQuery.size.width} x ${mediaQuery.size.height}\n'
                'devicePixelRatio: ${mediaQuery.devicePixelRatio}',
                style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 16),
              ),
            ),
          );
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

</details>

<details><summary>Optional diagnostic MainActivity used for the logs below</summary>

```kotlin
class MainActivity : FlutterActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        window.decorView.viewTreeObserver.addOnGlobalLayoutListener { logCaptionBar() }
    }

    private fun logCaptionBar() {
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.VANILLA_ICE_CREAM) return
        val flutterView = findViewById<View>(FLUTTER_VIEW_ID) ?: return

                "flutterViewTopInWindow=${location[1]}, flutterViewHeight=${flutterView.height}",
        )
    }
}
```

title: Building the flutter tool runs `dart pub upgrade`, so `flutter pub get --offline` needs the network on a fresh or updated SDK
body:
When the tool snapshot has to be built (a fresh git checkout of the SDK, or after an update changes the revision), `bin/internal/shared.sh` and `shared.bat` run `dart pub upgrade` in `packages/flutter_tools`. That step never runs offline, so `flutter pub get --offline` fails on a machine with no route to pub.dev, while `dart pub get --offline` succeeds from the same pub cache.

Every other step is already offline: once the snapshot exists, `flutter pub get --offline --enforce-lockfile` passes `--offline` to `dart pub get` and resolves from the cache. The exception is the launcher's own build of the tool, which no flag or environment variable reaches.

## Steps to reproduce

On Windows 11 ARM64, Flutter `main` at c0205700e0 (3.51.0-1.0.pre-291, Dart 3.15.0-173.0.dev). `shared.sh` has the same code.

1. Make an SDK whose tool is not built yet: clone the repository at that revision, and keep `bin/cache` but without `flutter_tools.snapshot` and `flutter_tools.stamp`.
2. Cut the network: set `HTTPS_PROXY` and `HTTP_PROXY` to an address nothing answers (`http://127.0.0.1:9`), and leave `NO_PROXY` empty.
3. Make an app whose only dependency, `path`, is already in the pub cache, then run `bin/flutter pub get --offline` in it.

## Expected

The dependencies are resolved from the cache, as `bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart pub get --offline` does in the same folder:

```
+ path 1.9.1
Changed 1 dependency!
```

## Actual

```
Building flutter tool...
Running pub upgrade...
Got socket error trying to find package dap_adapters at https://pub.dev.
```

The launcher then retries `pub upgrade` every five seconds, up to ten times, and the snapshot is never built.

## Cause

`pub_upgrade_with_retry` in `shared.sh` (and `:retry_pub_upgrade` in `shared.bat`) runs `"$DART" pub upgrade --suppress-analytics` before compiling the snapshot. `pub upgrade` contacts the hosted registry and does not read `packages/flutter_tools/pubspec.lock`. The lock file is already in the repository, so with the locked packages in the pub cache the resolution needs no network.

## Ask

When the tool is built, resolve from the lock file instead of upgrading: `dart pub get --enforce-lockfile`. Add `--offline` when the build is asked to run offline, either through an environment variable the launcher reads or by falling back to `--offline` when the online attempt fails and the cache holds the locked packages.

Related: #193422 is about the release archive missing `packages/flutter_tools/.dart_tool/package_config.json`, so the tool resolves itself with `pub get --example` at first use. This issue is about the step that builds the snapshot, which comes before that and also applies to git checkouts.

title: [macOS][a11y] VoiceOver cannot adjust a Slider: AXIncrement / AXDecrement are advertised but never dispatched to the framework
[Android][Impeller][OpenGLES] EGL_BAD_ACCESS after recreating an Activity with a retained engine and hybrid-composed WebView
body:
### What happens

With Impeller/OpenGLES, reopening an Android activity on the same FlutterEngine can leave the Flutter part of the screen black while an embedded WebView remains visible and scrollable. Dart still handles the back action, but the Flutter confirmation dialog never appears. I would expect the new FlutterView to render the existing route and respond visibly to input.

### Steps that reproduce this in our app

1. Use a process-owned FlutterEngine. The activity returns it from `provideFlutterEngine` and returns false from `shouldDestroyEngineWithHost`. An Android foreground service keeps the process alive.
2. Open a route containing a WebView using hybrid composition, with a Flutter toolbar above it.
3. Swipe the app away from Recents while that route is visible. Relaunch it from the launcher. The PID stays the same and a new activity attaches to the retained engine.

This was reported on a Pixel 10 Pro XL running Android 16 (2/2 from the WebView route, 0/3 from the home route). I also reproduced it on a Samsung SM-S936U running Android 17 with Flutter 3.41.9 (revision `00b0c91f062`, arm64 debug build, Impeller/OpenGLES explicitly selected). Skia recovered on the same Samsung device. Reproduction so far is in the app; I have not yet tested current Flutter stable or main.

### What the EGL trace shows

An Android GLES debug layer recorded these calls in one failing run. C identifies the same EGL context throughout; S1 and S2 are different draw surfaces.

```text
11:53:52.887  old activity starts destruction
11:53:52.898  platform thread 17600  eglMakeCurrent(C, old draw surface) -> success
11:53:53.920  new activity created in the same process
11:53:53.976  raster thread 17672    eglMakeCurrent(C, S1) -> EGL_BAD_ACCESS
11:53:53.977  raster thread 17672    eglMakeCurrent(C, S2) -> EGL_BAD_ACCESS
```

The engine repeatedly logs `Could not make the context current to acquire the frame`. The new Android surface reports valid. In a control run, releasing the identified context once on its owning platform thread during teardown allowed the raster thread to bind it successfully after relaunch. With an app-side workaround that releases the matching context after native surface teardown, three consecutive activity recreations succeeded in the same process, including navigating back from the WebView.

### Suspected engine path and follow-up

In 3.41.9, `Rasterizer::Teardown()` makes the render context current and resets `surface_` before unmerging the raster and platform threads. The merge/unmerge callback checks `surface_` before calling `ClearRenderContext()`. This ordering appears consistent with the binding left on the platform thread. [Rasterizer source at the tested revision](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/00b0c91f06209d9e4a41f71b7a512d6eb3b9c694/engine/src/flutter/shell/common/rasterizer.cc#L104-L142).

I plan to reduce this to a standalone reproduction, check current stable and main, and work on an engine fix if it still reproduces. I’ll validate the fix on physical Android devices with a retained engine and hybrid composition, add regression coverage, and follow up here with the results and a PR.
